  `board:lint` proves structure, the loaders prove data; none renders a pixel.
- `tests/guide-nda-current-affairs-themes.test.ts` fails (180 vs 191) and is
  PRE-EXISTING — verified failing on a clean tree via `git stash` before this
  lane started. Not mine, not fixed.


> **This block is NOT retired from CLAUDE.md.** Unlike batches 1-9, which were archived wholesale,
> September stays in the active log as a DIGEST — headline plus the load-bearing findings — and the
> full post-mortem for each entry lives here. If a digest is thin, the entry below is the long form.

- **2026-09-17 (second) — the four dark surfaces behind the PMF read get instrumented (migrations 0104-0106): export events, mock starts, bank answer-reveals and first-touch acquisition. Coverage on /dashboard/pmf goes 4 dark surfaces -> 1.**
  - **The question bank recorded NOTHING when used** — /browse plus the 317 /questions landing pages are 70k of the ~72k question rows, and the reveal meter already computed the act client-side and threw it away. That one gap is why "mocks are the most-used feature" could not be distinguished from "mocks are the only MEASURED feature", and it is what made three earlier readings of this same data wrong.
  - **REVEAL, not VIEW.** Revealing an answer is a discrete act of retrieval practice — the student tried, then checked. A "viewed" event clears no learning bar (scrolling past is not practice), would be an order of magnitude more volume, and would have failed the engagement principles gate that governs every kind in this spine.
  - **SIGNED-IN ONLY, as a decision rather than a limitation.** Attributing practice to an anonymous visitor over time requires minting a persistent device identifier, which is behavioural monitoring of an audience that is largely under 18 (India's DPDP Act treats children's data as its own category with a specific prohibition on tracking). Aggregate anonymous volume is already approximated by the Vercel Analytics that has been live in layout.tsx all along. The honest trade: we measure the minority we can measure cleanly, and the page says so.
  - **A BEACON, not a server write.** /questions is ISR-cached; doing this work during a render would mark those routes dynamic and cost the site its prerendering — the precise failure that once left this project with ZERO cached HTML files for months. Proven from the filesystem rather than from reasoning: **783 prerendered .html files before AND after**, including after mounting the acquisition capture island in the ROOT LAYOUT, which is the exact shape that caused the original incident.
  - **FIRST TOUCH WINS, and DIRECT IS NOT A FIRST TOUCH.** Last-touch would credit whichever link a student clicked most recently and make every campaign look like it works. And if a bare direct hit could claim the slot, the first internal page load after a campaign click would overwrite it with "direct" and the campaign would be attributed to nobody. Write-once is enforced IN THE QUERY (`.is("acq_source", null)`), not by a read-then-write that would race itself.
  - **UNKNOWN IS NOT DIRECT.** The 330 accounts that already existed have no channel and are not backfillable — the information was never collected. The coverage map states this where the number is read, because a null folded into a real bucket makes the past quietly look like a channel ([[default-becomes-assertion]]).
  - **`mock_started` fires only on a genuinely new attempt**, after every resume path in `startOrResumeAttempt` has already returned — otherwise a student reloading mid-paper inflates their own history. Before it, 33 students had opened a paper and had ZERO activity rows, so a 26% abandonment rate was invisible to every surface reading the spine.
  - **Three defects caught by the tooling, not by me.** (1) A structural coverage test REFUSED to let "Paper download: tracked" stand, because nothing in the row could say WHAT records it — `kinds` only covers activity kinds and exports have their own table; hence a new `via` field, so the map names its own evidence and cannot silently stop being true. (2) The exhaustive `Record<ActivityKind, string>` failed typecheck in TWO label maps the moment the new kinds landed, which is exactly the job that total Record is doing. (3) Search-engine hosts had to COLLAPSE to a channel name — google.com and google.co.in are one source, and keeping raw hosts splits a single channel across rows and makes every channel look smaller than it is.
  - **`server-only` had to come OFF the export logger.** It is reachable from /api/export, whose route tests import the handler directly, and vitest cannot resolve that module — 12 tests failed on it. The project's existing convention for service-role-adjacent modules on a tested route (lib/supabase/admin.ts, lib/rate-limit.ts) is a doc comment instead, and this now matches.
  - **NOT VERIFIED: the end-to-end click** (reveal -> row in user_activity). That path sits behind an interaction in a client component, which this repo has no way to drive headlessly — no jsdom, no Playwright. Compile, logic and invariants are proven; the click is owed to a browser. Gate: 332 files / 5,308 tests, 39 new pure-core specs.

- **2026-09-17 — `/dashboard/pmf` ships (migration 0103): cohort retention by signup week, a signal funnel, per-feature retention lift, target-exam segments, mock abandonment and NPS with its denominator. Built entirely from existing tables — no new write paths. The page is designed around three REFUSALS.**
  - **The brief was "which analysis page is a quick win" across competition / feature usage / page usage / security.** Measured rather than guessed: page usage is already collected by Vercel Analytics and unqueryable on Hobby; security has NO history to analyse because `rate_limit_increment` DELETES rows older than 2h on every call; competition has zero internal data and rots as a page. Feature usage won because `/dashboard/activity` + `get_activity_shape` already existed — the work was extension, not a pipeline.
  - **CENSORING is the load-bearing rule.** A cohort that signed up 3 days ago has not had 28 days to come back, so its d28 cell renders as a dash, never 0%. On live data the newest cohort carries `daysSinceClose: -4` (its week has not even closed) and every recent cohort reports `retD28: 0` — uncensored, the table reads as a collapse that is not happening. 8 cells are currently blank for this reason.
  - **SAMPLE FLOORS: the count shows, the RATE is withheld.** A lift over 3 users or an NPS over 6 responses is noise wearing a number's clothes. Currently withheld: 5 of 9 exam segments, 1 of 6 features, and the NPS headline (6 responses from 75 eligible). Same discipline as `lib/dbhealth/delta.ts`, which refuses to extrapolate from a window too short to support one.
  - **HONEST LABELS — step 2 is "left a recorded signal", never "activated"**, and a test asserts the string does not contain "activated". This is not pedantry: it is the difference between a measurement and a floor, and getting it wrong is what produced the three corrections below.
  - **THREE OF MY OWN EARLIER CLAIMS WERE REVERSED by this work**, all from reading a partially-instrumented log as if it were complete: "52% never activated" is really 26% with zero signal anywhere (the measure ignored notes reading and mock STARTS); "/notes is dead, 5 masteries" is 125 users across 1,296 subtopic views (only its COMPLETION mechanics are rare); and "mocks are the product" was unsupported — mocks were the most INSTRUMENTED surface, which is a different claim. The user's "we should not conclude on incomplete data" was correct and is now encoded as SURFACE_COVERAGE, rendered ON the page beside the rates.
  - **`notes_progress` is STATE, not history.** `last_viewed_at` is overwritten on every view, so it can answer "has read" and "read most recently" but never "read on these days". Active-day counts therefore draw ONLY from append-only sources; letting the notes column feed them would have silently produced one day per subtopic.
  - **The lift arms are drawn from mature AND already-signalled students**, so the comparison is "which feature keeps an engaged student" rather than the tautology "acting beats not acting". `pmf:smoke` asserts the arms PARTITION that pool — the invariant that would catch the used/unused columns drifting onto different populations, which is the way a lift table goes quietly wrong.
  - **Lift is CORRELATION and the page says so.** A student who was going to stick around anyway is also likelier to try things. Live: notes checkpoints +40pp, saved questions +35pp, mocks +29pp — hypothesis generators, not evidence that notes cause retention.
  - **Segments OVERLAP by construction** (`target_exams` is a `text[]`, so a student declaring two exams counts in both) and therefore never sum to the roster — nothing in the view divides by a roster total, and a test pins it. The segment cut was free insight sitting in a column already filled for 272 students: mh-hsc-12 69% d28, mht-cet 58%, nda 42%, jee-mains 40%.

- **2026-09-16 (third) — /about gets a CONTACT FORM (migration 0102 `contact_messages`) and a nav tab, and `CONTACT_EMAIL` goes BACK to the gmail. The brief was "help me with GoDaddy"; DNS said the premise was wrong.**
  - **`pyqvault.com` has NO MX RECORD, so mail to hello@ does not reach the wrong inbox — it BOUNCES.** Every `mailto:` on the site rested on an inbox that cannot accept mail, and `CONTACT_EMAIL` is not just a Footer link: it is `REPLY_TO` on every outbound student email. **A branded address that silently eats replies is strictly worse than an unbranded one that works**, so the constant reverts until the MX exists. Resend is unaffected — all its records sit on the `send.` subdomain, so a root MX for receiving cannot disturb sending.
  - **The form is the durable channel BECAUSE it does not depend on email**: the row is the delivery and the ops notification is best-effort on top. That inverts the usual arrangement, and it is the whole point.
  - **NOT filed into `teacher_access_requests`, despite a near-identical shape.** That queue is an ONBOARDING pipeline — statuses `new/contacted/provisioned/declined`, UI offering "provision this org" — and a student reporting a wrong answer key is not a lead. Same shape, different lifecycle, separate table. Its validation is deliberately the INVERSE too: mobile-required/email-optional there (phone-first audience, the number IS the lead), email-required/phone-optional here.
  - **A present-but-invalid phone is REJECTED, not silently nulled** — nulling loses a reply channel the sender believed they had given us. And the honeypot lives in the SHARED validator so form and route cannot disagree about what spam is; a tripped honeypot answers 200 with no row, because telling a bot it was detected teaches it which field to leave alone.
  - **The route is `f`, so the gate proved nothing about it** — smoke-tested live instead: valid → 200 + one row (phone canonicalised), missing email → 400, honeypot → 200 and NO row. About's nav tab follows the Blog precedent (desktop + account menu, never the mobile bar, which is a fixed five pinned by an arity test).
  - _(Digest-only: this entry was written as a digest in CLAUDE.md and archived here verbatim on 2026-09-16; there is no longer-form post-mortem.)_

- **2026-09-16 (second) — one `intro` string was doing four jobs; the /notes card + `<meta description>` get their own short blurb. 8 of 84 chapters needed an authored one.**
  - **It was not merely REPEATED, it was WRONG on the card: 18 of 84 intros say "below" / "the subtopics that follow"** — true in the chapter hero, false on a listing where what sits below is the NEXT CHAPTER'S CARD. That, not the duplication, is what made this a correctness fix.
  - **The scale was invisible from the screenshot that prompted it.** Statistics (61 words) is the SHORTEST of the 84; the mean is 171 and the max 267, so `/notes/nda-maths` rendered ~5,100 words of intro prose across 30 cards and every chapter page shipped a ~1,100-char meta description against Google's ~155-char truncation. Measured after: **mean 162 / max 233 chars**, from build artifacts.
  - **A paren-aware sentence splitter was tried and REJECTED** — across all 84 chapters it changed exactly ONE result and made it worse (42 words to 75). The naive cut plus an 8-40 word gate beat the cleverer rule, and the gate is what makes a future 267-word intro fail loudly instead of becoming a card.
  - **The authored blurbs state NO bank count on purpose**: the card renders a LIVE count chip inches away, so a hardcoded number is a visible self-contradiction waiting to happen. `notes-intro-counts` was still extended to scan `cardBlurb`, because a count written there reaches MORE surfaces than one in the intro, not fewer.
