  - **BOTH ANSWER-KEY DEFECTS FOUND THIS PASS ARE REFUTED BY THE KEY'S OWN MATERIAL, which is what made them safe to bracket rather than argue.** `Ex 11.10(c)` (Dual Nature) prints \(3.0 \times 10^{-23}\) m where the de Broglie wavelength is \(3.0 \times 10^{-25}\) — and the key's OWN part (b) fixes \(h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\), which at the stated momentum returns exactly \(3.0 \times 10^{-25}\), reproducing its own mantissa with only the exponent differing. `Ex 13.6` (Nuclei) prints `= 26.90 MeV` with the MINUS DROPPED: its own printed expression, evaluated with the stem's own masses, gives \(-0.028881\) u \(= -26.90\) MeV, **and its own verdict "not possible" REQUIRES \(Q<0\)**, since \(+26.90\) MeV would be exothermic and therefore possible. Both were read at 520 and 900 dpi to rule out a misread — on the 11.10 line the same row sets \(10^{-35}\) and \(10^{-32}\), so the typesetting demonstrably distinguishes the digits.
  - **TWO ROWS THAT LOOKED LIKE FINDINGS AND ARE NOT, recorded WITH their mechanism so they are not re-opened.** `Ex 13.2`: Bi-209 is exactly 7.8481 MeV/nucleon, which ROUNDS to our 7.85 and TRUNCATES to the key's 7.84 — a 0.1% last-digit convention the brief explicitly says not to report. (Separately worth knowing, and a defect in neither side's arithmetic: **that key prints PER-NUCLEON values while the stem asks for the totals** "in units of MeV", so it answers a different quantity than the question asks; our solution gives both.) `Ex 13.8`: the 2% gap is entirely the seconds-per-year constant — our elapsed time gives \(4.996 \times 10^{4}\) y at 1 y \(= 3.154 \times 10^{7}\) s, the value the book's OWN constants table prints, while \(3.2 \times 10^{7}\) reproduces the printed \(4.9 \times 10^{4}\) exactly, and the key hedges with "About". **A disagreement whose mechanism you can name is usually not a defect; one you cannot is usually the reverse.**
  - **A FLAG THAT WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT LOOKED PERMANENT.** `EXAM_REGISTRY` cbse-11 read *"NO mixedFormats — and unlike the other board corpora that is a PERMANENT property, not a 'not yet'"*. The measurement behind it was real (the Class 11 **Maths** book contains zero MCQs) and the conclusion was still wrong, because **the claim was measured on ONE SUBJECT while the flag is EXAM-scoped**. Physics landing on the same exam ended the "permanent" property immediately. Now `mixedFormats: true`. Two near-misses that look like MCQs and are not, both live in this book: "Choose the correct alternative" heading a SUB-PART list where each (a)-(d) carries its own inline either/or, and a "(i) sphere, (ii) cylinder…" list inside one subjective stem — **key on whether the four alternatives are RIVAL ANSWERS, never on the instruction line or the label shape.**
  - **A SCOPE CLAIM OF MINE THAT WAS HALF WRONG, corrected because it changes how a run is read: `board:lint` FETCHES every `question_kind='practice'` row regardless of visibility and only ENFORCES on PUBLIC ones.** I had said it could not cover the pre-flip rows at all. That is why its count moved 14,627 -> 14,642 across this work — **+15, Nuclei's newly-committed rows, not +111** — while the 96 wave-4 rows had been counted the day before as fetched-but-exempt. Running it after the flip was still the right call: those 111 are only now actually enforced.
  - **Verified rather than asserted**, and independently of the authoring agents' own reports: 11/11 dump rows covered with **(id, ref) PAIRS** diffed rather than counts or the id set (the permutation failure mode where every solution lands on the wrong question and every count still matches); 0 control chars, 0 double-escapes, 0 U+FFFD; **144 math zones rendered through the project's own KaTeX, 0 failing**; `audit:text` clean across all six classes; `audit:omml` 0 failing zones over 261 Class-12 rows; `audit:keys` correctly reporting NO MCQs TO SCAN for the wholly-subjective chapters (a real result, not a false green); `board:lint` green; stored errata brackets reconciling against errata-file entries in both chapters. Flip dry-run counts (47+15+14+13+12+6 subjective, +4 MCQ) reconciled exactly against the applied counts, and every flip is `source_file`-scoped so it cannot reach another chapter — the `scan-flip` lesson.
  - **No SEO movement, checked rather than assumed:** `cbse-12` is not `practiceOnly`, so `listChapterLandings` derives `kind='pyq'` while every Physics row is `question_kind='practice'` — 0 `/questions` landing pages gained or lost. The rows are live on `/browse` (Practice toggle) and in `/board`.
  - **Owed, and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through.** `/board` reveals answers on click, so nothing headless proves the reveal lays out — and that now includes two errata brackets carrying inline math. See [[ncert-physics-ingestion]].

- **2026-09-08 — THE CADET VOCABULARY BOOK SHIPS COMPLETE: 4,100 entries / 199 pages / 4 parts, with Part 1 restructured from four letter bands into an EIGHT-RUNG CLASS LADDER (migrations 0092 + 0093). The A-Z index was dropped, a contents page replaces it, and 398 words were authored to fill the rungs the source book leaves thin.**
  - **THE INDEX WENT ON THE USER'S CALL, AND THE LADDER IS WHAT REPLACED IT.** The A-Z index was 21 of 176 pages and its stated purpose was telling a reader which PART holds a word — a fact they cannot know before looking it up. That earns less in a book used as a WORKLIST than as a reference. Removing it also removed the reason Part 1 was cut into letter bands: **a band answers "where do I look this word up", a rung answers "what should I know by now"**, and only the second is a question Part 1 exists to answer. All four index surfaces went together (route, print component, two scripts, the index lib) plus `indexTagFor` and the now-dead `indexTag` fields, so nothing is left half-wired.
  - **THE SPLIT IS ONLY POSSIBLE BECAUSE OF *WHICH* CLASS A WORD IS FILED AT, and measuring that inverted my own recommendation.** I first advised AGAINST per-class chapters, and the data supported it: the source reprints a word in every list that revises it, so **676 words occupy 1,125 class slots, 188 (27.8%) appear in two or more, one in seven**, and Class 7 and 9 share 86% of the smaller list while 11 and 12 share 75%. A naive split prints **449 duplicate entries**. What dissolved the objection was the user's framing — *a student in class N should know these words* — under which a word revised in Class 8 was already learnt in Class 5 and belongs there, printed ONCE. `extract-docx.ts` warns the labels are not a difficulty axis; that warning still stands against ORDERING the book by them and does not touch the question the ladder actually asks.
  - **THE THIN RUNGS ARE THE POINT, NOT A DEFECT.** Filing at first-introduction leaves Class 9 with 21 of the source's words and Class 12 with 30, precisely because those printed lists are re-runs. Those are the rungs to author into. Target 130 a rung (the user's pick from three costed options); **Class 5 keeps its 164 rather than have real CBSE words dropped to hit a round number.**
  - **`school_source` IS THE COLUMN THAT MATTERS (0092), and it is structured data rather than prose for a reason this project has learned twice.** A heading that says "Class 9" is a claim about a word's level, and most of the upper rungs are OURS: `'cbse'` where a publisher graded it, `'authored'` where the level is our judgement. Prose in a blurb cannot be queried, and this project has twice shipped derived content that did not announce itself. **Not printed per entry** — the book's rule is that presence carries a claim (`sentence_source` present = a real paper asked it), and an "authored" label beside a word would read as a warning about the WORD rather than a statement about its grading. The part blurb says it once.
  - **0093 IS DEFERRED FROM 0092 ON PURPOSE, and the reason generalises.** "A school row must carry both columns" cannot hold the instant the columns are added — the 676 existing rows are NULL until the re-filing runs. Bundling it would either fail outright against real data or, **worse, pass against the EMPTY test project and fail only on a later replay**. All five CHECK behaviours were PROVEN by self-aborting `DO` blocks rather than assumed: the range refuses Class 4, the source refuses `'guessed'`, a valid pair is accepted, a school row cannot lose its rung, a non-school row cannot acquire one.
  - **PARALLEL AUTHORING COLLIDES STRUCTURALLY, AND 79 OF 398 DID.** Seven rungs were authored by seven agents against a SNAPSHOT of the taken list, so every author checked correctly against the book and none could see the others — and words on the boundary between two rungs are exactly the ones two authors both reach for. The Class 10 author PREDICTED this in its own report before the run finished. Contested words go to the LOWER rung (the ladder's own rule, and how the 676 CBSE words were filed); the 79 replacements were written by ONE agent covering all four short rungs precisely so it could not recur. Serialising seven agents to avoid a collision this cheap to resolve is the more expensive half.
  - **THE AGENTS FOUND A DEFECT IN MY OWN GATE, THREE TIMES OVER.** Exact-match grepping is insufficient — `evade` when *evasive* is taken, `zeal` when *zealous* is — and one author measured that exact matching alone would have shipped **~25% of its list** as duplicates of words already in the book. The Class 9 author then found that **a fixed 5-character stem check is BLIND to short words** (`gnaw`/`gnawing`, `urge`/`urged`, `zeal`/`zealous`), a bug its own first scan had. The check now tests PREFIX CONTAINMENT. It is a **warning, not a refusal**, and the asymmetry is deliberate: `vacant` when `vacation` is taken is two unrelated headwords sharing letters, and no rule separates that from a real inflection — so it reports and a human reads. All six survivors were read; all six are coincidental (`dire`/`direct`, `knack`/`knackered`, `flippant`/`flip`).
  - **THE HONEST BAD NEWS, which is worth more than the counts: the school ladder is mining what Parts 2-4 have left.** At Class 11 the A-E band survived screening at **7.5%**, not the 58% first estimated, because the exam parts already hold that vocabulary. Neither top rung is padded — both authors DECLINED the exotic survivors (*obsequious, truculent, querulous, cynosure, turpitude, adumbrate*) rather than reach into the archaic tail to hit a number, and said so. **A ninth rung at that difficulty is not fillable honestly.**
  - **VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE, in both directions.** One agent's collision check used `grep -oP` on a build with no PCRE support, extracted ZERO words and dutifully reported "0 collisions"; it caught the false green itself and re-ran with a control that had to go red. The top-up author injected four faults and confirmed its checker went red on each before trusting a clean run. **Against that, my own worst error: I "added" the near-collision check, the script printed `added`, typecheck passed — and the block was never written**, because Python's `replace()` silently no-ops when the needle misses and I had backslash-escaped backticks Python does not unescape. Only grepping for the code found it absent. **A print statement is not a verification.**
  - **[[heredoc-backslash-eating]] FIRED THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION** — a `\n` becoming a real line break inside a TS string literal, the silent no-op above, and a third mangling that forced a file to be rewritten wholesale through the editor. That is now the standing rule for this pipeline.
  - **A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND BY THE RESULTING SWEEP: `check-authored.ts` held LITERAL control bytes** where its `CTRL` regex meant escape sequences — the same corruption already recorded for `scripts/bank-paper/english.ts`. **The behaviour was never wrong** (proven, not assumed: both forms compared across all 256 codepoints, ZERO disagreements), but the file read as BINARY, so `grep` printed "Binary file matches" and **every text probe in the repo had been silently skipping it — including the probes that catch this very class of corruption elsewhere.**
  - **A TOOL BUILT FOR A PROBLEM THAT WAS ALREADY SOLVED, and how it surfaced.** `renumber-rungs.ts` was written because `commit-entries` assigns `position` from the authored FILE's order, which must collide when a chapter is topped up. Its dry run reported **0 rows to move** — contradicting my prediction — and reading the code rather than banking the green showed `commit-entries` already renumbers each touched chapter alphabetically, from a defect a previous session had found and fixed at the source. Deleted rather than left as dead code.
  - **Other shape decisions on the printed page, all reversed or set on the RENDER rather than on reasoning.** Chapters were made continuous and then **REVERSED**: a continuous section break lands the next chapter's heading part-way down the LEFT column with the previous chapter's entries still filling the right one, so it reads as a heading for the text beside it. The chapter name is CENTRED (left-set and full-width it was hard to tell from a long headword). Entries are numbered **within the chapter**, restarting at 1, so work is set precisely ("Part 2, NDA A-B, 1-40") and a corpus addition's churn is confined to the one chapter that changed. 6pt between word groups, 13pt where the initial letter changes — the old 2pt packed entries so tightly that a synonym line read as belonging to the entry below. The contents page carries **no page numbers**: nothing here knows where Word breaks a column, and a contents whose numbers are wrong is worse than one that has none.
  - Verified rather than asserted, from the database and from Word: **all 8 rungs at target (164/130 x 7), every row carrying a class and a source, 0 rows whose class disagrees with their chapter, 0 non-school rows carrying a class, every chapter in the book alphabetical and contiguous, 0 flags**; the export opens in Word at **199 pages / 62 sections / 4,100 entries**; `GATE_RESULT: PASS` with the merge tree byte-identical to the gated commit; 761 prerendered `.html`. `page-estimate.ts` is now calibrated three times and runs **13-17% high** — the bias is deliberate and kept, but quote the measured number. **Owed, and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through of `/books/vocab`** — every route there is superadmin-gated and `force-dynamic`, so the gate proves they compile and never that they lay out. See [[cadet-vocab-book]] + [[vocab-book-pipeline]].

- **2026-09-07 (fifth) — the FIRST practice mocks ship: five 120-question NDA Paper I papers from the LWS NDA-II 2026 test series (mocks 187 -> 192). The corpus turned out to be 97.5% ALREADY IN THE BANK, and 10 of the 11 questions that were NOT are broken — which is the finding, not the mocks.**
  - **THE DEDUP GATE PAID FOR ITSELF AT ITS FULL DESIGNED VALUE, and the runbook's ordering rule is why.** `.claude/commands/lws-test-ingest.md` mandates *dedup FIRST on stems, derive SECOND*, a rule it earned when a 75-question test was fully transcribed and every answer derived before the dedup ran last and found all 75 already PUBLIC. Here five agents matched 600 printed questions against the 7,294-row NDA Mathematics corpus: **585 DUP - 4 MAYBE - 11 NEW**. Test-5 is **120/120 duplicate**. Going straight to transcription — the natural reading of "ingest this content" — would have vision-transcribed and derived **600 questions to add 11**.
  - **MY OWN PRE-GATE ESTIMATE WAS WRONG BY A FACTOR THAT MATTERED: I measured ~55% overlap and the truth is ~98%.** That estimate came from an `ilike` over 32 distinctive prose stems, which is a far weaker instrument than semantic matching over the whole corpus. The gate is not a formality even when you think you already know the answer.
  - **THE HEADLINE: the "NEW" set is ENRICHED FOR DEFECTS, and the asymmetry is stark.** Across ~150 bank rows the agents independently re-derived, they found essentially **zero** wrong keys. Of the **11 questions with no bank match, 10 have no correct printed option**. These questions are not absent because nobody ingested them — **they are absent BECAUSE they are broken**; a previous ingest of this same material filtered them out. The bank is the good half of this series and the dedup residue is the reject pile. Corroborated by the papers' own solution PDFs, sometimes in writing: Mock 1 Q110's solution states *"the required sphere is identical to S, but the options suggest a slight variation in the constant term for different contexts"*; Q62's derives exactly 664/1225 and then keys 0.52; Q72's silently solves a DIFFERENT data set; Mock 3 Q44's derives k = -3 while its own key says -1/2 (both inconsistent); Q100's prints `72 + 107 = 179`, verbatim the overlapping-triangles error an agent had reconstructed before ever seeing it.
  - **A RESOURCE I EXTRACTED AT THE START AND THEN NEVER USED: the SOLUTION PDFs.** All five papers ship one — 18 pages, clean text layer, keyed by question number. An agent found and used them, and they settled Q49 outright and exposed Q92's faulty method. They are a THIRD independent ground truth on every derived key, free, and they were sitting in the same folder the whole time. Consult them first on any source of this shape.
  - **REPAIR vs REPLACE was decided per question by asking whether the true value is RECOVERABLE from what was printed.** Five were repaired with no invented content, every before-state asserted by `build-nda2-2026-records.py`: Q63 needed only a **re-key** (5/6 is neither (a) nor (b) and (c) is not a value, so "None of these" was simply correct); Q49 needed only a **stem fix** (`x^3` -> `x^2`, confirmed as printed at 9x DPI AND from span metrics — 6.48pt raised against an 8.04pt body — but the paper's own solution restates it as `x^2` and reaches 12 = (a), so the STEM is the misprint and the key is right); and Q65 / Q68 / Q92 are single corrupted digits whose true value is recoverable (3/**256** for 3/**715** with the numerator already right; 29.**33** where the author's own working prints 29.53; 64/663 for 59/663 on the SAME denominator). The other five were REPLACED, because repair there means authoring: three have no printed option anywhere near the truth, **Q110 is degenerate by construction** (the plane passes through the sphere's own centre), and **Q44 is structurally unfixable** — only two k values are inconsistent, so with four options at least two must be consistent and no unique answer can exist at ANY option set.
  - **THE REPLACEMENT FILTER THAT MATTERED IS RULE 1: never take a set member.** Matching on chapter + subtopic + difficulty alone surfaced *"What is u+v+w equal to?"*, *"The centre of the sphere lies on the plane"* and *"What is the area of the parallelogram?"* — all unanswerable alone, because they depend on a shared stimulus. Swapping one in would have been WORSE than the question it replaced. `find-replacements.ts` tests `set_id` **and** `context`, since this bank contains rows that share a context with `set_id` NULL. Every replacement key was verified by independent derivation, and each substitution records its own reason in the committed question list rather than happening silently.
  - **A SEPARATE BUILD PATH, and the reason is that a practice paper CANNOT BE DISCOVERED.** `build.ts` finds a paper by asking the corpus a question — which (year, month) sittings exist, which `source_file`s, which row BLOCKS within one. A practice paper has no sitting and its questions are scattered across 40+ unrelated source files, so it exists only as an ordered LIST of question identities, which is the committed artifact (`scripts/mocks/data/nda2-2026-practice.json`). What the two paths share is what matters: `buildMockPaper` and the `mock_tests` column list.
  - **`sourceRow = n`, and getting this wrong would have failed loudly rather than quietly — which is the good outcome.** `buildMockPaper` orders within a section by `sourceRow`, meaningful for a PYQ paper and meaningless here: 40+ files with overlapping row numbers collide, and `validatePaperRows` rejects the paper as ambiguous, correctly. The printed question number IS this paper's ordering key. No change to the pure core.
  - **THE GATE THE PYQ PATH GETS FOR FREE AND THIS ONE DOES NOT: PUBLIC.** A mock stores refs and renders content live through the RLS-bound cookie client, so a ref to a PRIVATE or missing row does NOT error — the student sees a BLANK question and `verdictFor` scores it skipped. `build.ts` is immune because its fetch is hard-filtered to `visibility='PUBLIC'`; a bank-mirrored paper takes its ids from a dedup pass that deliberately saw EVERY visibility, so the builder re-asserts PUBLIC + exactly-one-correct-option itself and REFUSES the paper otherwise. `preflight-practice.ts` runs the same check ahead of time; on first run it confirmed **586/586 ids resolve and all are PUBLIC**.
  - **Q109's figure is load-bearing, not decoration** — its stem is *"The curve given below represent a/an"* and is unanswerable without the plot. The transcribing agent deliberately did NOT describe the y-axis in the stem, because that axis is labelled *"Cumulative frequency"* and that phrase IS the answer. The figure is rendered from the page REGION rather than extracted as the embedded raster, because the rotated axis label sits outside the image's own rect.
  - **Three ledger entries came out of the dedup pass**, all verified rather than taken on an agent's word and all left unfixed pending permission: a PUBLIC row keying an angle that makes its own equations unsolvable (verified algebraically AND by a 400k-point scan — the `pi/6` branch reaches residual 0.000022, the `5pi/6` branch bottoms out at 2.098, and its own PRIVATE twin keys correctly); substantial internal duplication logged as a RANGE (91 strict / 161 aggressive) rather than a number, because the aggressive key collapses `\sin^{-1}` and `\tan^{-1}`; and 6 PUBLIC MCQs shipping an unreadable option.
  - **THAT LAST ONE I MEASURED WRONG TWICE — 4,657 -> 381 -> 6 — in the same session in which I logged the ledger entry warning about exactly this.** A `length <= 1` scan matches every legitimate single-character option (`0`, `1`, `n`, `pi`); restricting to markup fragments still counted **375 JEE image-options**, where empty text is CORRECT because the option is a picture. The honest figure is 6, severity LOW (the key is on a valid option in all six, so nobody was mis-graded). The narrative is in the entry because it is worth more than the finding.
  - Verified from the DB, not the builders' output: all 5 mocks `source=practice` / `scope=full` / **`pyq_year=NULL`** / 120 refs each **all distinct** / 0 non-PUBLIC / 0 dangling / 0 bad keys / positions contiguous 1..120 / one marking scheme. `check-taxonomy` clean on all three record sets (nothing auto-created), `commit-paper` inserted 6 with 0 skipped, `audit:text` clean across all five classes, `audit:keys` 0 flagged, `audit:omml` 0 failing zones, **`GATE_RESULT: PASS`** (284 files / 4,184 tests), 761 prerendered `.html`. `db:backup` taken before the bulk write (76 tables / 390,812 rows). **Owed and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through** — the runner is client-interactive behind auth, so nothing headless proves a practice mock starts, grades and reviews; worth sitting one end to end, including Q109's figure. See [[mock-tests]].

- **2026-09-07 (fourth) — /mock gains a TYPE axis: past papers · practice mocks · sectional tests (migration 0088). SKELETON ONLY — every route, group and label ships with ZERO practice or sectional rows, so nothing has to be un-built when content lands.**
  - **THE LOAD-BEARING DECISION IS THAT IT IS TWO AXES, NOT ONE ENUM — and both combinations already exist as printed papers.** The obvious column is `kind: pyq|practice`. It is wrong because sectional tests are coming and `papers` already holds *"NDA - Matrices & Determinant"* (25 questions, every one a PYQ) beside *"NDA Maths — Circles, Height & Distance and Binary Numbers"* (60 assembled ones). A single enum would grow to four values that are really a product type, or gain a second column later that makes the first one's NAME a lie. So `source` (pyq | practice) and `scope` (full | sectional) are separate, because they answer separate questions a student actually asks: *am I sitting the real thing?* and *is this three hours or thirty minutes?* Navigation follows **scope** first — that is the commitment axis — and `source` renders as a badge only where the two genuinely mix (the sectional list and `/mock/attempts`).
  - **This also de-risks the phase nobody has built yet: `mock_tests` already denormalises `duration_secs`, `marking`, `sections` and `total_marks` per row, so the blueprint is a BUILD-time contract only. A sectional test needs no further schema — it carries its own duration and marking.**
  - **TWO CONCRETE BREAKAGES forced the new level, and the second is the interesting one.** (a) `/mock/exam/[slug]` was a flat year-grouped list — NDA is already 36 cards under 10 year headings and MHT-CET 64; the 27 assembled papers sitting in `papers` would take NDA past 60. That is exactly the wall the 2026-08-29 picker rewrite removed one level up, recurring one level down. (b) **Year is the SECTION HEADING, and an assembled paper has no sitting.** Stamping the build year would print *"2026"* over papers nobody ever sat. So `pyq_year` became NULLABLE, guarded by `mock_tests_full_pyq_has_year`: only a paper claiming to be a whole real sitting must name one — a SECTIONAL test built from PYQs draws on many sittings and honestly has no year, so "pyq implies a year" would have been the wrong constraint.
  - **All three CHECK behaviours were PROVEN, not assumed** — a self-aborting `DO` block confirmed it refuses an undated full past paper, refuses an undeclared `source`, and **allows** an undated practice row (the whole point), then `RAISE`d so nothing committed; prod re-verified at 187 rows / 0 null years afterwards. Both new columns DEFAULT to what every existing row is, so the migration is a no-op and `build.ts` kept working untouched — though it now writes `source`/`scope` EXPLICITLY rather than leaning on a default, so a row can never acquire a type by accident.
  - **THE ROUTE SPLIT IS A CACHING DECISION AS MUCH AS AN IA ONE.** `/mock/exam/[slug]/[type]` is a real route rather than a `?type=` filter because a searchParam here would either bail the static prerender to client rendering (`useSearchParams`) or make the route dynamic (server `searchParams`) — and these are ISR pages the sitemap points at. All **15** (exam × type) combinations prerender, INCLUDING the empty ones: a type page is reachable and shareable, so it must render an honest empty state rather than 404 the day before a build lands. Empty ones are kept OUT of the sitemap — reachable is not the same as worth indexing.
  - **`mockKindNote` states the type on EVERY instructions page, past papers included.** Labelling only the practice mocks would make the ABSENCE of a note mean "this is the real thing" — a claim carried by omission, on the one screen someone reaches from a shared link with no route context. Same [[default-becomes-assertion]] shape the syllabus map's "no single section" and the MHT-CET negative-marking line each cost a session.
  - **THREE PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS THAT THIS CHANGE WOULD HAVE MADE WORSE, each found by asking what a null year does downstream.** (1) **`readPublishedMocks` (the recommendation email) casts `pyq_year as number` unchecked**, and its whole selection logic is `sittingRank = pyqYear * 10 + month` — so a practice mock would rank as year 0 and still be emailed to a student as "the next paper in the sequence". Scoped to `source='pyq' AND scope='full'`: today's behaviour exactly, and it refuses to silently extend an email feature to content it was not designed for. (2) **Postgres orders NULLS FIRST on a DESC sort**, so every undated mock would have floated ABOVE the newest real sitting in both the catalogue and the admin performance table — `nullsFirst: false` in both. (3) **The CDS picker copy was stale**: tagline `"English"` and a blurb naming only the English paper, three weeks after GK and Elementary Mathematics shipped — the exact hand-typed-string rot that file's own header warns about.
  - **A MEASUREMENT ERROR OF MINE, corrected: I reported the `getPublishedMocks` overfetch as 84x and it is 53x.** The first figure divided the discarded `questions` payload (2,446 kB across 187 mocks) by only three columns (29 kB); the honest denominator is the whole used payload, 46 kB. The finding stands and is worth knowing: `MOCK_SELECT` is shared with `getMockBySlug`/`getMockById`, which genuinely need the ordered snapshot, so the LIST fetches it and discards it on its own last line (`const { questions: _q, ...rest }`) — **after** Postgres has read it, PostgREST has serialised it and it has crossed the network. This change takes the pages calling it from 6 to 21, i.e. ~15 MB -> ~51 MB of fetched-and-binned payload per full build. **NOT fixed — left for a decision**, since it is scope beyond the skeleton; the fix is a second column list without `questions`.
  - **Logged, not fixed (pre-existing, out of scope): the homepage is still DYNAMIC.** `/` declares `revalidate = 86400` and then calls `getSessionMember()`/`getSessionUser()` at render to redirect staff, so it emits no `index.html` and that directive has never taken effect. The 2026-08-13 entry fixed its DB reads (`unstable_cache`) but left the cookie read, which is what decides the render mode — the [[shell-component-decaches-site]] shape, one page rather than the whole site. Fixing it means moving the staff redirect to middleware or a client island.
  - Verified: **`GATE_RESULT: PASS`** (typecheck -> lint -> notes:lint -> notes:latex -> test -> build); **761 prerendered `.html` on disk** with all 20 mock exam+type pages static and `/mock`, `/notes`, `/guide`, `/questions` all still present (the filesystem probe, not the route legend); **24 new TDD cases** in `tests/mock-catalogue.test.ts`, every one confirmed failing for the right reason before implementation, plus 2 added to `tests/mocks-nav.test.ts`; migration replayed into the test project (`88 files, 87 applied, 1 pending -> ok`). **Owed and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through.** These are static pages so the build genuinely proves they RENDER — but not that they LAY OUT, and the mobile side-nav is a Radix Sheet that does not exist until tapped.
  - **Deliberately NOT done — Phase 1 is the content.** No practice or sectional mock is published; the `papers` -> `mock_tests` builder (27 eligible full-length papers, measured in the 2026-09-07 analysis) and the student-facing title scheme for them are the next step. See [[mock-tests]].

- **2026-09-07 (third) — an OMR key mismatch on the paper above exposed THREE wrong keys in live PUBLIC NDA GAT PYQs; all three corrected against the ORIGINAL printed booklets, and 8 student mock attempts re-graded upward. A fourth finding is bigger: one 10-question PYQ block is keyed "A" nine times and is wrong eight times.**
  - **THE TRIGGER WAS A THREE-ROW DISAGREEMENT, and every one resolved against us.** Grading the new paper, the teacher's Evalbee RESULTS key and the tags sheet built from the bank disagreed on printed Q10, Q28 and Q29 — and the teacher was right in all three. Reading each sentence settles it: Q10's parts are cut so that **"what you cannot" must be completed by "control, shift your energy"**, which only RSQP does; Q28's "dealing" needs its object and "with them" needs an antecedent, which only QSPR supplies; Q29's Q is the only part carrying a finite main clause, so only QPSR can open the sentence. The keyed alternatives are broken, not merely inferior.
  - **THE BANK'S OWN SOLUTIONS ALREADY SAID SO — and that detector found EXACTLY these three, with no misses and no false positives.** A scan of all 288 rows in the chapter for a solution that derives one sequence and then defers to the key returns three rows: *"…gives QPSR. **The answer key indicates PRSQ.** Matches option B"*, *"…gives QSPR. **On review**, QPRS also assembles a coherent sentence; the standard key is QPRS"*, and one that derives "QPRS" — **a sequence that is not even among the four options** — then picks A. Two entirely independent detectors, the teacher's key and the bank contradicting itself, landing on the same three questions is as settled as this gets. All three solutions were rewritten so they justify the answer instead of deferring to a key.
  - **THE USER'S INSTRUCTION — "review those against original pdf/doc not xlsx" — IS WHAT MADE THE CORRECTION LEGITIMATE, and it changed the verdict's basis rather than confirming it.** The standing convention PRESERVES a printed paper's key even when wrong, because students were marked against it. Reading the booklets removes that objection at the root: `GAT_2022_NDA1.pdf` (SDFR-F-TAG/44A) and `GAT_2020_NDA1.pdf` (KJU-F-GTA) are UPSC **question** papers and **print no answer key at all**, so there is no issued key being overridden — the stored letters came from a prep-house `.xlsx` Answer column, which the 2026-08-26 precedent already treats as a derivation. The booklets also confirmed our parts and all four options are byte-faithful in every row checked, so the defect is isolated to the key. **Both PDFs are pure scans (0 text characters), so this was a vision read, page by page.**
  - **REAL STUDENTS WERE AFFECTED, AND CHECKING THAT WAS NEARLY MISSED.** These are PYQs, so they sit in published mocks — `nda-2022-apr-gat` and `nda-2020-apr-gat`, 4 submitted attempts each. `mock_attempts` stores a FROZEN score, so a key flip alone would leave the review screen calling an answer correct while the result screen still called it wrong. **All 12 answer-events were students picking the correct answer and being marked wrong**; re-graded via the app's own `gradeMock`, +10.66 on four attempts and +5.33 on four more, every move upward. That 12-for-12 agreement is itself corroboration: candidates reading the sentence naturally chose what the bank called wrong.
  - **THE BIGGER FINDING, adjudicated and deliberately NOT fixed: `GAT_NDA1_2022_PYQ.xlsx`'s rearrangement block is keyed A on 9 of 10 rows and is wrong on 8.** Every other source in the chapter sits at 30-60% max share, so 90% is a defect signature rather than chance. All ten were read off the booklet; **only Q27 and Q28 are correct**. Six remain wrong (Q23→C, Q24→C, Q25→B, Q26→D, Q29→C, Q30→B). Blast radius measured rather than estimated: all 6 PUBLIC, all in one published mock, 23 answer-events, and a regrade would **RAISE 16 and LOWER 5** — so unlike the three above this is *not* uniformly in students' favour, which is exactly why it needs its own permission. In the SUGGESTIONS backfill ledger.
  - **AND THE OMR REPORT COULD NEVER HAVE FOUND THEM: the teacher's key agrees with the bank on Q23, and both are wrong.** A disagreement report finds where two sources DIFFER, never where they are wrong in the same direction — so "3 mismatches" is a floor on the defect count, not a measure of it. That is the same correlated-error limit this file records for dual-blind derivation, arriving from a different direction.
  - **A MEASUREMENT ERROR OF MINE, corrected: I reported "5 other wrong keys" and listed six.** The count was wrong, not the list. Also worth recording that **`audit:keys` reports NOTHING SCANNED for both sources** — it is scoped to `question_kind='practice'` and these are `pyq`, so the one probe that could have caught a solution-contradicts-key row has never been able to see them. It says so loudly rather than reporting a false clean, which is the only reason that gap is legible.
  - Verified: three keys flipped in place via `apply-adjudicated-fixes.ts` (asserts the current letter, recomputes `content_hash`, re-stamps IN PLACE so `paper_questions` is never orphaned — each row confirmed "still in 1 paper(s)"), mirrored into the records file with the patched record proven byte-equal to the DB target on stem, solution AND answer; recorded in `question_reviews` as `source_key_crosscheck`/`key_fixed` under run `key-fix:2026-09-07-lws-pqrs-test-1`; the OMR sheet rebuilt (answer distribution moved A11→9, D6→8, exactly the three flips); `verify-commit` still clean on the paper after all three hashes moved; `audit:text` and `audit:omml` clean.

- **2026-09-07 (second) — LWS "PQRS Test 1" becomes a `/dashboard/papers` paper, and the whole test turns out to be ALREADY IN THE BANK: 30 of 30 are live PUBLIC NDA GAT PYQs. Zero questions committed, zero bank drift — and the `verify-commit` gate had to be generalised before it could report the truth about a correct ingest.**
  - **THE DEDUP GATE PAID FOR ITSELF AT ITS FULL DESIGNED VALUE, which is the first time on this pipeline.** The skill's rule is *dedup on STEMS first, derive second*, precisely so a fully-recycled paper is caught before the expensive answer work. It was: all 30 items matched an existing bank row **fragment for fragment WITH THE SAME P/Q/R/S LETTER ASSIGNMENT and the same four printed options**, across five NDA GAT sittings — `GAT_2020_NDA1` Q11-20 → printed Q1-10, `NDA1_2019` Q38-40 → Q11-13, `GAT_NDA2_2019` Q37-40 → Q14-17, `NDA2_2021` Q21-30 → Q18-27, `GAT_NDA1_2022` Q21-23 → Q28-30. The teacher assembled the test out of past papers. **Nothing was derived, nothing was transcribed for the bank, and no answer was authored.**
  - **RECORDS COPIED OUT OF THE BANK, NOT OUT OF THE .docx — and that is what made the commit provably a no-op.** `contentHash` is `sha256(stem + sorted options + answer)` with whitespace collapsed, so mirroring each bank row verbatim makes the hash identical **by construction**; it was then verified against the stored `content_hash` for all 30 **before** applying (0 mismatches). `commitStaged` upserts with `ignoreDuplicates: true`, so `inserted=0 skipped=30`, and commit-paper's `content_hash` fallback resolved all 30 to the pre-existing rows. Confirmed afterwards from the live DB: **0 rows under the new `source_file`, and the Sentence Rearrangement chapter still holds exactly 288 rows — the count it held before.** Re-transcribing from the .docx would have hashed differently on the 17 rows whose bank stem carries a trailing instruction line, and inserted 17 PRIVATE near-duplicates of live PUBLIC PYQs.
  - **`verify-commit.ts` REPORTED 4 FAILURES ON A WHOLLY CORRECT INGEST, and the failure mode is the one the ledger predicted that morning.** Every check was scoped by `source_file`; a bank-mirrored paper owns **zero** rows under its own, so the gate measured an empty set and reported row-count 0-vs-30, a numbering mismatch, foreign paper questions and broken OMR parity. The ledger had identified exactly this on the APJ Biology ingest (where ONE question deduped byte-exactly) and left it unfixed pending permission. **A gate that cries wolf on a legitimate outcome is worse than no gate** — the next person either burns time re-deriving or learns to wave it through — and there was no honest way to report this ingest verified while it was red. Now it resolves each record the way `commit-paper` does (source_file, then content_hash), prints a `note` naming how many questions are bank-mirrored, scopes the practice-kind and dedup-gate checks to rows the ingest actually CREATED, and checks OMR parity on **resolved row identity** rather than `question_number` — which a mirrored row carries from its ORIGINAL paper, so numbering cannot identify a printed Q. **This touched a shipped gate that the ledger says needs explicit permission; it was flagged to the user rather than slipped in, and it is one commit to revert.**
  - **THE CHANGE WAS PROVEN BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BY SWEEPING ALL 65 REGISTRY SPECS, OLD BUILD VS NEW: 0 regressions, 27 papers fail → pass, 26 still failing on unrelated pre-existing causes.** Reasoning about the diff would not have been enough — and the sweep is what surfaced a SECOND, unrelated false alarm: a `createPaper:false` paper commits only `status:"new"` rows by design, so its dup/flawed records legitimately have no row and were reading as missing. Fixed by mirroring `commit-paper`'s own `commitRecs` rule at the call site so the two cannot drift.
  - **OMR PARITY WAS CONFIRMED A SECOND, DIFFERENT WAY, with a deliberately-failing control.** A throwaway read `paper_questions` ordered by `position` and compared raw question ids against the 30 resolved by hand: 30/30 in printed order, each link naming its origin paper. The control (two ids swapped) was detected as wrong — a check that has never gone red proves nothing, and the pre-fix run had already shown this one can.
  - **MY OWN VERIFICATION PROBE WAS WRONG BEFORE THE DATA WAS, and it read as a finding.** A first pass reported **17 of 30 "DIFF"** at fragment level while every option set matched — which should have been the tell. The cause: the bank stem for those rows ends with the printed instruction (`The correct sequence should be :`), and my splitter glued it onto fragment **S**, so S could never match. Corrected, all 30 are letter-for-letter identical. Same shape as [[probe-must-reach-the-code]]: the probe contradicted a much stronger signal sitting beside it.
  - **A LIVE KEY CONFLICT FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED.** Printed Q30 exists in the bank **twice with the identical four options and opposite keys** — the PYQ row (`56ee0236`, `GAT_NDA1_2022` Q23) keys **A = SPQR**, an Oswaal mock row (`563bfed0`) keys **C = QSPR**. QSPR is the grammatical reading; SPQR strands "in the arena of sport, perhaps" mid-sentence. They survive `content_hash` because the two typings differ in apostrophe and separators, and `audit:keys` never scans the pyq row because it is scoped to `question_kind='practice'`. Shipped PUBLIC content ⇒ logged to the SUGGESTIONS backfill ledger with the instruction to settle it against the actual UPSC paper first, **not** flipped on a reading.
  - **`flip-public` must never be run for this slug** — all 30 records are `status:"dup"`, so it is a no-op by construction, and the spec comment says so. Verified: paper `cde90a37-…`, 30 links, positions 1-30, one section, status `draft`; `check-taxonomy` clean; `build-tags` emitted the 30-row OMR sheet; typecheck clean; a `db:backup` was taken before the write. The scoped `audit:text`/`audit:keys`/`audit:omml` runs are deliberately skipped — they filter on `source_file`, which owns zero rows here, and the 30 PYQs they would otherwise scan belong to five other corpora.

- **2026-09-07 — JEE Mains gets 24 timed mocks (163 → 187), and they are the first in this bank whose answers are NOT option labels. NEET needed nothing: it was already complete. Migration 0087.**
  - **THE ASK WAS "JEE MAINS AND NEET", AND HALF OF IT WAS ALREADY DONE.** NEET has 8 PYQ papers in the bank and 8 published mocks, counts matching exactly — nothing to build until a new sitting is ingested. Measuring that first is what kept the session from re-deriving a finished pipeline. (Incidentally NEET has since grown a **1,769-question PRACTICE corpus** this file does not record; irrelevant to mocks, which are PYQ-only, but the header is stale.)
  - **A `source_file` IS NOT A SITTING FOR JEE, and that is a THIRD discovery rule.** NDA splits sittings by `pyq_month`; CDS, NEET and MHT-CET by `source_file`. JEE can use neither: `pyq_month` is NULL on all 10,493 rows, and a 2025 file holds a whole DATE — `JEE_2023_Jan25.docx` is 180 rows because rows 1-90 are one shift and 91-180 the next, `JEE_2025_Jan23.docx` is 150 = 2 × 75. So a sitting is a **`source_row` BLOCK within a file**. Read off the data, not assumed: each block runs Physics 1-20 MCQ / 21-25 NAT, Chemistry 26-45 / 46-50, Maths 51-70 / 71-75. The split is deterministic (`block = ceil(source_row / 75)`), so no registry guesswork was needed — only the holds are hand-maintained, and `scripts/mocks/jeeSittings.ts` derives everything else from `scripts/jee/papers/*.json`.
  - **ONLY 2025+ IS EXPRESSIBLE, and the reason is a pattern change rather than a corpus gap.** A 2021-2024 shift printed 90 questions of which a candidate attempted **75** — all 60 MCQ plus **any 5 of 10** NAT per subject. `gradeMock` has no "attempt at most N" concept, so those sittings would score out of **360 instead of 300** and let a student answer all ten; the marking also differed between Section A and B in those years, while `buildMockPaper` stamps one flat `marks`/`negMarks` on every question. From 2025 Section B is 5 compulsory NAT at the same +4/−1, so the paper is simply its 75 and the whole problem disappears. The 2021-2024 corpus is ingested and deliberately NOT built; `deriveJeeSittings` drops it by year rather than failing on it.
  - **THE DATABASE ITSELF REFUSED THE FEATURE, which is what made a migration unavoidable.** `attempt_answers.selected_label` carried `CHECK (selected_label IN ('A','B','C','D'))` from 0044 — the only column holding a student's answer — so a NAT response of `17280` was rejected by Postgres and no application code could route around it. **0087 adds `numeric_response numeric` rather than widening that column**: widening is the smaller diff and the worse change, because it would store a number in a column named *label* (read as a letter by grading, palette and review), **delete the existing guard for all 163 already-shipped mocks** to serve 24 new ones, and make the two answer kinds indistinguishable — a student typing `3` on an MCQ is a different event from choosing option C. A coherence CHECK keeps three states legible (both null = unanswered, exactly one = answered, both = refused), the 0046/0051 pattern. **Proven deployed rather than assumed**: a DO block mutated a real row to the incoherent state, reported `constraint_fired=t`, and aborted itself so nothing committed — 31,232 existing rows untouched, 0 numeric set.
  - **THE ANSWER AXIS IS NOW A DISCRIMINATED UNION, and choosing that over an optional field is the load-bearing decision.** `"A"|"B"|"C"|"D"` ran unbroken from storage through `loadAnswerKey`, `gradeMock`, `paletteState`, `MockRunner` and the review page. An extra optional `numericAnswer` field would have let every one of those keep reading `.label` and silently mis-grade Section B; a union made **the typechecker enumerate all of them — 9 source call sites plus 3 test files**, including `scripts/reviews/regrade-attempt.ts`, which was not on the plan's list at all.
  - **THAT SCRIPT TURNED OUT TO BE THE WORST OF THEM.** It read the key straight from `options` — a SECOND implementation of "what is the answer", and one **blind to numeric questions by construction**, so regrading any JEE attempt would have scored all 15 Section-B questions as skipped and quietly moved real students' marks. It now calls the same `loadAnswerKey` the app grades with (`query.ts` has no `server-only` guard, so a script can), and its A-D validation guard became an ABSENCE guard, which is what a validated union leaves worth refusing.
  - **TWO MORE PLACES WERE COMPUTING RIGHT-VS-WRONG SEPARATELY.** `getAttemptReview` derived its own per-question verdict, and `submitAttempt`'s activity emitter compared `selected !== gq.answer` by hand — so the score, the review list and the wrong-answer drill fuel were three implementations free to disagree on screen, and the latter two could not see a numeric response at all. All three now go through one pure `verdictFor`, and the emitter reads the verdict `gradeMock` already produced. Same two-renderers drift this file records twice for the docx exporter.
  - **A SILENT FALLBACK REMOVED: `answer: key[q.questionId] ?? "A"`** marked every A-picker correct on a question whose key was missing. It cannot fire (`validatePaperRows` refuses to build such a paper) but the union forced the question, and `verdictFor` now scores a null key as **skipped, never wrong** — our defect must not cost a student marks.
  - **THE NTA TOLERANCE IS CORRECT AND INERT, and measuring that is worth more than implementing it.** The 2-decimal rule was chosen deliberately — and **all 546 NAT answers across 2025+2026 are non-negative integers at scale 0**, so no real question in the shipped corpus can exercise it. It is implemented properly (a distance comparison, not round-then-compare: `Math.round(4.005*100)` is 400 because 4.005 is held as 4.00499…, so rounding disagrees with itself at the boundary; ties go to the student) and pinned by **synthetic** tests that say so in their own comment. It earns its place in the 2021-2024 tier, which carries 14 decimal answers and negatives down to −640.
  - **THE 2025 SHIFT LABELS ARE AN INFERENCE AND ARE RECORDED AS ONE.** 2026 states its shift twice — the filename (`JEE_2026_Jan21_S1.docx`) and the config's own pyqNote ("21 Jan 2026 Shift 1"). 2025 states it NOWHERE: its pyqNote is the bare date and the extracted pages carry only `Physics / Section - A`, with no shift, session, morning or afternoon marker anywhere. So "Shift 1 = rows 1-75" is convention. Following the `MHT_CET_2025_PCM` precedent it ships labelled but flagged `shiftInferred`, with the builder printing the inference on every run — a distinctive-stem check against a published copy would settle it. **11 of the 24 shipped papers are affected.**
  - **13 OF 37 SITTINGS ARE HELD**, each short by 1-3 questions the bank never had — a mock is the real paper or it is nothing, and a soft count would relabel a 72-question fragment as "JEE Mains 2025 (3 Apr, Shift 1)". A hold is an ASSERTION: the builder still attempts it and FAILS on one that now reconstructs, so closing a corpus hole surfaces as a prompt. The builder's 24-built/13-held split independently reproduced the figure derived from SQL beforehand.
  - **A LATENT GAP FOUND EN ROUTE: `CDS_GK_PAPER` and `CDS_MATHS_PAPER` were never added to `ALL_BLUEPRINTS`**, so `getBlueprint("cds","gk")` returned null for 35 published mocks. Nothing in `src/` calls it today, so it was inert — but it is exactly the gap that bites the first consumer. Fixed, with a test that resolves every exported blueprint so it cannot recur.
  - **A TEST WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON, caught by my own fixture.** `deriveJeeSittings`'s orphan-hold guard compared the real HOLDS map against a one-file fixture, so the "throws on a stale hold" test threw because *all thirteen* real holds were orphans — not because of the bogus one it named. Holds are now injectable and the test asserts BOTH directions (a matching hold does not throw; only the bogus one does).
  - **`tests/mocks-nav.test.ts` used `jee-mains` in FOUR places as its "registered but no mocks" exemplar** — moved there from MHT-CET on 2026-09-01, the third instance of this shape. Rather than move it to another exam that might gain mocks later, each invariant now uses **`worksheets-11-12`, which is practice-only and therefore can NEVER back a mock**; jee-mains gains the positive assertion. A structurally permanent exemplar, so this does not have to move a fourth time.
  - **VERIFIED, not asserted**, all after the write and against the live bank: 187 mocks · 24 JEE · 1,800 refs · **0 dangling, 0 non-PUBLIC, 0 non-pyq, 0 MCQs with anything but one correct option, 0 NAT without a numeric answer, 0 NAT carrying options** · 0 wrong-section rows · Physics occupies 1-25, Chemistry 26-50, Maths 51-75 in every paper · positions contiguous 1-75 · exactly 15 NAT per paper · every paper drawn from ONE source file spanning exactly 75 consecutive rows · **0 questions appearing in two mocks** (the check that matters most, since blocks 1 and 2 come from the same file — 2025-jan-23 S1 reads rows 1-75 and S2 reads 76-150) · totals 75/300/180min. A slug/id collision check ran BEFORE the write (the mock id is `slugToUuid(slug)`, so a clash silently overwrites a real mock): 24 distinct slugs, 24 distinct ids, 0 colliding. The other 163 mocks were confirmed untouched by `updated_at`, and CDS (55 + 3 held) and NEET (8) still dry-run identically after the union refactor.
  - **OWED, and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through.** The runner is client-interactive behind auth, so nothing headless proves the numeric input accepts a value, that the palette turns green for an answered NAT question, or that the review page's two-value block lays out. Worth checking a Section-B question end to end (type → resume → submit → review) on one 2026 paper.

- **2026-09-06 (second) — `/books` gains its SECOND book: MHT-CET Mathematics, 2,136 printed of 2,228. It is structurally the opposite of the English book, and building it found SEVEN wrong answers in the public bank — two of them in the copy the book would have printed.**
  - **THE CORPUS INVERTS EVERY ASSUMPTION THE FIRST BOOK WAS BUILT ON, measured before a line was written.** `set_id` is NULL on all 2,228 rows against 3,175-of-3,180 in English, so **sets do not exist**; the Layout-A gate ("no set spans a subtopic") is satisfied VACUOUSLY in all 27 chapters and subtopic grouping is free everywhere, where English has three chapters that can never group. 100% MCQ, 100% carry a solution, 0 missing a subtopic, 11 figures in the whole corpus. And the subject row is **`Maths`, not `Mathematics`** — nine other exams spell it the long way; a near-miss there does not error, it yields an EMPTY BOOK, which is exactly what `tests/books-registry.test.ts` exists to catch (it now covers both books in both directions: 27 chapters + 86 subtopics resolved).
  - **THE SITTING NEEDED A THIRD RULE, because MHT-CET reads by neither.** `pyq_month` collapses 45 source-file labels into 6 buckets (17 share `2023/May`, 12 share `2024/May`) and is ACTIVELY WRONG on one — `MHT_CET_2025_PCM.xlsx` is stamped May and is a second upload of an April paper. The filenames carry the date in at least eight conventions, one of them a typo (`14tthMay2024`), so no regex reads them all. The answer already existed in `scripts/mocks/mhtcetSittings.ts`, so the sitting IDENTITY moved to `src/lib/mocks/` (a page needs it at request time and `src/` cannot import `scripts/`, which reaches for `node:fs`) and the mock builder re-exports it. **Proven behaviour-preserving**: 42 sittings, semantically identical output, `tests/mock-mhtcet-sittings.test.ts` green untouched, and the config-agreement guarantee kept — it was structural (derivation) and is now an explicit throw, **proven to fire** on a renamed booklet and on a duplicated source file.
  - **THE HEADLINE FINDING, and it inverts the obvious reading twice.** 122 of 2,228 rows are a repeated stem (5.5%, against ONE duplicate in the English book's 3,180) and would print adjacent under one subtopic heading. They survive `content_hash` because the hash covers the options and two independent typings spell them differently. Collapsing them into one question carrying "Asked N times: …" turns the defect into the book's best feature — a high-yield marker. **But the count must be in SITTINGS, never in rows: 90 of the 118 groups resolve to ONE sitting** through the three duplicate-upload pairs, so a row-counting badge would print "asked twice" on 90 questions that were asked ONCE. That makes `mergeWith` load-bearing for correctness rather than a convenience. Final split: **90 duplicate-upload (90 rows, no badge) / 28 genuine repeat (32 rows, badge)**.
  - **THE STEM KEY MUST KEEP MATH OPERATORS, and measuring that prevented deleting real questions.** The obvious key (strip all punctuation) finds 126 redundant rows; keeping `+ - * / ^ = < >` finds 121. Reading the five-row difference settles it: **three are genuinely DIFFERENT questions** — `cos 2t` vs `cos^2 t`, two plane pairs differing only in a sign, and a line through `z-m` vs `z+m`. A false merge DELETES a distinct question AND mislabels the pair as an answer conflict; one of those three was sitting in my "18 answer conflicts" and was never a conflict at all. The one true duplicate the strict key splits is separated by an empty `_{}^{}`, a typesetting artifact, so that alone is stripped. Net 122 rows, and the rule is that the key errs towards SPLITTING.
  - **SEVEN WRONG ANSWERS FOUND AND FIXED AGAINST THE PRINTED PAPERS — the mechanism is the point.** A defect invisible in one copy becomes loud when the same paper exists twice: where two independent typings of ONE paper disagree about the answer, one is simply wrong and the source settles it outright. Every fix was adjudicated against the booklet AND re-derived by hand, so a defect in the published key could not be inherited. **THE KEEPER IS NOT ALWAYS THE RIGHT COPY** — four sit in the redundant copy and **two sit in the copy the book PRINTS**, so "trust the primary upload" would have shipped two wrong answers. The sharpest: a triangle question stored as `l(AB) = 2sqrt(3)` where the paper prints `sqrt(23)`, which makes it evaluate to 6.4 and **match no printed option** — unanswerable, in BOTH copies; and a cosine keyed as `17/9`, which exceeds 1 and so cannot be a cosine (the paper prints `sqrt(17)/9`). Also two option-text corruptions where all four options read `log_e x` for the paper's `log(e/x)`. Recorded in `question_reviews` under `source_key_crosscheck`; the fix script asserts BOTH the current and target state, refuses the whole batch on any mismatch, and is idempotent. **`content_hash` is deliberately left untouched** — recomputing it would make a re-upload of the original defective spreadsheet insert a DUPLICATE of the row just repaired (the 2026-09-02 statement-layout call, same reasoning). **Fixing the defects then resolved 5 review groups into agreement**, taking the review list 34 -> 29.
  - **THREE LATENT BUGS THE SECOND BOOK EXPOSED, all silent.** `loadBookOverview` hardcoded `examOfSection = { nda, cds }`, so any other section key counts **0** for every chapter with no error; the reader's move-to-section control was a hardcoded `nda <-> cds` flip that would have offered a section the book does not have; and four scripts hardcoded `NDA_CDS_ENGLISH`, so `smoke.ts` would have reported the English book healthy while the MHT-CET book was the broken one. Two more surfaced on first run: **`smoke.ts` assumed TWO sections** (it threw) and compared a section's raw `questionCount` against the TOC, which counts only what PRINTS — equal only in a book with no curation, so it fired on every collapsed duplicate. All five fixed, with the English book **proven byte-identical throughout** (3,180, every per-exam count unchanged, "every check passed").
  - **A GAP NO TEST COULD HAVE CAUGHT: the print view rendered NO provenance at all for a maths question.** Both its branches are conditional on a shared passage or an authored Directions line, and a maths question has neither — so the book would have printed 2,136 questions with nothing saying which paper any of them came from. Provenance is now per-question, and only where the set did not already print one, so the English book is untouched.
  - **FOUR PROBE FAILURES, every one mine, and three of them nearly became findings.** A grep for `l(AB)` "proved" two 2023 files were different papers — the second writes it as `\mathbf{l}\mathbf{(AB)}` and the merge was fine. `grep -c` counts LINES, so minified HTML reported 185 provenance lines where there are 221. A SQL `LIKE` scan for double backslashes returned 0 because **LIKE treats backslash as its own escape** (the real count is 147 options bank-wide). And [[heredoc-backslash-eating]] fired **four times**, twice corrupting a regex into an unmatchable one. In every case the probe was wrong and the data was fine.
