And I had written "found only by looking at the rendered card" into the pipeline memory an hour earlier. **Checking a precedent means checking its OUTPUT, and a render-layer change is accepted against the render, never against the stored string.**
  - **`formatProvenance` prefixed "Q" onto every ref, and 22,368 PUBLIC rows across 8 exams read wrong.** The helper does `Q${questionNumber}`, which is right for a PYQ paper's bare numeral (`42` -> `Q42`) and wrong for every textbook and worksheet corpus, whose refs are DESCRIPTIVE: `QEx Q.2 (ii)`, `QMisc I (iv)`, `QLvl I-CW Q1`, `QA relation between length of an arc...`. **Pre-existing and shipped**, surfaced only because a new chapter put it in front of a reader; it was taken with a 360 and explicit go-ahead rather than folded in silently. The fix is CONDITIONAL, never a blanket removal — `Q42` is correct and wanted for the PYQ corpora — and it is render-only: exactly two consumers (the `/browse` card and `/guide` worked-example citations), no DB write, and the Word export deliberately avoids this helper. **All 8 pre-existing assertions use bare numerals, so the fix ADDS cases rather than changing pinned behaviour**; three new tests pin both directions and were confirmed failing for the right reason first.
  - **A second lane exists and is the agreed next step:** `State_Board/PYQs/` holds 16 chapterwise board-PYQ `.docx` (Std XII ch.1-16, ~25 provenance tags per chapter, real pi surviving in the text layer) plus 9 raw papers 2016-2025 — precisely the `scripts/mh-hsc-12-pyq/` shape, born-digital and pandoc, so far cheaper per question than the vision lane. See [[state-board-physics-ingestion]].

- **2026-09-02 — A 120-q NDA paper over four State Board Std XI chapters, and the bank-wide statement-layout repair it surfaced: 285 stems across 4 exams now print each numbered claim on its own line, and the BLOCKING gate that should have caught it is no longer blind.**
  - **THE PAPER.** `NDA Maths - State Board XI: Angle, Trigonometry-I, Sets & Relations, Functions (120 Q)` — Functions 48 · Sets & Relations 42 · Trigonometry-I 15 · Angle and its Measurement 15. Scope came from the **syllabus map** (`syllabus_concept_exams.covered_by` on the NDA bank spine, authored 2026-08-07), never from chapter names, and that is what made it correct: **95 of the 138 NDA "Trigonometric Identities" PYQs are Trigonometry-II** (Compound Angle 38, Multiple/Half-Angle 30, Product-to-Sum 27 all cite XI:3.x). The two surviving subtopics cite BOTH XI:2.x and XI:3.x, so they straddle and no subtopic filter separates them — all 43 were read individually and 15 solo rows survive strict Ch.2 scoping. **`Angle and its Measurement` has ZERO NDA PYQs** — only 5 of 2,160 mention radian/arc/sector and none is in a trigonometry chapter — so it is filled per blueprint RULE 2 from the Cadetprep Worksheets course, tiers stepped up one per RULE 2a.
  - **Three additive `ChapterPlan` filters**, each defaulting to prior behaviour so every existing spec selects byte-identically: `allowUsed` (23 of the 32 in-scope HARD rows are already in a paper; refusing repeats caps the paper near 7% HARD against an NDA norm of 26.5%), `soloOnly` (RULE 1 the cheap way — `selectByQuota` is set-blind and the docx exporter groups a shared context by ADJACENCY, so picking set members risks both splitting and scattering a set), and `includeIds` — an **allow**-list, because an exclude-list fails OPEN and would admit Trig-II rows added by a later ingest.
  - **THEN THE PAPER PRINTED 22 OF ITS 120 STEMS WITH THE STATEMENTS RUN TOGETHER, and the diagnosis that mattered was that this is DATA, not rendering.** Both renderers already honour a real newline — the Word exporter splits on `\n` into `TextRun({break:1})` (`mathRuns`), the web renderer wraps text in `white-space: pre-wrap` (`KatexRenderer`). Proof: 6 stems in the same paper printed correctly because their text carries newlines. **198 of 286 NDA Maths statement-style rows (69%) were stored flat.**
  - **THE BLOCKING GATE WAS ONE PATTERN AWAY FROM CATCHING IT.** `paper-text.ts`'s `P1-statement-run-on` is in `BLOCKING_RULES` and does exactly this job — but `STATEMENT_LABEL` requires the literal word `Statement`/`Assertion`/`Reason`, while NDA's dominant style is a bare `1.`/`2.` after a lead-in. So the build reported "Paper text: OK" and applied. The narrowness was deliberate (its comment says it exists so the prose word "statements" cannot match), so P1 now ORs in a second scan over `findStatementLabels` rather than loosening the original, which is preserved bit-for-bit. **Proven rather than asserted: P1 fires on 284 of the 285 pre-repair stems and 0 after.**
  - **THE SCOPE DECISION IS THE LESSON. A regex is not a scope.** A bare label pattern matches **899 PUBLIC rows bank-wide and 521 of them are Match Lists** whose labels are already table cells. Reading the survivors by exam showed the defect rate is wildly uneven: in JEE Mains / NEET / MHT-CET roughly **12 of 14 candidates were false positives** — options named in a parenthetical (*"(Options are structures: (1) nitrobenzene…"*), reagent sequences, mid-sentence enumerations (*"as the train (1) approaches … and then (2) recedes"*), and a figure reference (*"Figure 1. electron probability density"*) that produced a line reading only "Figure". Those exams are therefore excluded **by name** (`--exams` allow-list), not by pattern.
  - **FIVE GUARDS, EVERY ONE EARNED FROM A LIVE ROW** (`scripts/lib/statementLayout.ts`, pure + 30 TDD cases): mask math zones first (`\(1\cdot5\)`, `\([.]\)`); skip a real GFM table; skip `Match the following/column` and a bare `Column I / Column II` list; require the run to ASCEND from its first label, scanning each label only AFTER the previous one (so *"…can never be less than 2. Which of the above"* takes the label, not the trailing numeral); and require the FIRST label to be **introduced** by `:`/`?`/`.`/newline, which is what separates a list from an enumeration inside a sentence. **`A.`/`B.` alpha labels were dropped entirely** — measured across every live candidate they drove ZERO rewrites while prose supplies the shape readily.
  - **THE LEAD-IN GUARD VALIDATED ITSELF ACROSS CORPORA.** It was derived from the JEE/NEET false positives, and it independently caught **every one of the 5 corrupting rows** that two review agents later found by reading — including two NDA Chemistry `Column I / Column II` lists whose naive split glued each Column-II entry to the NEXT Column-I entry and thereby **asserted pairings the question exists to test, one of them the correct answer**.
  - **`content_hash` IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTOUCHED — do not "fix" the mismatch.** Dedup is `(org_id, exam_id, content_hash)` over the text, so adding newlines changes what the hash would be. Recomputing it would make a re-upload of the original `.xlsx` (which still holds flat text) match nothing and insert a duplicate of every repaired row; leaving it means such a re-upload still dedups and skips. No `.xlsx` is tracked, so there is no upstream source of record to correct instead. The cost is that `question_reviews.reviewed_content_hash` will not mark a review stale after this edit — defensible, since a line break changes no claim, option or answer, but it is a real weakening and is recorded in the script header rather than left to be discovered.
  - **Verified, not asserted:** 285 rows updated and read back; **285/285 whitespace-only** (a character-frequency diff shows the only changes anywhere are `\n` added and spaces consumed); **0 newlines inside any math zone**, 0 unbalanced zones across all 3,537 multiline rows in scope; 0 new blank lines; 0 label-only lines; **re-run finds 0 to repair** (idempotent); the paper's Word export gained **94 line breaks** with 0 raw-LaTeX fallbacks. Snapshot written per run and `--revert=<file>` restores. `db:backup` taken first (76 tables / 353,335 rows).
  - **A probe failure worth recording, because it fired FOUR times in one session.** Authoring anything containing a backslash through a shell heredoc or `python -c` corrupts it: `\b` became a literal **backspace byte (0x08)** inside a regex, making it unmatchable and invisible in review — caught only because a test went red. A later `python -c` check then reported **58 rows with a newline inside a math zone**; the file-authored version of the same check reports **0**. Both the data and the earlier agent reports were right; the one-liner was wrong. Author through the editor. See [[heredoc-backslash-eating]] + [[control-char-latex-corruption]].
  - **Left alone, deliberately:** ~31 rows where the closing directive stays glued to the last item because it follows a `.` inside that item — an under-repair, not damage (the text is intact and no worse than before), and widening the split rule there is exactly what starts cutting mid-sentence. Also logged and NOT fixed: a pre-existing **label-space mismatch** in ~15 Foundation Physics rows whose stems number items `1.`/`(1)` while their options refer to them as `A and C` or `(i) and (ii)`.

- **2026-09-01 — MHT-CET gains 60 timed PYQ mocks (mocks 63 → 123): the PCM group's TWO papers per sitting, across 45 shifts 2021-2025. 30 of the 90 possible papers are deliberately HELD rather than shipped short, and the single most consequential fix in the ship is a UI bug that had nothing to do with MHT-CET until MHT-CET arrived.**
  - **THE CORPUS RECONSTRUCTS BETTER THAN CDS DID, and measuring that first is what made this small.** `source_row` is non-null on all 6,614 PUBLIC PYQ rows with **zero duplicate ordering keys** within any subject, and **zero rows lack an answer key**. Two numbering conventions coexist (the xlsx uploads run Physics 2-51 / Chemistry 52-101 / Maths 102-151, the 2025 April docx run 1-50 / 51-100 / 101-150) and neither needs handling, because `orderPaperRows` only ever sorts WITHIN a section. Verified after the write: **0 ordering mismatches across all 4,350 refs** — position order equals `source_row` order in every section of every mock.
  - **`pyq_month` is not merely useless here, it is ACTIVELY MISLEADING — 17 of the 45 sittings share (2023, "May").** The NDA year+month discovery loop would emit ONE slug for all 17 and, since the mock id is `slugToUuid(slug)`, each upsert would silently overwrite the last, leaving 16 real papers missing with no error. So MHT-CET is `source_file`-keyed (the CDS/NEET shape) with a date-and-shift slug stem, `mht-cet-2023-may-03-s1-maths`.
  - **THE REGISTRY IS HALF-DERIVED AND HALF HAND-WRITTEN, and that split is forced by the corpus rather than chosen.** `scripts/mhtcet/config.ts` is the source of record for the 13 April-2025 shifts, so those are DERIVED exactly as CDS derives from `scripts/cds/config.ts` — a renamed booklet there now fails a test here instead of leaving a mock silently empty. The other **32 shifts came in through the generic `/upload` path years earlier and have no config anywhere in the repo** (grepped repo-wide), so they can only be hand-written. Their labels are deliberately NOT taken from `pyq_note` — see the next point.
  - **A `pyq_note` IS FREE TEXT AND ONE OF THEM IS PROVABLY WRONG.** `MHT_CET_3rdMay2023_S1_QB.xlsx` stores the note "3rd May 2nd Shift", contradicting its own filename, while a *separate* file already legitimately claims that sitting — so on the note's word we would have had two files for 3rd May Shift 2 and none for Shift 1. Settled against the local source booklets rather than by picking the more official-looking field: stems unique to that file ("watch glass", "coloured compound") appear ONLY in `3 may shift 1 (ques).docx`, and the Shift-2 file's stems ("cold or hot water", "equal intercepts") only in `3 may shift 2`. **The FILENAME is right and the note is a typo**; both 3-May shifts exist and neither is missing. Worth noting a single probe would not have settled it — "r.p.s" appears in BOTH files and discriminates nothing. The wrong note is still live on ~150 rows and is a backfill-ledger item, not something to repair in passing.
  - **30 PAPERS ARE HELD, AND THE DECOMPOSITION IS WHAT MADE THE POLICY DECIDABLE.** A soft count (NEET's) was rejected: NEET omits `count` because its layout genuinely varies by sitting, whereas a short MHT-CET paper is questions MISSING, so a soft count ships a fragment labelled as the real paper — `13 May 2024 Shift 1` would have become a 62-question "100-question paper". Splitting the gap by CAUSE gives two different answers: **10 papers are short because a flawed question is deliberately PRIVATE** (irrecoverable — the alternative is un-withdrawing a question we judged bad) and **20 because rows are absent from the bank** (never ingested, or absorbed by cross-shift `content_hash` dedup — closable by a future ingest). Both are held, but only one is a defect. **A `hold` is an ASSERTION, not a mute**: the builder still attempts every paper and reports a hold whose paper NOW reconstructs as a failure telling you to delete the line — otherwise closing a corpus hole would leave the mock un-shipped forever, in silence.
  - **THE SHARPEST FINDING WAS NOT ABOUT MHT-CET AT ALL: the mock instructions screen had a live latent bug that only a zero-penalty exam could expose.** `/mock/[slug]` hard-coded a marking scheme true for the only three exams it had ever served, and for MHT-CET would have rendered *"**0** marks for every wrong answer (negative marking)"* — asserting a rule the exam does not have — and *"**0** marks for un-attempted questions — **skip if unsure**"*, which is **STRICTLY HARMFUL**: with no penalty a guess is never worse than a blank, so that advice costs marks. It would have contradicted our own MHT-CET guide (which sets `targetAttempts` to the full paper for exactly this reason) **on the page a student reads immediately before starting**. Fixed at the cause with a pure `src/lib/mocks/marking.ts` so the zero-penalty branch is provable without rendering the page. The same [[default-becomes-assertion]] shape as the coverage and "no single section" bugs: a default defensible for the cases its author had becomes a false assertion for the first case they did not. The `MockRunner` marks chip was left alone deliberately — `+2 / 0` is accurate, and rewriting it would have changed CDS's shipped display for no correctness gain.
  - **`tests/mocks-nav.test.ts` used MHT-CET as its exemplar of a registered-but-mock-less exam** — the third instance of this shape (after `exam-nav`/`format-mix` on 2026-08-22). Each invariant MOVED to JEE Mains (a live 10,614-question exam with no mocks) and MHT-CET gained the positive assertion, rather than an assertion being deleted.
  - **Verified rather than asserted**, all after the write and against the live bank: 60 mocks (33 Maths + 27 Phy&Chem) · 4,350 refs · **0 dangling, 0 non-PUBLIC, 0 non-pyq, 0 duplicated within a mock, 0 missing keys** · **0 wrong-section** (every `physics` ref really is a Physics row) · Physics occupies positions 1-50 and Chemistry 51-100 in every Paper II · **0 mocks mixing two sittings** · **0 questions appearing in two mocks** · totals exactly 50/100 and 100/100 marks. The builder's own 60-built/30-held/**0-unexplained-failures** split independently reproduced the split derived from SQL beforehand. A `db:backup` was taken before the bulk write per the standing runbook. **Owed and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through** — the runner is client-interactive behind auth, so nothing headless proves a CET mock starts, grades and reviews; worth checking that the new no-negative-marking instruction line reads correctly there.

### 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31 — archived 2026-09-14

- **2026-08-31 (fourth) — every `/books` chapter's printed pages now open with a CONTENTS table putting each subtopic's range under BOTH exams side by side, and Grammar joins the grouped chapters via a new `members` field that lets ONE printed heading cover SEVERAL bank subtopics. Grammar goes from 18 spanning sets / 81 questions under a wrong heading to ZERO of both.** Gate PASS, 744 prerendered `.html` (the pre-change baseline, so nothing de-cached).
  - **THE CONTENTS TABLE IS DERIVED FROM THE SAME PASS THAT NUMBERS THE PAPER AND THE KEY, deliberately.** `chapterContents` takes the `ChapterNumbering` rather than re-walking the sections, so the contents, the printed numbers and the answer key at the back are ONE computation; a hand-written "Synonyms Q.1-150" is a fourth place for the truth to live and would rot on the next sync or exclusion with nothing to say so. Exclusions flow through free — a block curated down to nothing has no row, matching what prints.
  - **IT GOES AT THE FRONT, NOT PER SECTION, and the reason is that only the front can put the two exams SIDE BY SIDE** — which is the premise of the book, since a chapter exists to carry both exams' take on one subtopic. A per-section line would also mostly repeat the page: each subtopic block already prints its own heading and count inline. Instead the block heading gained its own range (`Synonyms  Q.1-150 · 150`), so mid-chapter orientation needs no trip back to page 1. **A BLANK CELL IS REAL INFORMATION** — it says that exam does not ask this subtopic here — so it prints a dash, never nothing; Fill in the Blanks demonstrates it live (`Contextual Word Selection` is NDA-only). A FLAT chapter gets the table with no subtopic rows, because its sets span subtopics so a per-subtopic range would be non-contiguous and therefore FALSE; the section ranges still answer the question a flat chapter raises, which is where the other exam begins.
  - **THE HEADLINE FINDING ON GRAMMAR: all 18 spanning sets mix ONLY three subtopics — Preposition Usage, Discourse Markers and Connectors, Articles/Determiners/Quantifiers — and never any other. Merging those three takes the chapter to 0 spanning sets.** Measured, not eyeballed. And the reason they interleave is that they are ONE TASK: those CDS papers print a single instruction, *"fill the blank with the appropriate word"*, over ten questions, and the three subtopics classify what the ANSWER turned out to be rather than what the student was asked to do. **CDS says so itself** — three of its "Preposition Usage" sets are headed *"select the most appropriate preposition OR DETERMINER"*. So `SubtopicGroupDef` gained `members?: string[]`: one printed block, several bank subtopics, no set split and no re-tagging of the bank.
  - **THAT ALSO CORRECTS THE REGISTRY'S OWN STATED REASON, which was right about one chapter and imprecise about two.** It said grouping Grammar, Spotting Errors and RC "would tear questions away from their passage". True of **Reading Comprehension** — 1,434-char passages, 46 of CDS's 52 sets spanning. False of the other two, whose "set" is a 135- and 209-char DIRECTIONS LINE with no passage at all; nothing would be torn. The *verdict* still held for a different reason — filing a whole set under its first question's subtopic mislabels 81 Grammar questions and **236 of Spotting Errors' 403 (59%)**, which is worse than useless. **Measure the harm, not the shape.**
  - **IDIOMS AND CLOZE WERE NEVER THE PROBLEM PEOPLE ASSUMED, and had simply never been measured** — the old comment listed spanning counts for three chapters only. Each has **exactly ONE subtopic** (all 236 `Idiom Meaning`, all 219 `Word Selection in Passage`), confirmed against the taxonomy so it is an editorial fact and not an untagged gap. Grouping them yields one block restating the chapter name. The answer is not "can't", it is **"nothing to group"**. Left alone, with RC, on the user's call.
  - **QUESTION-LEVEL GROUPING WAS DESIGNED, COSTED AND REJECTED — and the tagging is why.** Because Grammar's and Spotting Errors' sets carry no passage, splitting one is permitted, and grouping by question would give 9 and 7 clean blocks. But reading the actual stems shows the trio's tagging is NOISY: *"If I ___ you I ___ love to accept the offer"* is tagged Discourse Markers and is a conditional verb form; *"My sister asked me ___ willing to go abroad"* is reported speech. Stated as an observation needing a human eye, not a proven defect — the answers are blanked, so certainty is not available. Either way, **question-level grouping would render a noisy classification as three confident headings, presenting noise as structure.** Merging does not. It would also have shredded a ten-question set into up to nine fragments (`GBGBGBGBGG`), and the curation unit is the whole SET (`planSetMove`).
  - **A MERGED BLOCK MUST KEEP THE SECTION'S CHRONOLOGY, and that is the one test that matters.** `toBlocks` now FILTERS the ordered set list per block instead of concatenating each member's sets — gathering all the prepositions then all the connectors would silently reorder a half that prints oldest-first. It is pinned by a test whose naive implementation fails. **`toBlocks` had ZERO tests before this**; six of the eleven new ones pin its EXISTING behaviour (declared order, appending an undeclared subtopic rather than dropping it, "Other" for an untagged question) so the rewrite could be shown behaviour-preserving.
  - **THE REGISTRY GUARD NOW COVERS SUBTOPIC NAMES, which it never did — and that failure is quieter than a bad chapter name.** A typo'd subtopic does not error: the declared block simply never matches and those questions are APPENDED under their raw name in alphabetical order, chapter intact, every question present, silently disagreeing with the authored order and the contents ranges. It checks three things — a declared name that resolves nowhere, a live subtopic no block declares, a subtopic claimed by two blocks — and **each was PROVEN to go red by injecting the fault**, then green when restored.
  - **TWO MEASUREMENT SCRIPTS, both closing a gap that existed rather than speculative.** `scripts/books/subtopic-report.ts` re-measures the Layout-A gate for every chapter (spanning sets, questions-under-a-wrong-heading, median context = passage vs directions-line, `--spanning` and `--directions` detail modes) — it exists because the gate's numbers lived only in a hand-written comment, and **a number in a comment cannot be re-checked**. Its headline counts are measured against BLOCKS, so a merged chapter reads clean instead of reporting a permanent false alarm about the grouping it just validated. `scripts/books/render-print.tsx` renders the print view to a standalone HTML file: every `/books` route is auth-gated and `force-dynamic`, so `next build` never executes one and a green build proves only that those pages COMPILE. It is also the fastest way to eyeball a layout change with no dev server and no login.
  - **`--directions` settled a second registry decision with evidence rather than taste: NO block carries an authored Directions line.** Parts of Speech and Sentence Completion each could — all seven and all three of their wordings are the same task, and the tool prints EVERY wording rather than a top-N precisely because the unseen tail is where a different task hides — but writing that prose needs the full instruction text read, not the measurement that it exists. **Correct Sentence Identification can never take one:** its five CDS wordings are five different tasks (combining two sentences · choosing which of two uses a word correctly · a word used variously across S1/S2/S3). Per-set Directions are always correct, so they stay.
  - **AN OPERATIONAL LESSON THAT COST REAL TIME AND IS RECORDED NOWHERE ELSE: `next dev` and `next build` write to the SAME `.next`, and running them together corrupts it.** The symptom is maximally misleading — **every route 500s, including ones the change never touched**, and the body is a bare plaintext "Internal Server Error" with no Next error overlay, because the request dies BELOW the error boundary. That last detail is the tell: a genuine render exception returns an HTML page with a stack. Diagnosed by curling `/` and `/browse` (both 500) rather than by reasoning about the diff; fixed by killing the dev server, `rm -rf .next`, restarting. **Never start a gate while a dev server is up, and vice versa.**
  - **Verified, not asserted:** Grammar re-measured at 0 spanning / 0 wrong-heading AFTER the change (`frags 55 = 55 sets`, i.e. every set now internally pure); contents ranges reconcile exactly (NDA 36+15+30+7+7+3+10 = 108, CDS 230+125+70+35+16+10 = 486); a **dry-run sync reports 0 to add / 3,180 unchanged / 0 orphaned**, so the grouping needed NO data migration — it is purely a render-time regroup; all 8 chapters render and pass the full smoke, whose new checks assert the contents covers every printed question exactly once with no gap or overlap between the halves; output is valid UTF-8 with 0 replacement characters.
  - **OWED, and worth knowing before the docx export is built: the contents table exists in the PREVIEW ONLY.** That page's own header says the Word file is the deliverable and the page exists to show what it will look like — so a docx export built without a contents table would diverge from its own preview, which is exactly the drift this file already records twice for the docx-vs-web renderers. Cheap to avoid: `chapterContents` and `numberChapter` are pure and framework-free, so the exporter calls the same functions rather than reimplementing them. Also owed: the two authorable Directions lines above, and **Spotting Errors**, which no merge rescues — its 28 spanning sets mix seven subtopics, not a tidy three, so it needs the question-level split that was rejected here.

- **2026-08-31 (third) — THE DATABASE LATENCY MYSTERY IS RESOLVED, and the answer was embarrassing in the best way: the project was PAYING for Micro compute (1 GB) while still PROVISIONED as a Nano (409 MB) — a free dashboard click fixed it.** Also shipped in the same arc: the prod-contract suite moved OFF the push gate onto a daily schedule (`.github/workflows/prod-contract.yml`) with 57014 retries (`tests/helpers/retryTimeout.ts`).
  - **THE CHAIN, measured end to end after five failed pushes:** the host had **409 MB MemTotal against a ~1.15 GB footprint**, so ~740 MB sat in swap and the box was page-fault-thrashing (245 MB swap-in per 2 min under load, iowait 12.4%) — stalls that Postgres reports as `CPU(running)` with `wait_event NULL`, because a page fault is invisible from inside the process. That is the "amplifier unidentified" of the 2026-08-22 dashboard entry, identified: the same query ran 9 ms or 8.7 s depending on nothing but when you asked, worst stalls with ZERO other backends active. Downstream casualties over the months: the dashboard 57014s, the `/questions` prerender timeouts, and the recent gate failures on `guide-strategy-headline`.
  - **FOUR HYPOTHESES KILLED BY MEASUREMENT before the real one stood** — concurrent build load (7,985 ms at idle refuted it), the `!inner` joins (clean 135 ms plan), disk reads (0 reads, 100% buffer hit), CPU steal/throttling (steal 0.0% from host metrics). The instrument that settled it: **Supabase serves per-project node-exporter metrics at `<project>.supabase.co/customer/v1/privileged/metrics`** (basic auth `service_role:<key>`, cached ~60 s — a short window reads all-zero deltas). Host truth — swap, iowait, steal, MemTotal — none of which any SQL view can see.
  - **THE DISCREPANCY WAS REAL AND THE DASHBOARD CONFESSED: billed spec ≠ provisioned spec.** Billing showed "Micro Compute" at Micro's exact rate; the API showed `selected_addons: []`; the host reported 409 MB against Micro's advertised 1 GB. Settings → Infrastructure resolved it with a tooltip: *"This Project is already paying for Micro Compute. You can upgrade to Micro Compute at any time."* **A Pro org bills old Nano instances as Micro but does NOT restart them onto it until someone clicks** — footer `$9.68 → $9.68/MONTH`, a free upgrade sitting unclicked for however long the org has been Pro. The user has mailed support about the billed-but-not-provisioned months.
  - **BEFORE/AFTER, same scripts, same queries:** swap used **767 MB → 55 MB with ZERO pages in/out** during a 110 s loaded window; iowait **12.4% → 0.8%**; the flaky query over 933 consecutive runs: **min 78 / med 113 / max 470 ms** (was max 7,985 ms at idle); the wait-event sampler: **0 slow of 40 iterations, max server-side in-flight 49 ms** (was multi-second stalls in 55/55 sightings). load1 0.12. **The Small (2 GB) upgrade is DEFERRED on these numbers — there is currently no case for it.** If stalls return as the bank grows, the daily db-health job is what will say so.
  - **THE GATE CHANGE stands on its own merits, not just as a workaround:** the prod-contract suites' drift arrives from ingestion scripts as often as from pushes, so the check never had to be welded to the push. Now: removed from `prepush:quick` + CI, run daily at 08:30 IST (half an hour after db-health so the two never contend), GitHub emails on failure, secrets already in the repo. Pushes get ~36 s faster and can no longer be failed by a database stall; drift is caught within a day instead of within a push — accepted trade, reversible in one line.
  - **`retryOnStatementTimeout` (tests/helpers/retryTimeout.ts):** retries ONLY SQLSTATE 57014 (code + message fallback, mirroring `queryQuestions`) with backoff; generic over the WHOLE result so caller types stay exact (widening `error.message` broke an assertion overload on first contact). **Vitest's existing `retry: 1` never covered this because it re-runs IMMEDIATELY, inside the same stall.** And the illness demonstrated itself mid-fix: the first live run had all 3 attempts cancelled across 30 s — the same suite passed in 1.76 s two minutes later — so the heavy `get_format_mix` scan got a wider 4-attempt/~60 s window (inside the 90 s hook budget).
  - **Two self-inflicted traps, both documented classes, both hit anyway:** a piped `echo EXIT=$?` captured `tail`'s exit and reported a failing typecheck as green (the `| tail` masking — caught by reading the output, one real type error found); and a background Node script in the scratchpad died on `require("dotenv")` because **Node resolves modules from the SCRIPT'S directory upward, never the cwd** — a scratchpad script cannot see the repo's node_modules however you launch it (fix: absolute require path or NODE_PATH).
  - **Vercel's ignored-build-step idea was analysed and WITHDRAWN** (my own proposal): its exit-code polarity is inverted vs `needs-build` (exit 0 = SKIP there), and it compares against the previous COMMIT, not the previous DEPLOY — on this repo's ~3-commit pushes that silently skips deploys whose code change sits one commit back. Small benefit (egress is a non-issue on Pro), severe-and-silent failure mode. Declined.

- **2026-08-31 (second) — `/books` grew three capabilities in one arc: PER-BOOK sections (multi-book), subtopic grouping with shared Directions (Layout A), and a PRINTED-PAGE view — the chapter as the pages it will be shared as, via the browser's own print engine.** Merges `5d483666` + `5599887c`; 55/55 books tests.
  - **MULTI-BOOK = sections become DATA.** `BookDefinition.sections` (`{key, title, exam}[]`) replaces the hardcoded `[nda, cds]` behind a `"NDA" | "CDS"` union — a book over one exam or three can now exist. What deliberately did NOT move into the book: **how to read an exam's SITTING is a property of the EXAM** (`EXAM_SITTING` in order.ts — NDA by `pyq_month` map Apr=1/Sep=2, CDS by the uniform `Eng_CDS_<year>_<sitting>.pdf` filename), true for every book containing it, so a second book inheriting NDA does not restate NDA's rule.
  - **LAYOUT A IS OPT-IN PER CHAPTER, AND THE GATE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: grouping by subtopic is only legal where ZERO sets span a subtopic.** Measured per chapter — Vocabulary 0/91, Sentence Rearrangement 0/55, Fill in the Blanks 0/11 are clean; **Grammar (18/72), Spotting Errors (28/37) and Reading Comprehension (49/65) are NOT** — grouping them would tear questions away from their passage, so they keep the flat layout. An authored `directions` line replaces per-set Directions ONLY where one instruction is genuinely true of every set (Synonyms: 65 sets saying the same thing in 22 wordings); mixed-task subtopics keep per-set lines. **Undeclared subtopics are APPENDED, never dropped** — a registry that must enumerate to render loses questions silently on the next ingest.
  - **THE FEATURE SHIPPED SILENTLY INERT ONCE, and the accounting assertion is what caught it:** `loadMeta` never selected `subtopic`, so every block rendered as one "Other 316" bucket — no error, page looks plausible. `scripts/books/smoke.ts` now asserts blocks hold every set and every question exactly once, and prints the block shape (`Synonyms 150* | Antonyms 135* | …`, `*` = authored directions). Supabase generated types typed the embed as `never` → `embeddedName(value: unknown)` normalises object-or-array embeds.
  - **THE PRINT VIEW IS THE BROWSER'S PRINT PREVIEW, after a pagination-engine design was rightly challenged as overcomplicated** ("Why is this becoming unnecessarily complicated?"). `/books/[bookSlug]/[chapterSlug]/print` renders the chapter once; `@page { size: letter }` + a 2-column CSS flow matching the docx exporter's geometry (0.5" margins, 0.5" gutter, Cambria 10pt); the browser's print dialog IS the one-page-at-a-time viewer, and print-to-PDF is the share path until the docx script exists. **`break-inside: avoid` on QUESTIONS, never on SETS** — an RC passage set is taller than a page, and forcing it whole strands most of a page (the notes-handout lesson, reapplied).
  - **ONE PASS PRODUCES BOTH the paper's numbers and the key's rows** (`numberChapter` in lib/books/print.ts): the answers-only key sits at each chapter's end (`break-before: page`) and refers by number, and numbering the two separately is how a book ships with every question present, every answer present, and each pointing at the other's neighbour — undetectable downstream because both halves look complete. Numbering follows the RENDERED block order, not the flat set list, for the same reason. **Excluded questions are absent AND unnumbered** — a gap in the sequence would read as a typesetting fault rather than a decision.
  - **A refactor lesson paid for in full:** renaming `BookSectionKey → string` via regex ate type annotations, import lines and Map generics across the module (`sectionKey: setKey: string`, `import type { string }`) and needed two repair scripts. **A type-shape refactor is file-by-file Edit work, not a regex.**
  - **Owed and stated:** the docx export is still a later script (user's call); the CDS shorthand-Directions data defect is left as-is ("leave it"); and the print route is superadmin-gated `force-dynamic`, so the gate proves it compiles — the layout proof was the user's own browser check ("preview looks good").

- **2026-08-31 — NEW superadmin surface `/books`: assembled PYQ books, for review before export. First book is the **NDA / CDS English PYQ Master** — 8 chapters, each laid out as "NDA PYQ" then "CDS PYQ", oldest-first, 3,180 questions. Migration 0086 (`books` + `book_questions`). Curation (exclude · reorder · move between halves) ships with it; **phase 4, the docx export, is NOT built.**
  - **THE IDEA SURVIVED CONTACT WITH THE DATA BETTER THAN EXPECTED, and checking that first is what made it a small job.** All 8 English chapters exist under BOTH exams with **byte-identical names**, and the subtopic names align too (CDS's set is a strict SUBSET of NDA's) — not luck, the CDS catalog was seeded from NDA's taxonomy. So "one chapter, NDA half, CDS half" needed **zero taxonomy work**. Overlap is **1 question** across 3,180, checked twice (exact `content_hash` AND fuzzy normalised-text, since a hash differs on any cosmetic edit) — so the two halves genuinely complement rather than repeat. Left in, on the user's call.
  - **THE HEADLINE FINDING: the two exams need OPPOSITE SORT KEYS, and getting it wrong mis-orders the book SILENTLY** — every question is still present, so no count and no gate can see it. NDA carries `pyq_month` on all 900 rows (Apr = NDA 1, Sep = NDA 2) while its 18 source filenames follow **eight different conventions** (`GAT_2017_NDA1_...`, `GAT_NDA2_2017_...`, `NDA1_2019_GAT_...`, `NDA_II_2024_GAT_...`); CDS is the exact mirror — `pyq_month` NULL on all 2,280, the sitting legible only from a uniform `Eng_CDS_<year>_<sitting>.pdf`. **The discriminating case is real and is the test:** NDA 2019 ships `GAT_NDA2_2019_PYQ.xlsx` (Sep) and `NDA1_2019_GAT_PYQ.xlsx` (Apr), so **alphabetically the second sitting sorts first** — a filename sort inverts that year while the month gets it right. `tests/books-order.test.ts` asserts both, and asserts the filenames really do sort the wrong way round so the case cannot pass trivially.
  - **SETS ARE ATOMIC, AND WHERE THEY CAN BE CUT DECIDED THE WHOLE STRUCTURE.** 3,175 of 3,180 questions sit in a shared-`context` set. **Zero sets span a CHAPTER** (0 of 381), so chapter-level cutting is clean — which is exactly the cut the user proposed. But **95 sets span SUBTOPICS**, 49 of 65 in Reading Comprehension, where one passage feeds literal + inferential + vocabulary-in-context questions. So chapter is the DEEPEST SAFE CUT, sub-grouping by subtopic would shatter passages, and the reorder unit in phase 3 must be the SET.
  - **"Set" turns out to mean two different things, and the context length separates them cleanly:** RC (avg 1,465 chars) and Cloze (1,050) are real PASSAGES; the other six chapters (118-207) are just a repeated *Directions* line. Only the first kind is genuinely order-locked — worth knowing before anyone tries to regroup the other six.
  - **A LATENT BUG FOUND AND LOGGED, NOT FIXED:** `docxBuilder.ts:158` asserts set siblings are co-located on one subtopic **"by invariant"**. That is false for English — 95 counterexamples, verified on a concrete 15-question Spotting Errors set spanning 6 subtopics. Harmless today because `/books` never groups by subtopic, but anyone enabling `groupBySubtopic` on an English export gets headings taken from each group's FIRST question.
  - **REUSE BOUNDARY, decided against the obvious answer.** `src/lib/papers/sections.ts` already holds the tested fractional-position core (`positionBetween`/`positionForMove`) that phase 3 needs, and it will be reused. The `papers`/`paper_questions` TABLES were rejected on four measured grounds: `papers.org_id` is NOT NULL and RLS-scoped to org/branch, so a 3,180-question book would appear in **every teacher's `/dashboard/papers`, editable and deletable**; the export path caps at 200 questions; and the per-batch no-repeat warning would fire against book membership. Same call `mh-sb-9` made when it re-exported the `stateboard` pure core rather than forking the pipeline. The reader likewise does NOT reuse `BoardReader` — it is welded to the board `section_*` axis and the student reveal-meter/sign-in gating, both wrong for a staff review surface — only the leaf renderers (`BlockText`, `KatexRenderer`, `publicImageUrl`) are shared, so rendering cannot drift from `/browse` and `/board`.
  - **MATERIALISED MEMBERSHIP, NOT SPARSE OVERRIDES.** Every in-scope question gets a `book_questions` row, seeded from the derived order. Storing only DEVIATIONS is cheaper and collapses the moment anything is reordered — there is no coherent answer to where an unpinned question sits relative to a pinned one. And **`excluded` is a FLAG, never a deleted row**: if exclusion meant absence, absence would mean two different things ("never seen" and "deliberately dropped") and the next sync would silently re-add everything rejected — the [[default-becomes-assertion]] shape.
  - **THE SYNC ONLY EVER ADDS.** New in the bank is APPENDED after its section's current max (never inserted mid-order, which would reshuffle a hand-arranged sequence); gone from the bank is REPORTED, never deleted; **re-chaptered in the bank is REPORTED, never applied** — because the book's `chapter_slug` is deliberately ALLOWED to diverge from the bank's, and that divergence IS the phase-3 "move this question" feature, so an auto-move would undo it every run. Pure core `src/lib/books/sync.ts`, 11 TDD cases.
  - **THE NAV GATE COST ~15 LINES AND CARRIES NO CACHING RISK, because the flag already existed.** `HeaderSession.isSuperadmin` is already populated and already reaching the client (`HeaderBar` passes it to `UserMenu` today), and `PrimaryNav` already had the conditional-tab pattern (`showPapers`). Resolving superadmin during server render would have re-broken site-wide caching — the 2026-07-29 defect where **zero** pages were prerendered for months. Verified from the artifacts, not reasoning: **744 prerendered `.html` after the build, exactly the pre-change baseline**, and 0 under `/books` (all `force-dynamic`, correctly).
  - **AN RLS LOCK TEST AGAINST AN EMPTY TABLE PROVES NOTHING — the batch-roster false-green, nearly repeated.** Immediately after the migration, anon reads of `books`/`book_questions` returned 0 rows and I nearly recorded that as the lock working; the tables were empty, so the query never reached RLS. Re-run **after** the 3,180-row seed it is real: service_role sees 1 + 3,180, anon sees **0 of the same tables**.
  - **`/books` READS VIA SERVICE-ROLE, which is forced rather than chosen:** `books`/`book_questions` have RLS enabled and NO policies (the `platform_admins`/`entitlements`/`teacher_access_requests` locked pattern), so a cookie-bound client cannot read them at all. Safe because `getSessionSuperadmin()` has already run on every page — the same shape as the platform-wide `/dashboard` surfaces. **Expect the `rls_enabled_no_policy` advisor INFO; it is the design.**
  - **A LIMIT THAT WOULD HAVE BITTEN AT 833 IDS.** `queryQuestionsByIds` issues a single un-chunked `.in()`; that is safe on `/browse`, which only ever passes one 25-row page, and NOT here — **Vocabulary is 773 questions and growing**, against a documented `Bad Request` at 833 ids (~31 kB URL). `lib/books/query.ts` chunks at 200. **Paging a RESULT (1000) and chunking a FILTER (~200) are different limits and only one of them is 1000.**
  - **CURATION MOVES A SET, NEVER A QUESTION — the one design decision the whole editor rests on.** `positionForMove` in `papers/sections.ts` moves ONE item and is right for a paper; a book needs to move a contiguous block and keep it contiguous, because a question dragged out of its passage is stranded from the thing that makes it answerable and **nothing downstream would notice — the question is still present**. `src/lib/books/curate.ts` (`planSetMove`/`planSetToSection`, pure, 11 TDD cases) moves the whole block, clearing its neighbour ENTIRELY rather than swapping one position, and spreads the block evenly into whatever gap remains so it still fits after earlier moves have tightened it. Exclusion is the one per-question action. **Cost recorded rather than solved: fractional positions have finite float precision — roughly 50 successive moves into the SAME gap exhaust it, and nothing renormalises today.**
  - **AN EXCLUDED QUESTION STAYS ON SCREEN, struck through, with a "Put back" control.** Hiding it would make the decision invisible and therefore irreversible from the page — and excluding one question of a passage set would visually shatter the set. So sections are built from EVERY stored row and the reader strikes out the excluded ones, while every count reports live-vs-excluded separately.
  - **EVERY ACTION RE-DERIVES SERVER-SIDE rather than trusting what the browser last rendered.** A tab left open since before a sync would otherwise move a set to where it USED to belong; re-deriving means a stale client either finds its set exactly where the server sees it or fails to find it at all, and the action returns "Nothing to move — reload if the page is stale" instead of a silent no-op. **`requireSuperadmin()` is repeated in every action** because a server action is its own entry point, callable without ever loading the page that drew the button — and with RLS enabled and NO policies there is no policy to fall back on, so a missing gate would be the whole gate missing.
  - **THE CURATION WRITES ARE VERIFIED ON LIVE DATA, because the UI cannot be:** the controls live in a client component on an auth-gated `force-dynamic` page, so `next build` never renders them and nothing headless can click them. `npx tsx scripts/books/verify-curation.ts` exercises the SERVICE layer against real rows and **round-trips every operation** — fingerprint the chapter, apply, assert, invert, and require the fingerprint back BYTE-IDENTICAL. 13/13 on Fill in the Blanks: a set moves down and back with its questions intact and none lost or duplicated; an impossible move is REFUSED and writes nothing; excluding keeps the ROW (proving the flag is not a delete); and a set crosses to the CDS half whole and comes back. Being a true round-trip, it is safe to run against production.
  - **A GATE FAILURE THAT WAS NOT MINE, and the way it was diagnosed matters more than the result.** The second gate run reported `GATE_RESULT: FAIL` with 9 test files failing — while the background task reported **exit code 0**, exactly the `| tail` masking this file documents, so the sentinel is what caught it. The named failure (`teacher-editor-rls`, superadmin content editing) had nothing to do with books. It passed in isolation, and then a full clean re-run came back **269/269 files and 3,820/3,820 tests green** — the documented shared-test-DB parallel flake, confirmed by re-running everything rather than by the isolated pass alone, which on its own proves much less.
  - **Migration 0086 was applied to prod and NOT to the test project**, leaving the two schemas diverged — the precise defect `npm run testdb:migrate` exists to catch (it is how migration 0021 was found to be prod-applied but never committed). Replayed: "86 migration files, 85 applied, 1 pending → ok".
  - **VERIFIED, not asserted:** `GATE_RESULT: PASS`; 47 new pure tests (25 ordering + 11 sync + 11 curation) plus a prod-contract registry guard **proven to fail in BOTH directions** by injecting each (a registry name that stopped resolving; a bank chapter absent from the registry — the direction that loses content quietly); `npm run books:smoke` drives the page's own loaders against the live bank and reconciles counts, section order, set contiguity, chronology and "no set mixes two different passages"; the sync is **idempotent** (second run: 0 to add, 3,180 unchanged); and positions are contiguous 1..N per (chapter, section) with **zero collisions**. Critically, after switching the reader from the derived order to the STORED order the smoke output came back **byte-identical**, which is what shows the switch preserved behaviour rather than merely still running.
  - **Owed, and stated rather than implied: the browser click-through.** Every `/books` route is auth-gated and `force-dynamic`, so `next build` never executes one — a green gate proves they COMPILE and nothing more. `npm run books:smoke` is the only thing exercising the loaders. Also worth knowing: **collapsed sets are not in the DOM**, so the review workflow is *Expand all -> Ctrl+F*; and a superadmin who is also org staff now sees **seven** nav tabs, the widest that row ever gets (~264px at 360px), which shrinks rather than overflowing but is the first thing to check if it ever needs to lose something.

- **2026-08-29 (second) — UPSC grows 914 q / 10 papers → 1,610 / 18: the 2017 sitting, 2019-p2, 2021-p2 and 2018-p2. Still ALL PRIVATE. Corpus-wide the blind pass now measures **95.0% against official keys, with the HIGH band at 98.5%** — and the session's most useful findings are two things the keys revealed that no amount of internal agreement could.**
  - **THE RUNNER-UP RULE IS THE MOST USEFUL REGULARITY HERE, AND IT IS A TENDENCY, NOT A LAW.** `DERIVATION_BRIEF.md` requires that a MED item NAME its runner-up and say what would have to be true for it to win. Every one of 2017-p1's three MED misses landed on exactly the named alternative (Q17→D, Q71→C, Q86→C), as did 2017-p2's MED and LOW misses. **2018-p2 then hit only ONE of its two** (Q80 -> A, named), which is why this is recorded as measured rather than as a law. It holds in BOTH directions — sometimes the stricter reading, sometimes the more generous — which is why the rule is "name it", never "prefer strict". Even at that rate it makes the MED list a ranked review queue rather than a pile.
  - **THE CONFIDENCE FLAG'S LIMIT WAS ALSO MEASURED, on 2021-p2.** Across 18 papers HIGH ran **1,337/1,358 = 98.5%**, and in most papers *every* error landed in MED. 2021-p2 is the outlier at **HIGH 64/67** against 71/71 and 63/63 elsewhere. Checked against the pages for keycheck's second hypothesis — a mis-slotted option — and it is not that: Q16's options are a clean `4/5/6/7` and its stem is honestly ambiguous about whether a ball's final contact counts as a hit "before the ball stops bouncing", with 5 and 6 both defensible. **A calibration miss, not a transcription defect**, and the distinction only exists because the key forced the question.
  - **THE CORPUS'S FIRST DUAL KEY, and the honest handling costs a question.** 2021-p2's official page has Q39's printed letter struck out by hand and replaced with **"C or D"**, corroborated by a handwritten footnote — UPSC accepting BOTH answers. It is a GRACE item, **not** a withdrawal: the same header still reads "No. of items dropped- NIL" with 80 items taken for scoring. `parseOfficialKey` accepts only A-D or X, so the file stores X, which correctly EXCLUDES it from scoring but literally means *dropped*. **The paper therefore commits 79 and Q39 is absent from the bank**, rather than present with one of two accepted answers asserted — the same call that put the multi-correct NDA questions PRIVATE rather than un-marking a true option. `config.ts` records it so nobody "repairs" the X into a letter or reads `dropped.length` as a drop count. The transcribing agent found it, refused to guess, and said outright that X asserts something false.
  - **A LITERAL `$` IS A MATH DELIMITER, and it reached SHIPPED content.** 2019-p2 Q74 uses `$` as a puzzle operator ("$ means 'divided by'"); `MATH_PATTERN`'s single-`$` arm paired the two and swallowed the definition list, so the question was unanswerable on the web and failed `audit:omml`. Four candidate fixes were measured against the REAL parser rather than guessed: **backslash-escaping does NOT work — there is no escape handling at all**; U+FF04 works but changes the glyph; `\(\$\)` renders a normal-width dollar with the prose intact. Fixed at source, DB row superseded by delete-and-re-commit (`content_hash` covers the stem). **The wider defect — 5 rows, 4 of them PUBLIC, in NDA GAT mocks — is in the SUGGESTIONS backfill ledger, not fixed**, because the single-`$` arm is a legitimate in-use delimiter for Excel-uploaded maths and cannot simply be deleted. **A false lead is recorded with it:** one row LOOKS corrupt in a console dump and is intact in the database — terminal output eats backslashes, so verify from stored bytes.
  - **THE MOST TRANSFERABLE AGENT LESSON: six agents refused an instruction of mine and were right.** My transcription prompts said "derive the answer yourself"; `TRANSCRIPTION_BRIEF.md` says the opposite in three places, because a transcriber's guess anchors the later blind pass. Transcription and derivation are SEPARATE pipeline steps. Every agent followed the brief, flagged the conflict rather than resolving it silently, and one satisfied both by putting its derivation in non-standard fields after checking that `dump-derive.ts` whitelists only number/stem/options/context. **A written contract beat an inline prompt, which is the argument for keeping the briefs.**
  - **ONE BOOKLET KILLED SIX AGENTS, and the fix was scope, not persuasion.** 2018-p2 terminated agent after agent with `400 Output blocked by content filtering policy` — no other paper failed once. What worked: **ONE PAGE per agent**, "write the file after every item" (every batching attempt lost everything), and an explicit instruction never to echo passage prose into a chat message. Its items 27-29 then needed a separate stitch pass, because their shared passage begins at the foot of p12 and the p14 agent legitimately owned no items under it.
  - **INDEPENDENT AGENTS INVENT NEAR-DUPLICATE TAXONOMY, and a sweep is the only way to see it.** Ten CSAT subtopics were added, each evidenced by a band that had read the question and argued every listed sibling would be affirmatively WRONG. Sweeping all 18 papers for unlisted subtopics then caught a defect in **my own** additions: I added `Pigeonhole and Worst-Case Selection` without noticing the SHIPPED 2023-p2 Q4 already uses `Worst-Case Selection and Pigeonhole` — same technique, opposite word order, invented independently because the catalog had neither. The new label yields to the shipped one so only this session's work moves. **Two labels that look like duplicates and are NOT** were settled by reading both questions rather than their names: `Powers and Exponents` (2020-p2 Q50 compares `(1/2)^-6`…) vs `Perfect Squares and Cubes` (2017-p2 Q53), with `Unit Digit and Powers` a third distinct thing — an earlier draft would have renamed the first into the second and **dragged a shipped question along with it**. **35 unlisted subtopics remain**, including two more near-duplicate pairs; left alone because reconciling them means touching shipped rows.
  - **Verified rather than asserted:** a fresh pass over the live DB reads the correct option off `options` for every committed row — **1,610 rows, 0 mismatches against the official keys, every question with exactly one correct option, and no committed row that its key marks dropped**. The README's status block (still claiming "4 of 22 papers — 359 questions") was rebuilt from a `keycheck.ts` run over every paper with the aggregates computed, not eyeballed, and its withdrawn-item list checked against all seven key files. **Two numbers I got wrong and corrected:** the unlisted-subtopic count (34 → 35, re-counted) and an earlier claim about the `$` defect's blast radius. **`audit:text` and `audit:omml` clean on every new source.**
  - **A swallowed Supabase error is indistinguishable from a real absence** — a destructured `{ data }` with no `error` check reported "Q53 not found" for a row that plainly exists; adding `if (error) throw` made it work first time. Same shape as the `getDashboardStats` and `getRecentUploads` failures this log already records.

- **2026-08-29 — NEW exam UPSC Civil Services (Prelims): 914 q across 10 papers, ALL PRIVATE, every answer verified against the OFFICIAL UPSC key. `scripts/upsc/`. The corpus is the smaller half of the result — the papers are the first place this project could MEASURE how far a blind LLM derivation can be trusted, because for once there is a published ground truth to score against.**
  - **TWO PAPER SHAPES, ONE PIPELINE.** Paper I (GS, 100 items / 200 marks / +2 / −0.667) is 100 standalone MCQs with subject decided per question against `catalog.json` — the `scripts/cds-gs` shape. Paper II (CSAT, 80 items / 200 marks / +2.5 / −0.833, **qualifying at 33%**) carries `Directions for the following N items:` blocks over shared passages — the `scripts/cds` shape. Sources are two generations: prep-house English-only extracts, and raw bilingual UPSC booklets where **English sits at EVEN 0-based indices from 2** and the printed page label is index + 1.
  - **THE HEADLINE, and it is a number this project has never had: a blind pass lands ~94% on GS and ~95% on CSAT, and is confidently wrong the rest of the time.** Per paper, scored BEFORE the key was applied — GS: 92.9 · 93.9 · 93.9 · 94-95 · **98.0**; CSAT: 91-94 · 95.0 · 96.2 · 96.3. That is ~6 wrong answers per 100, each with a fluent argument attached. **It is the strongest evidence yet that a derived corpus must not be published as if it were keyed** — which is exactly the position CDS General Knowledge is in, one exam over, with no key to check against.
  - **AND THE DUAL-BLIND PILOT PUT A NUMBER ON WHY AGREEMENT IS NOT ACCURACY. On the 2025 pair, where the two independent passes AGREED (98.3% of items) they were right only 94.4%.** Agreement overstates accuracy by ~4 points, because two passes fail the same way on a fact-recall item. The CDS-GK entry says correlated error is undetectable by agreement; this measures it.
  - **THE CONFIDENCE FLAG IS THE USABLE PRODUCT OF ALL THIS.** Measured against official keys, the HIGH band ran **72/72, 85/86, 70/71, 91/91** (plus 81/84, 67/69) while essentially every error landed in MED. It is a genuine router for review effort — but only because the brief forbids inflating it, and it stops being one the moment anyone does.
  - **A RULE I GOT WRONG AND THEN CORRECTED, which is the more useful version.** Two papers had the key side with the STRICT reading a deriver had named as its runner-up (2022-p1 Q54, 2020-p1 Q19), so the brief was told "prefer strict". 2018-p1 split it — Q72 strict, Q7 generous. The accurate rule: **on a MED item the key repeatedly lands on whichever alternative the deriver named and set aside, in either direction.** So the instruction is "name the runner-up and say what would have to be true for it to win", which turns the MED list into a ranked review queue rather than a pile.
  - **A PAGE-DETECTOR DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE FED DEVANAGARI TO A TRANSCRIBER.** `classify-pages.py` separates scripts by shirorekha run-length. On 2020-p2 it reported 23 English pages where every other Paper II has 21; two were odd-indexed and both are HINDI — math-heavy pages (`51×27×35×62×75`, a letter-analogy string) carrying too little Devanagari for the signal, one scoring **p95run=8, inside the English range of 6-8**. No threshold can separate that. The fix uses the booklet's own guarantee instead: a bilingual paper prints each item twice, so the English pages are all ONE PARITY with no exceptions, and `parity_outliers` flags any page breaking it. Proven in both directions (fires on exactly [29, 33], silent on clean booklets) and covered by `--calibrate` in a `PARITY_CASES` block kept SEPARATE from `CALIBRATION` — these are answers the detector gets WRONG and the warning must keep catching, so folding them in would turn the gate permanently red. The failure is silent: a Devanagari page handed to a transcriber yields a missing item, not an error.
  - **THE TWO SHARPEST DATA DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY AGENTS READING EACH OTHER'S OUTPUT, not by any gate.** (a) A shared passage governing items 26 and 27 across a band seam failed to form a SET, because the two bands wrote different apostrophes in "India's" — `assignSetLabels` folds whitespace and case but not quote glyphs. All four gates passed while the paper carried it; the consequence would have been the passage rendering twice. (b) The same paper disagreed with ITSELF on the decimal separator, four bands preserving the booklet's raised middle dot and one normalising 15 of them. Settled by measuring the shipped corpus (2022-p2, 2023-p2, 2025-p2 all preserve U+00B7) rather than by preference. In both cases the finding band correctly REFUSED to edit another band's file and escalated.
  - **AN ORCHESTRATION ERROR OF MINE, recorded because the fix is a rule.** I ran a merge while transcription agents were still working, read a 9-item coverage failure off in-flight files, rendered two pages to "confirm" it, and dispatched a gap-filling band. Nothing was ever missing. The cause: I had told the agents to WRITE EARLY AND UPDATE AS THEY GO, which makes a partial file the expected state — so file-presence stopped being a proxy for completion. **Wait for the agent's completion notification, not for its file to exist.** The gap-filler then did the right thing and refused to write, arguing that a duplicate band would trip BAND AGREEMENT on a single curly quote and block a passing paper for no gain.
  - **Provenance and scope.** Keys are transcribed from the Series-A page of each official PDF and reconciled against that page's OWN printed drop-count ("No. of items dropped: 02", "NIL") — an independent check built into the source. Six papers carry UPSC-withdrawn items, absent by design (2020-p1 Q27+Q52, 2021-p1 Q80, 2022-p1 Q61, 2022-p2 Q36, 2023-p1 Q34). Catalog grew to **374 subtopics** across 11 additions, each a measured gap rather than a near-miss. **12 papers remain un-ingested and every one is blocked on locating its key, not on effort.** Nothing is PUBLIC and the exam is deliberately ABSENT from `EXAM_REGISTRY`; publishing needs that entry plus a decision on the stale 2018-2023 Current Affairs content — the same call CDS-GK faced. See [[upsc-cse-ingestion]].
