- **2026-08-28 (third) — THE MH STATE BOARD CLASS-10 TEXTBOOK LAYER IS COMPLETE: 51 chapters in ONE run of 30 parallel full-pipeline agents, taking it 374 → 1,766 q PUBLIC across all 7 subjects and the exam to 3,286. Zero rows lack a solution, a section or taxonomy. The transferable findings are about running 30 agents at once, and most of them are defects in MY OWN scaffolding that the agents found.**
  - **THE SHAPE: one agent, one chapter, end to end** — transcribe from page images, commit, author, apply, audit, section, publish — against a written contract (`AGENT_BRIEF.md`) rather than an inline prompt repeated 30 times. Each dispatch added only what was specific to its chapter. Concurrency capped at 20, so the run went in waves. **Not one agent auto-created a chapter or a subtopic** across ~1,700 rows, which is the result that matters most: `commitStaged` auto-creates both, so a near-miss on a name (a space before a colon, "&" for "and") silently splits a corpus in two with no error. Verified by a cross-agent check none of them could run for itself.
  - **FOUR DEFECTS IN MY OWN SCAFFOLDING, EVERY ONE FOUND BY AN AGENT, and the pattern is that each was found by an agent looking at territory it did not own.** (1) **The printed-answer census was short by 15.** I told four chapters they had no printed answers; the real count is 24 across six chapters, not nine across two. Being case-SENSITIVE was right — a case-insensitive scan matches "org**ans.**" — but the pattern was rigid where the book is not: four chapters print `Ans :` with a space and Heat spells it `Answer :`. The cost landed precisely on the chapters it silenced, two of them numerical. Two agents found it independently, and **each of their own re-counts was ALSO short** (19 and 24, missing respectively the `Answer` spelling and a trailing period) — a census of a typeset feature is only as good as the variants you thought to allow for. (2) **The brief's `options` schema was wrong** (plain strings; the real type is `{label,text}` with labels forced to A–D) — found by the HEAT agent, which had no MCQs at all and reported it anyway. (3) **A page range short by one**, and the missing page held **17 of that chapter's 23 questions**; the agent rendered the extra page rather than concluding the chapter had six. (4) **I wrote a new brief without checking that FOUR already existed in the same directory**; mine contradicted the older `MATHS_TRANSCRIPTION_BRIEF.md` on ref style and split the twelve Maths chapters six-and-six. Three agents flagged it.
  - **THE PROVENANCE GAP, and it is the one that mattered most.** ~940 PUBLIC rows said nothing about where their answers came from: `derived_model` NULL, `pyq_note` naming only the book. These books print almost no key, so nearly every answer is authored — and a published derived answer that does not announce itself reads as an official key. **Exactly the CDS General Knowledge failure**, where it was caught at the publish gate, one step too late. Fixed at the cause first: `apply-solutions.ts` stamps as it writes, `flip-public.ts` REFUSES to publish an authored answer without the stamp, and `backfill-provenance.ts` covered the 852 already applied. **The seam is exact and needs no bucket logic** — a Maths chapter's solved examples carry the BOOK's own printed solution, arrive at commit time from the questions file, and never pass through `apply-solutions`, so they are correctly left unclaimed. Verified after: every remaining unstamped PUBLIC row is a `solved_example`. **I shipped the fix out of step first** — the columns stamped and the sentence missing, leaving 355 rows half-labelled — so both halves now live as one shared constant and helper in `config.ts`. And the gate was **proven to go red** by clearing one row's stamp, not assumed.
  - **A RENDER DEFECT NO GATE COULD SEE: 68 shipped answers printed literal asterisks.** Single-asterisk `*italics*` are not emphasis to this renderer — the solution path is `BlockText → KatexRenderer → parseRichSegments → splitBold`, and `splitBold` splits on `**` only — so `*Homo sapiens*` reached students with the asterisks visible. Delimiters balance, `audit:text` checks other classes, and `audit:omml` covers the WORD path rather than the web one. Found by the Cell Biology agent in its OWN file, then reported as a risk to its siblings. All 65 distinct spans were read before repairing: every one is a scientific name or an emphasised word, none a literal asterisk that should survive. Converted to bold — the only emphasis this renderer has — with each row's `content_hash` compared before and after.
  - **TWO PROBE BUGS, both proved with a control rather than asserted.** `audit-grounding` stripped possessives from the CANDIDATE but not from the chapter haystack, so any multi-word name whose printed form carries one was permanently unmatchable ("Let's Discuss" → "Let Discuss", never found); the Environment agent demonstrated it with a matched pair. And the same probe read `\Rightarrow` inside a math zone as an ungrounded proper noun. Both fixed and **diffed across every chapter to prove the fix is strictly noise-reducing** — 12 and 6 candidates silenced, 0 new in each case.
  - **`merge.ts` FAILS OPEN BY NAME, so it gained a fail-CLOSED shape guard.** Its auto-glob was swallowing `data/<id>.sections.json` — the per-chapter `/board` outline convention introduced this run for the twelve Maths chapters. Adding the suffix would have been the obvious fix and the wrong one alone: **a denylist goes stale by construction**, and this run alone produced `.solution-images.json`, `.solutions-by-ref.json` and `.mcq-blind-derivation.json`, none of which any list would have known. It now also refuses a fragment whose rows lack a string `ref`/`bucket`/`stem` — proven to refuse all three artifacts and pass three real transcription bands.
  - **THE AGENTS' BEST WORK WAS REFUSING TO ANSWER, and it recurred in every subject.** Where a chapter asks what it never states, the answer says so: Life Processes 2 asks for male reproductive hormones while naming only four, all in the female section, and asks for family-planning methods while its own box sends students to interview a health officer; Environmental Management asks for biodiversity hotspots and **names not one**; Animal Classification's Q8 row 1 has no germ layer assigned to Porifera anywhere, and the agent declined to supply the standard textbook answer; Disaster Management's nine pictograms are never explained, and the agent read each from the drawing rather than naming them with GHS terms. **Not one supplied a plausible external fact to fill a gap.**
  - **BOOK DEFECTS: roughly 60 across the run, and the sharpest are self-refuting.** Probability's key gives three exhaustive outcomes summing to **11/9**. Heat's Q9(b) prints 586.4 g where the question's own data require 586.51 — its value back-multiplies to 37.6 cal short of what it specifies. Mensuration prints a pair of answers that **cannot come from one value of π**. Similarity's componendo step evaluates to 5/2 and the next blank prints 5/3. Circle keys "two common tangents" to externally-touching circles while **its own two figures draw three**. Periodic Classification prints `A1` and `C1` — capital letter, digit one — for aluminium and chlorine, and **contradicts itself in a single line**, printing both `₁₇Cl` and `₁₇C1`. Against that, Quadratic Equations diffed **108 rows with zero errors on either side** and Linear Equations 65 with none — this publisher's keys are not uniformly dirty.
  - **THE BOARD REUSES THIS TEXTBOOK VERBATIM — measured, not suspected.** Three chapters had a question dedup against an existing board PYQ with a byte-identical stem, and in two cases the board's own key then independently confirmed an answer we had derived. That is the strongest evidence available that the textbook layer is worth having beside the PYQ layer.
  - **THE FAILURE MODE THAT RECURRED MOST WAS A PROBE, NOT DATA.** Nearly every agent hit a false finding in its own verification: `LIKE` in Postgres treats `\` as its escape character, so a check for a literal `\n` matches the letter *n* (five agents, independently); a heredoc ate the backslashes in a LaTeX probe so it tested strings containing no math at all and passed trivially; a probe asserted `section_seq` should be contiguous 1..N when it is the BLOCK ordinal (six agents). In every case the probe was wrong and the data was fine. Several agents ended up building a deliberately-failing control before trusting a green result, which is the right habit and is now the house expectation.
  - **A CROSS-AGENT HAZARD I CAUSED: `git add` on the data directory while 30 agents were writing into it.** Unstaged and committed by explicit path instead. Also `tsconfig` now excludes `scripts/**/out` — those are pipeline OUTPUT dirs, gitignored, but `tsc` reads from disk regardless, so one agent's half-finished scratch file turned the prepush gate red for everyone else mid-run.
  - **CLEAN-UP, approved off a 360 and the 360 changed the work.** 445 rows normalised onto one ref style, and three near-duplicate subtopics merged (two articles and a plural, one PYQ row each; blast radius re-measured at write time: 0 papers, 0 attempts, 0 tags). **Two candidates were DECLINED on measurement.** `Construction of Circumcircle` vs `Construction of Incircle and Circumcircle` is a narrower name against a broader one, not a spelling variant. And the "configured subtopics that receive no textbook rows" turned out not to be drift at all: **ZERO subtopics under this exam are empty** — every one holds live board-PYQ rows, legitimate filing for content past papers asked and the current edition dropped. My own ledger entry had framed them as duplication; merging them would have destroyed real filing to tidy a list.
  - Verified at close: 1,766/1,766 PUBLIC · 0 without a solution, a `section_seq`, a chapter or a subtopic · 0 near-duplicate chapters · 0 agent-created subtopics · all 13 Maths chapters on one ref style · `audit:text` clean on all five classes · `audit:omml` 0 failing zones over 1,766 · `audit:keys` 153 MCQs scanned, 0 flagged · `board:lint` green over 9,519 rows. **Owed and stated rather than implied: a browser click-through** (`/browse` reveals answers on click, so nothing headless proves the reveal lays out, and that now includes a great many GFM tables), and **an independent blind re-derivation of every MCQ key** — each chapter keyed at transcription time, and every `mcq-verify.json` says so rather than claiming a blind pass it did not earn. `mark-mcq-verify.ts` was deliberately never run, so no false `blind_rederivation` row entered `question_reviews`. See [[mh-ssc-10-ingestion]].

- **2026-08-28 (second) — BATCH ROSTERS: a batch stops being a name and gains actual students. Migrations 0083-0085 + two ways in (invite by email, or a class join code). This is the first time a teacher can see how their own students are doing.**
  - **THE PROBLEM WAS NOT PERMISSIONS, IT WAS THAT THE SET DID NOT EXIST.** The question that opened this was "can a teacher or admin add students?" — and the answer was nobody can, structurally: the `role` enum holds only ADMIN and TEACHER, `createMember` is hard-typed to those two, `student_profiles` is own-row for every verb, and `/dashboard/students` is a superadmin-only READ. A student is defined by the ABSENCE of an `org_members` row. So **"this org's students" is not a queryable set**, and a staff-facing student PICKER is impossible — it would list every student on the platform, other institutes' included. Enrollment therefore cannot start from a directory. **The roster is the OUTPUT of enrollment, not its input.**
  - **ENROLLMENT IS NOT MEMBERSHIP, and that is what keeps the security model intact.** No `org_members` row is written; the student stays org-less and nothing changes about what they can see or do. `batch_enrollments` is a ONE-WAY visibility grant — staff may read that student's mock results — and being per-batch rather than per-org, a student can legitimately be enrolled at two institutes.
  - **NO INSERT POLICY ON `batch_enrollments`, deliberately.** Joining is authorized by something only the server can verify (a pending invite addressed to your own verified email, or a valid join code). RLS cannot express either, so an INSERT policy of `user_id = auth.uid()` would let any student enrol into any batch id they obtained and skip the check entirely. Writes are service-role behind a grant check — the `entitlements`/`platform_admins` locked pattern.
  - **THE FIRST RLS TEST WAS A FALSE GREEN, AND FINDING THAT IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE PART.** "A student cannot enrol themselves" passed — *and still passed with a deliberate `user_id = auth.uid()` INSERT policy added to the test database*. Cause: the fixture already enrolled that student in that batch, so the insert died on the PRIMARY KEY and the assertion never reached RLS. It was asserting a constraint while claiming to assert the security boundary. Now it targets an empty batch and **asserts the row does not exist**, which no constraint can fake. Every negative test in this feature was then proven to go red — the invite email-match check too. **A check that has never gone red proves nothing**, and "an error came back" is not the same as "the policy stopped it".
  - **INVITE + ACCEPT IS THE INDUSTRY SHAPE, and Google Classroom ships exactly this pair** (email invite AND class code) — as do Canvas, GitHub orgs and Slack. The accept step is not ceremony: enrollment exposes a person's exam performance, so consent has to come from them, not from whoever typed the address. The two mechanisms fail in **opposite directions** and cover each other — an invite needs an accurate address and reaches a stranger on a typo; a code needs no addresses but depends on the student acting.
  - **KEYED ON EMAIL, NOT user_id, so an invite works for someone with no account yet — and there is NO binding step at signup.** `/account` resolves pending invites by the caller's verified email on read: stateless, no signup hook, no pending-row migration. **That is only safe because email is verified, which was MEASURED (156/156 accounts have `email_confirmed_at`) and is recorded in the migration header** — if signup confirmation is ever disabled, this table's security model breaks.
  - **THE ONE SECURITY CHECK ON ACCEPT is that the invite names the caller's own verified email.** Invite ids travel in payloads and are NOT secrets; without that check, holding an id is enough to enrol someone else. The route takes the email from the SESSION, never the body.
  - **NEVER REVEALS WHETHER AN ADDRESS HAS AN ACCOUNT.** The invite row is written either way and the counts returned are identical, so a teacher cannot use the box to probe who is registered. `joinByCode` deliberately breaks the other way — `closed` is distinguished from `invalid_code`, conceding that a valid-but-closed code exists, because over a 1.1e12 space behind a rate-limited endpoint the leak is negligible and a student in a classroom needs to know whether they mistyped it or should ask the teacher.
  - **A DELIBERATE BRAND EXCEPTION, documented at the template.** The invite email names the tenant org, which is otherwise a staff-gated string a student never sees. **Consent that cannot name the party asking is not consent.** PYQ Vault stays the sender brand; the org is named as the inviter. The mail is thin on purpose — institute, batch, nothing else, plus an explicit ignore path — because a mistyped address reaches a stranger.
  - **JOIN CODES USE CROCKFORD BASE32** (no I, L, O, U). Excluding those is what makes the normaliser's confusable mapping a REPAIR rather than a guess: O can never legitimately appear, so a typed O is unambiguously 0. 8 chars over 32 symbols ≈ 1.1e12, rate-limited at 10 attempts/hour. Wrong length returns null rather than padding — "you mistyped it" and "that class does not exist" send the student to their teacher with different questions. A DB CHECK mirrors the generator's contract so a malformed code fails at write rather than becoming a code that prints but can never be typed; **proven to reject lowercase, excluded letters and short codes before use**. `join_open` is separate from `archived` because closing the door is not the same as ending the course.
  - **RLS IS THE BOUNDARY, NOT THE ROUTE GUARD.** `requireEditor` proves the caller is org staff, never that they may touch THIS batch — the per-batch scope check reads through the CALLER's own client so `batches_select_scoped` (0057) does the work, and the roster reads enrollments and attempts the same way. Service-role hydrates names ONLY for ids that already passed RLS (the `listMembers` pattern). Reading the roster with service-role and filtering by hand would make a route-guard bug a cross-org leak.
  - **The `mock_attempts` grant is ADDITIVE** (permissive/OR'd), so student own-row access cannot narrow — asserted by test. It leads with a `current_user_org_id() IS NOT NULL` guard because that is NULL for every student, i.e. the majority read path exits before touching a table; this project has already had an RLS predicate turn a hot read into a seq scan (0082). Scope is the student's ENTIRE attempt history, not just post-join: the institute wants the baseline, and access ends the moment the enrollment row goes.
  - **A latent 1000-row bug caught in self-review, in its auth-API form.** Two `listUsers({ perPage: 1000 })` calls hydrated across ALL accounts un-paged — the same silent-truncation shape as the PostgREST cap this project has hit five times. Past 1000 accounts the roster would render students as "(unknown)" and re-invite people already enrolled. `members/admin` gets away with one page because it hydrates 7 staff; these grow with every signup. Now paged, like `listStudents`.
  - Verified: `GATE_RESULT: PASS`, 744 prerendered `.html` (nothing de-cached), 52 new tests across 5 files. **Owed and NOT provable headlessly: the browser click-through** — `/account` and the roster are auth-gated `f` pages, so the gate proves they compile, never that they lay out. See [[batch-roster]].

- **2026-08-28 — CDS GENERAL KNOWLEDGE COMPLETE AND PUBLISHED: 19 papers / 2,280 q, built with NO answer key anywhere. CDS 2,280 → 4,560; the bank reaches 61,863. Five catalog rounds, and the durable finding is that four of the five were ONE rule violated in different places.**
  - **THE EVIDENCE BASE IS THE WEAKEST IN THIS BANK AND THE DESIGN FOLLOWS FROM THAT.** No key exists — not in the booklets, not on disk, no external anchor (measured twice: 5 distinctive stems → 0 matches in the 4,086-q NDA GK bank, and a cross-paper sweep over 720 questions found **exactly one genuine repeat**, which then passed as a free control — four agents on two papers all answered it identically at HIGH from different distractor sets). So every answer is two INDEPENDENT blind derivations plus hand adjudication. **99.2% mean, 7 papers at 100%, HIGH 1798/1798.** That last number is the useful one: **every disagreement across nineteen sittings landed in MED or LOW**, so confidence is a reliable router for review effort. It is also the number most likely to be over-read — agreement bounds DISAGREEMENT risk, not CORRELATED error, and no amount of it detects two passes wrong the same way.
  - **PROVENANCE WAS MISSING AND FOUND AT THE PUBLISH GATE, WHICH IS TOO LATE BY ONE STEP.** The rows carried a `pyq_note` naming only the paper and `derived_model` NULL on all 2,280. Published in that state a derived answer is indistinguishable from an official key — the one thing this corpus must not imply, and the thing every sibling key-less corpus here already stamps (`mh-sb-9`, `mh-ssc-10`). Now stamped on all 2,280 with a clause saying no key is published, the answer came from two blind passes, and disagreements were adjudicated against the page. **The rule earned: for a key-less corpus, provenance is part of COMMIT, not of publish** — `flip-public.ts` writes it before visibility so a row can never be publicly readable without it.
  - **THE CATALOG RULE, discovered by violating it four times.** Round 2 added a subtopic to ONE period chapter of History and stranded content in another, twice; the rule written then was that a subtopic which is not period-specific belongs in EVERY period chapter it can occur in. It generalises past History and the catalog broke it three more ways: **scientist attribution existed in Physics and nowhere else** (Biology had only the topic-specific `Antibiotics — Discovery`, Chemistry nothing, so both absorbed "who discovered X" into CONTENT subtopics — the exact mechanism that formed the awards catch-all); **economic geography existed for India and not the world**, and because `chapter` is hard-validated a world-scope question cannot be parked on the Indian chapter, so a MINING question was filed under POLITICAL geography because its options were country names; and the **Delhi Sultanate had no dynastic slot** beside the Mughals and Vijayanagara. **Round 3 then applied its own rule too narrowly** — it added the scientist slot only to the subjects that already had hits, and Geography produced one within a paper. The refinement: **when a rule NAMES its targets ("every science subject"), apply it to all of them; when it does not ("world equivalents of Indian economic geography"), add only what is evidenced.** An unused subtopic is a filter nobody clicks; a missing one puts a question under the wrong SUBJECT, which no `/browse` control recovers.
  - **AN ADDITION AND A RENAME HAVE DIFFERENT ECONOMICS, and round 2's blanket "sooner is cheaper" is only half right.** It holds for an ADDITION, whose value is preventing FUTURE mis-filing — every paper transcribed before it lands had to park content somewhere approximate. It does NOT hold for a RENAME or re-file, which only corrects filing that already happened: that cost is per-QUESTION, not per-paper, so it is identical whenever paid and can wait for one pass against a settled corpus. Hence rounds 3-5 shipped mid-run and the awards rename waited for paper 19.
  - **THE AWARDS SPLIT, and the cheaper answer that measuring produced.** `Civilian Awards, Honours and Educational Institutions` held 18 rows doing two jobs — 14 awards, **3 pure institution-identification rows that never mention an award**, 1 event. The banked note had proposed splitting by award TYPE; reading all 18 showed the axis is awards-vs-institutions and that `National Institutions, Milestones and History` **already existed**. Done as a RENAME plus 3 moves rather than 18 re-files, because a question points at a `subtopic_id` and renaming that one row renames it for every question at once. **NDA carries a subtopic of the IDENTICAL NAME with 13 rows** (this catalog was generated from NDA's taxonomy) — verified separate, deliberately untouched as shipped published content, and the two exams now diverge on that name by design.
  - **MEASUREMENT SHRANK EVERY GAP IT TOUCHED, in both directions.** The Delhi Sultanate looked urgent at 9 affected questions and is 3 — `sultan` matches inside **conSULTANt** and **reSULTANt**, and separately matched **Sultan*pur* National Park**. The "cluster outside the subject structure" was 13 hits and is 5: two false positives (the Deccan Riots and the Hathigumpha inscription both matched on *confederacy* and are Indian history), and three of four "medieval Islamic" hits are Al-Biruni and Ibn Battuta under `Medieval Travellers`, which is correct since they are sources FOR Indian history. **Macro theory was never a scope question at all — all six rows were already under Economics.** The same probe also UNDER-counted chemistry, missing a Gibbs row because the pattern read `spontaneit` and the stem says *spontaneous*. Both directions of probe error in one round; the fix is reading each hit, not a better regex.
  - **WHAT WAS DECLINED, and why the numbers justify it:** sociology 2 q, 19th-century world history 2 q, medieval Islamic 1 q — **five questions across nineteen papers, ~0.26/paper**, most already defensibly filed. No new chapters. Chemistry genuinely has **no thermodynamics chapter** and its 2 rows were **the only questions in the corpus under the wrong SUBJECT** (filed in Physics, unreachable by a Chemistry filter) — fixed as a subtopic, because 0.11/paper does not earn a chapter. Kansas-Nebraska and Al-Khwarizmi were checked for a better existing home and have none, so they stay put rather than justify structure alone.
  - **THE TRANSCRIPTION HAZARD THAT NO DOWNSTREAM CHECK CATCHES is code-option ORDER**, and it is inconsistent WITHIN a single booklet: one paper used SIX layouts, putting the all-three row at (a) in one question and (d) in another; several papers OMIT rows the statement set implies (a four-statement question with no all-four row); one printed two Match Lists whose rows were identical but for an (a)/(b) swap; another reused ONE permutation pool across four Match Lists in four different orders. A Directions block can also govern several consecutive items — seen covering three, four and five — and once covered an item **continuing OVERLEAF with no options printed on its own page**. Every code row is read off the page at high zoom, never inferred.
  - **FIGURE DESCRIPTIONS CAN PRESERVE ANSWERABILITY WITHOUT LEAKING THE ANSWER — proven, not assumed.** 2017-2 carries two map questions whose List-II has no text at all. The transcriber described each by GEOMETRY AND ADJACENCY ONLY, never naming what a numeral marked, and both blind passes independently resolved both maps and landed on the same printed code row.
  - **AGENT-RUN LESSONS, each earned by a failure:** "write early" is too weak — an agent finished a whole band, batched every check, died on the last step and lost all of it, so the rule is now **write after every PAGE**; the shared scratchpad needs per-band namespacing after two agents both created `merge_2019_1.py` and one silently overwrote the other; and **page parity is per-reprint, not universal** — 2016-2 prints EVEN page numbers where every other booklet prints odd, so the mapping is derived from the first page read rather than assumed.

- **2026-08-26 (second) — the 16 `audit:keys` flags on the NDA practice bank resolved: NOT ONE was a wrong answer. 11 are genuine MULTIPLE-CORRECT questions in a bank that models exactly one correct option, 3 are probe false positives, and both duplicate-option rows are the BOOK's own duplicates. 12 rows withdrawn to PRIVATE, 4 solutions reworded, and a different defect class surfaced in the CBSE corpus.**
  - **THE FINDING THAT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS READING: on all 11 rows with two options marked correct, the second mark was NOT spurious.** The tempting pattern — the printed key is the alphabetically-first of the two marked, in all 11 — reads as "an extra `is_correct` leaked in, drop it". Solving each one says otherwise: **every second option is genuinely TRUE.** `Q656`'s `det(adj P) = 4` gives `det(P) = ±2`, so −2 AND 2 are both possible; `Q820`'s two options are the two ORDERINGS of the same `{3/5, 4/5}` solution; `Q1498`'s `|t+2| = 1` yields both printed points; `Q734`'s feasible `P(A∩B) ∈ [0.3, 0.6]` makes both 0.65 and 0.28 necessarily false. And the stems say so out loud — *"which of the following **is/are** true"*, *"the possible **value(s)** ... **is (are)**"*, *"**statement(s)** is/are"*. These are **JEE-Advanced-style multiple-correct items reprinted in an NDA practice booklet**, and the transcription was right; the printed answer key simply cannot carry two letters.
  - **So the defect is in the MODEL, not the data — and that decided the remedy.** `question_format` has members `mcq | subjective | numeric` and no multi-correct, and the single-answer repair available is to un-mark one TRUE option. That would mark a student wrong for giving a correct answer — **the exact harm fixed on Q34 earlier the same day**. Withdrawn to PRIVATE instead: visibility only, so ids, text, options, solutions and paper references all survive, and it reverses with one `UPDATE`. Checked before acting: none is in a mock, none carries a concept or principle tag, none has a student answer, and the single row in a teacher paper (`Q734`, paper "Probability") still builds because org members can read their own org's PRIVATE rows.
  - **3 of the 16 were PROBE FALSE POSITIVES, and the probe was right to be suspicious.** Each solution already carried an adjudicated `[Textbook note: the source book keys option D …]` bracket recording a BOOK error we had overridden — and `audit-keys` reads that letter as the solution's own conclusion. Our keys are correct (re-derived: `1+ab>0` on ℤ is reflexive and symmetric but **not** transitive at (2, 0, −2); `|a−b|>0` is symmetric only; the symmetric difference quotient gives `f'(2) = 1`). **The fix is to name the option's TEXT rather than its LETTER**, which keeps the pedagogy and silences the probe permanently instead of relocating it — the same repair this repo has applied to this class before, now applied three more times.
  - **BOTH duplicate-option rows are the BOOK's own duplicates, and they were treated DIFFERENTLY because their harm differs.** `Q2280` prints `0` at both (a) and (d) — a duplicated **distractor**, so the key `1/2` is unique and nobody can be mis-marked: preserved PUBLIC with the defect named in the solution. `Q2517` prints `2π sq. cm/s` at both (a) and (b) — a duplicated **ANSWER**, so a student choosing (b) is mathematically right and would be marked wrong: withdrawn, because every available repair invents an option the book never printed. **Harm, not shape, is the right axis for a duplicate-option row** — the Worksheets "twin" rule says repair the option text and never the key, and that rule has no move when the duplicate is the printed page's own.
  - **THE SCOPE CHECK THE USER PROMPTED WAS WORTH RUNNING AND CAME BACK CLEAN.** Asked whether JEE Mains might also carry multi-answer questions, a bank-wide scan of all 57k rows across 13 exams found **exactly 11 multi-correct rows — these 11**. JEE Mains has none by construction: Mains is single-correct MCQ + NAT, and multi-correct belongs to JEE *Advanced*, which this bank does not ingest. Post-fix the count of PUBLIC rows with more than one correct option is **0**.
  - **A DIFFERENT DEFECT CLASS SURFACED FROM THE SAME QUERY, and it is invisible to every gate here: 5 PUBLIC CBSE Class 12 board-PYQ MCQs have four options and ZERO marked correct.** Nothing catches it — `audit:keys` is scoped to `question_kind='practice'`, `board:lint` checks section structure, `audit:text` checks long-form text, and a NULL solution is legal — so the plainest question of all goes unasked: does this MCQ have an answer? On `/browse` the reveal shows nothing; in a mock the grader finds no key and marks every attempt wrong with a penalty. **Logged, NOT fixed** — different corpus, and its source of record is the official CBSE marking scheme, which that pipeline's own notes say must be read as IMAGES because the text layer yields no math. Deriving five board answers without it would put a guess where the corpus promises a verified key. The standing probe to add is one SQL line.
  - **A probe defect of my own, and it is the discriminating-test-point rule in miniature.** My first counterexample for `Q650`'s "MN is symmetric for all symmetric M, N" used `[[1,2],[2,3]]` and `[[0,1],[1,1]]` — whose product happens to come out **symmetric**, so the check "failed" and would have argued the statement was TRUE. Replaced with a search over 2×2 symmetric pairs, which finds a genuine counterexample immediately. A test point where the right and wrong answers agree proves nothing, and picking one by hand is how you land on it.

Public practice corpus 3,088 → **3,076**.

- **2026-08-26 — The 14 REPORTs from the RULE 5 hand-wave sweep adjudicated against the printed sources: 10 stem/option repairs + 4 CORRECTED PYQ KEYS + 4 rewritten solutions, and one student re-graded in their favour. The finding is that WHICH CORPUS a REPORT comes from predicts what is broken, and the two halves needed opposite treatment.**
  - **THE SPLIT IS EXACT AND IT IS THE WHOLE ENTRY. 10 practice rows: every key was already RIGHT — 10/10 matched the booklet's own printed answer key, so not one was a wrong answer. 4 PYQ rows: every key was WRONG — all four stems byte-faithful to the scanned UPSC booklets, so the answer was the issue, not the text.** The rule behind it: a practice row comes from a vision-transcribed booklet that ships its own printed key, so the KEY is the trustworthy half and the TEXT is suspect; a PYQ row comes from a clean scan that ships **no key at all** (tail pages are "SPACE FOR ROUGH WORK"), so the TEXT is trustworthy and the *answer* is a derivation someone made later. Check the half that can be wrong. Recorded as a rule in the blueprint rather than as a one-off.
  - **THE PYQ HALF TURNED ON THE USER'S INSTRUCTION MID-SESSION — "for pyqs dont use excel as source, refer to actual pdfs" — and it is what makes correcting these keys legitimate rather than an override of the examiner.** The repo's convention is to PRESERVE a printed paper's key even when wrong, because students were marked against the issued key. **That needs an issued key to preserve, and there is none**: the booklets carry no key, and the stored answer traces to a prep-house Excel whose `Answer` column sits beside plainly LLM-authored solutions — Q34's contains a literal `?` placeholder mid-derivation, Q57's says the power is 4 and then concludes 3 "indirectly", and Q77's ends **"REVIEW: official answer is 0; ... check problem statement."** A derivation, not a published key — and a demonstrably worse one than a fresh careful derivation. Keys moved **A→C, C→D, B→D, B→D**, each re-derived from the printed stem WITHOUT consulting the stored key and verified symbolically and numerically (25 checks, 0 failures), with every new solution stating in its own text that the answer is derived and that the paper carries no key.
  - **ONE REAL STUDENT WAS AFFECTED, AND THE MECHANISM IS WORTH KNOWING: `mock_attempts` stores a FROZEN score, so a key move does NOT re-grade.** Left alone, the review screen (which reads live options) would show a student's answer as correct while the result screen (which reads the stored score) still called it wrong — worse than either state alone. On Q34 a student had picked **C, the correct answer, and been marked wrong**; re-graded **11.72 → 15.05 (+3.33)**. The other three rows were unanswered by every attempt, so nobody else moved and nobody lost marks. New `regrade-attempt.ts` reuses the app's own `gradeMock` rather than re-implementing the marking scheme, and **refuses to lower a score without `--allow-lower`** — silently reducing a mark someone has already seen is not a side effect to take on a data fix.
  - **RECONSTRUCTIONS WERE WRONG 3 TIMES OUT OF 4, which is the standing argument for reading the source instead of reasoning about it.** Where a rewriter proposed what the "intended" stem must have been, the printed page contradicted it on Q2023 (guessed `x/1 = y/2 = z/3`; actually `(x+1)/2 = (y+1)/3 = (z+1)/4`), Q2010 (guessed two corruptions; there were five) and Q1831 — and was right only on Q2007, where it had predicted the unique integer triple with magnitude √38. The same pattern as Q32 the day before. Every REPORT went to the page, none was applied on a derivation.
  - **THE TRANSCRIPTION DEFECTS ARE INSTRUCTIVE ABOUT VISION INGEST, because in every case the corruption produced a question that still READS as well-formed.** Q447's stacked fraction `(1/6)sin θ` was read as **`1 − sin θ`**; Q1831's concrete vectors `î+ĵ−k̂` and `2î−3ĵ+k̂` were **symbolised into `a⃗+b⃗` and `2a⃗−3b⃗`**, which is exactly why that question appeared to state no magnitudes and no angle — the data was there and got abstracted away; Q741's "two options each, namely true and false" became "three options each (A, B, C)", moving the answer from 3/64 to 7/288, which matches no option; and Q2010's option block was **shifted**, so our (A) held printed (b)'s value — the CDS mis-slotted-option class, in a different corpus. Options were corrupted on 5 of the 8, so a stem-only repair would have left the row wrong.
  - **TWO ROWS ARE BOOK DEFECTS AND ARE PRESERVED, VERIFIED BY GLYPH FORENSICS RATHER THAN INFERENCE.** Q2406 prints `sin⁻¹(2x − √(1−x²))` — the minus confirmed at **12× zoom** — but as printed the argument leaves [−1,1] at x = −0.4, *inside the domain the question itself states*, and the derivative matches no option; the printed domain and printed key both belong to the product form. Q1163 prints `2cos 2β − 1` — confirmed at **16× zoom** — which gives `tan²α = (1+7tan²β)/(3+tan²β)`, matching no option. Both stems left exactly as printed with the defect named in the solution; both content hashes verified **byte-identical**, which is the proof the stem was untouched.
  - **A TRAP CONFIRMED BY CAS RATHER THAN ASSERTED: on Q1163 the printed and intended relations agree at EXACTLY ONE point, and it is β = 45° — the natural angle to spot-check.** `solve` returns `tanβ = 1` as the sole intersection. So a numerical spot-check there agrees by coincidence and *falsely confirms the wrong stem*, which is almost certainly how the original hand-wave was produced. This is the concrete case behind RULE 5's ban on numeric-check-as-justification.
  - **Q1803 is a genuine printed-book defect of a rarer kind: the page names FOUR points and prints only THREE position vectors.** Our pass then corrupted two of the three it did print. The omitted vector is **not guessed** — with P, R, S fixed, `Q = P + (R − S) = 4î` is the unique choice making PQRS a parallelogram, which the book's own key (a) asserts. Restored with that derivation stated in the solution.
  - **THREE OF MY OWN ERRORS, each caught by re-measuring rather than by reasoning.** (1) `count: "exact", head: true` through supabase-js returned **null** for every per-question tally and I read it as "zero student answers"; SQL showed 5 — a degraded value indistinguishable from a meaningful one, the exact shape this file already records for `/dashboard`. (2) A bare `.select()` on `attempt_answers` returned **exactly 1000 rows**, the PostgREST cap, and its per-id counts were therefore meaningless. (3) A final verification query silently returned **13 of 14 rows** because I typo'd one uuid — caught only by counting the result. In each case the tell was a number that had no business being what it was.
  - **A probe's failure is a question, not a verdict — twice.** My first symbolic check "failed" on Q34 because sympy leaves `tan θ/(tan 2θ − tan θ)` alone; rewriting in sin/cos gives `cos 2θ` exactly. And a `simplify` on a list threw rather than disproving anything. Both were probe defects; the mathematics was never in doubt.

- **2026-08-25 — CDS gets 19 timed mock tests, and the CDS corpus goes PUBLIC (2,280 q; bank 53,705 → 55,985; mocks 44 → 63). The mocks are the smaller half of the story: preparing them found and fixed 19 WRONG ANSWER KEYS, and proved that the blind re-derivation this project relies on CANNOT catch the defect that produced them.**
  - **THE BUILD ITSELF WAS SMALL, because CDS is shaped exactly like NEET and the pipeline already generalised for it.** One subject ⇒ one 120-question section; `source_row` clean 1..120 ⇒ ordering free. `pyq_month` is NULL on all 2,280 rows AND two sittings share a year, so the NDA year×month discovery loop cannot express it — CDS reuses NEET's `source_file`-keyed path with an edition-aware slug (`cds-2025-ii-english`). **That slug is load-bearing: `mockSlug()` emits the SAME string for the I and II sittings of a year, and since the mock id is `slugToUuid(slug)` the second upsert would SILENTLY OVERWRITE the first** — one sitting of that year simply missing, no error. The sittings are DERIVED from `scripts/cds/config.ts` PAPERS rather than hand-written, because that file is what stamps `source_file`; a copied 19-row table drifts silently. `buildNeet`'s loop was EXTRACTED rather than copy-pasted a third time, with "the 44 shipped NDA/NEET snapshots come back byte-identical" as the acceptance criterion — verified, and paired with an `updated_at` witness, since an unchanged fingerprint is also what you get when the write never happened.
  - **CDS BRINGS THE BANK'S FIRST FRACTIONAL MARKING** (120 q / 100 marks ⇒ +0.8333, −0.2778) and it exposed a real bug: `gradeMock` rounded `score` but not `maxScore`, so results would have read **"/ 99.996"**. Rounded in both `gradeMock` and `totalMarks`; NDA (300/600) and NEET are provably unaffected.
  - **THE HEADLINE FINDING. 15 questions had two or more character-identical options. That looked like OCR noise and was not: the transcriber had copied the CORRECT option's text into the WRONG letter's slot and then keyed that letter.** The answer as *content* was right; the answer as a *letter* was wrong. So the duplicate was a SYMPTOM OF A WRONG KEY, and the repair is two-sided — **fixing the option text ALONE makes the row strictly worse**, because it moves the correct answer to another letter, leaves the key on a genuine distractor, and removes the duplicate that was the only tripwire.
  - **A BLIND RE-DERIVATION CANNOT CATCH THIS, AND THAT IS PROVEN RATHER THAN ARGUED.** The blind protocol is this repo's strongest key control, but it is defeated when the OPTION TEXT is itself mis-transcribed: the solver derives the right answer, looks for the label carrying that text, and confirms whichever label holds it. `question_reviews` already held `bank-paper:cds-english-blind-2026-08-23` — 89 rows, **every one `confirmed`** — and one of them, `2021-2 Q59`, is a key this session disproved by reading the printed page. A swap or rotation of an option block leaves four distinct strings, invisible to `audit:keys`, to duplicate scanning, and to a set-only comparison. **The check that works is per-question and needs no solving: compare the option SET against the page (catches a wrong option) AND, separately, the label→text ORDER (catches a swap/rotation).** `2025-1 Q78` is why you need both — its set was wrong yet printed (d) is `1 4 2 3` in both its own and its neighbour's table, so the wrong table still yielded the right letter; a set-only check would have "fixed" a correct key into a wrong one.

  - **THE CONTAMINATION, and it is mine.** The house style records a chapter's transcribed key in its `config.ts` comment for the step-6 diff; `TRANSCRIPTION_BRIEF.md` separately tells every transcription agent to *"DERIVE the MCQ answer by solving"*; and I told each band agent to read the config entry for its block inventory. So the b3 agent met `// Prob 8  1. (i) A (ii) D (iii) C (iv) D` roughly **50 lines above the sentence in the same comment block saying that key must be withheld**. It derived all four correctly, recorded its reasoning, and then **refused to call the pass blind** — which is the only reason this surfaced rather than shipping as a false "blind-verified". **A key recorded FOR the cross-check and a key hidden FROM the derivation are the same bytes in the same file.** Fixed for this chapter with an `AGENT-STOP` fence; the blind pass was then re-run by an agent that confirmed it never opened config, `out/_answers/`, the band files, `.questions.json` or the DB, and returned the same **A D C D, 0 mismatches**. **Systemic, not local: `circle-9` and `statistics-9` carry un-fenced Problem-set MCQ keys in their configs today** — logged as a backfill candidate rather than edited, since they are shipped, and worth deciding before Ch.6 Circle is ingested, because that chapter's key is already sitting in the file its agents will be told to read.
  - **THE MCQ-SOLUTION GAP WAS CAUGHT TWICE BY TWO INDEPENDENT GATES**, which is the ledger entry for NCERT Integrals (22 shipped rows with a correct key and no working) being prevented rather than repeated. `apply-solutions` warned *"a key with no working ships to students"*; then `dump-review` **refused to dump at all**. The blind agent had produced `derived_answer` + a one-line `why`, which is the verify contract but not a student-facing solution. Worth noting the gap is invisible to everything else — `board:lint` checks structure, `audit:keys` skips a row with no solution, and a NULL solution is legal for an MCQ, so it shows up only as a count.
  - **THE 119/120 SEAM: `Ex. 4`'s solution is TRUNCATED at the page foot and completes overleaf.** This is the truncation class, not the duplicate class, and the distinction decides how much care it needs: a duplicate ref makes `merge.ts` throw, whereas a truncated solution passes every gate and simply stops before reaching its answer. Bands were cut at BLOCK boundaries and each agent was told to report on territory it did not own; b2 stitched both halves and confirmed the stored solution ends at `cos θ = 12/13, tan θ = 5/12`. The same instruction independently confirmed **no stranded fifth example on p118** and **no PS 8.1 spill onto p114**.
  - **`answerPages` MUST BE READ AT A CHAPTER'S LAST ANSWER — proven here rather than restated.** The Ch.8 key block spans the page break and **p-137 opens with a bare "2." and NO repeated "Practice set 8.2" heading**. A page-scoped read of p-136 alone yields PS 8.1 plus Q1 of 8.2 and silently drops Ex 8.2 Q2(i)-(vi), Q3, Q4 and all of Problem set 8 — **16 of the 33 keyed rows, with nothing on the page to signal the loss.**
  - **STEP-6: 33 exercise rows diffed — 33 AGREE, 0 OUR-ANSWER-WRONG, 0 BOOK-KEY-WRONG, 0 NO-KEY-ENTRY.** Coverage is stated as **33 of 37, not 37**: the four solved examples are outside the gate by construction (this ANSWERS section is organised under exercise headings only, and a worked example's answer is printed inside its own solution). Every one of the 33 has a key entry — unusual for this volume's terse five-page Part-2 key, and it has a cause: **Ch.8 contains no proof questions, and proofs are what that key skips.** Verified by a THIRD independent derivation from the stems (sympy over 45 numeric quantities) testing BOTH our answer and the book's against it, never by comparing the two to each other, which lets a shared error hide.
  - **TWO EQUIVALENT-FORM CASES that would each have read as a false disagreement**, and one was pre-empted by the authoring agent rather than caught later: Ex 8.2 Q2(iv), where the book prints `2√3/(√3+1)` unrationalised and we print `3 − √3` (the author gave both forms deliberately); and Ex 8.1 Q4(i), where the book writes `RQ/PR` and we write `QR/PR` — **the same segment with its vertices reversed.** Everywhere else the surd forms coincide exactly, so the 18-cell table needed no equivalence work at all.
  - **TWO KEY ENTRIES LOOK LIKE TYPOS AND ARE CORRECT** — `Ex 8.1 Q1(i)` and `Q1(ii)` are both `QR/PQ`; `Q3(i)` and `Q3(iv)` are both `MN/LN`. In each pair the angles are complementary and the same segment is opposite one and adjacent to the other, so sin of one genuinely equals cos of the other. Recorded so a later pass does not "fix" the book into being wrong.
  - **FOUR PRINTED DEFECTS, ALL IN THEORY, so they get no errata bracket and no errata file** — this chapter produces zero question-level errata. The sharpest is a **wrong formula in a `Remember this !` box: `tan θ = opposite side of ∠θ / opposite side of ∠θ`**, where the denominator must be *adjacent* — in the box students memorise from. I suspected it from the render and had the band agent confirm or refute it from the image rather than take my word; it cropped and zoomed and confirmed. The other three are `adjcent` for adjacent (in the same box, beside the wrong formula — the left column has the right word misspelled and the right column the wrong word spelled correctly), `Trigonometic` in the "Let's study" list, and `complimentary` for *complementary* on two pages.

Shipping it would put a `/browse` filter on the page returning nothing (the Class-12 Linear Programming precedent). Chapter ships with 3 subtopics, not the book's 4.
  - **VISION-ONLY, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED:** beyond this volume's operator substitution, the text layer **flattens exponents** — the opener's Pythagoras statement extracts as `(AB)2 + (BC)2 = (AC)2`, a different equation — and destroys the key's surds (`1/√2` extracts as `1 2`). **Figures were anchored from measured ink bounds rather than eyeballed**, via a column-profile probe committed as `gen-fig-trigonometry.py`; all 7 crops were then eyeballed at native resolution in a contact sheet, confirming every vertex label, angle mark (50°/40°, α/θ), side label and caption intact. Captions are kept deliberately — every stem cites its figure BY NUMBER.
  - **Two verification traps fired, both the shell-backslash class, both in PROBES rather than data:** the blind agent's first inline KaTeX check reported **176 of 176 zones failing** — entirely its own corrupted regex; re-authored as a file it read 0 failures. My own first double-escape count on a band file reported 61 and was likewise a shell artifact. **A probe authored through a shell is as likely to be corrupt as the data it checks.** The blind agent also removed four sentence-initial "A" articles that `audit:keys` would read as a concluded option letter — one on the row whose key **is** A, so that false positive would have agreed by coincidence and stayed latent until someone reordered the options.
  - Verified: 37/37 PUBLIC · 0 without a solution · 0 unsectioned · 0 missing chapter/subtopic · 17 figures · `board:lint` green (9,371 rows across 5 board exams, reconciling exactly against the 9,334 baseline + 37) · `audit:text` 0 across all five classes · `audit:omml` 0 failing zones · `audit:keys` 0 for this source. Backup taken before the bulk write. **Owed, as on every chapter of this book: a browser click-through of `/board`** — answers reveal on click, so nothing headless proves the reveal lays out, and that now includes a nine-column GFM table. **Found incidentally and logged, not fixed:** a live PUBLIC practice row (`question_number 1097`, NDA Trigonometric Identities) with **two of four options marked correct** — `audit:keys` is documented as run-after-every-ingest but is scoped by source substring, so a source nobody has re-ingested has never been scanned.

- **2026-08-22 — MHT-CET Mathematics gets a `/guide` subtree (Template C): 6 routes + 22 chapter playbooks off 2,228 PYQ across 45 shifts, and `/guide` stops being a redirect and becomes a registry-derived exam picker.** The second exam ever to get guides, and the first non-NDA one. Merge `e579256`.
  - **THE TEMPLATE WAS PICKED BY MEASUREMENT, AND THE FIRST ANSWER WAS WRONG.** The decision script's step 2 (cross-chapter levers) looked alive on a keyword scan — 8 candidates clearing "≥4 chapters AND ≥40 q", which is Template A. Reading the actual questions killed it: **`family-through-point` (96 q / 9 ch) is not a technique** — "passes through the point (1,2)" is how you pin down a constant — and `substitution` (144 q / 20 ch) is incidental in 16 of its 20 chapters ("substituting b=8, a=6 into the sine rule" is arithmetic). `mean-variance` matched inside **"not necessarily MEANingful"** and swallowed "MEAN Value Theorem", so 3 of its 6 chapters were false. The catalog went 8 → 5, which is thin against Template A's precedent of 12, and the user called Template C.
  - **Two rules came out of that and generalise beyond this guide.** (1) **Negation separates a lever from a precondition**: "the lines ARE coplanar" is the condition under test, "three NON-coplanar vectors" is scene-setting before a triple-product identity — applying it cut one candidate 46 → 19. (2) **Word boundaries are not optional**, the `cement`/`displaCEMENT` trap in another dress. Both are recorded in the survey artifact.
  - **EXECUTION-MODE STRANDS ARE DEAD HERE, and that is measured rather than asserted.** Probing four candidate modes per chapter shows them uniform — evaluate 10-40%, solve-for-parameter 20-40% almost everywhere — with **exactly one outlier, Mathematical Logic at 70% "which statement is true" against ~0% elsewhere**. Per step 5 that forces **tier-style strands**, the History/Polity shape, on a subject nobody would have guessed needed it.
  - **THE STRATEGIC FACT THE WHOLE GUIDE RESTS ON: MHT-CET HAS NO NEGATIVE MARKING.** Every shipped guide organises its strategy page around attempt-vs-skip. Here a blank and a wrong answer score identically, so the axis is **ORDER and TIME**: 50 q × 2 marks in 90 minutes = **1.8 min/question**, `targetAttempts` is 50 because anything less is strictly worse, and no page tells a student to skip. `skipSubtopics` renders as "Last in the prep queue" with the strike-through deliberately dropped — on this paper anything reading as "skip" is actively wrong advice.
  - **TIERS ARE BUILT ON RECENT WEIGHTAGE (2024-25), NOT LIFETIME, AND THAT CAUGHT A REAL TRAP.** The 2025 syllabus moved: **Measures of Dispersion ran 1.0 q/paper across 29 shifts of 2023-24 then scored ZERO across all 14 papers of 2025**, while **Conic Sections went 3 → 16**. At 9% HARD, Dispersion is exactly what a lifetime-tiered guide would recommend as a cheap win — and it is dead. My first per-chapter rate query got this wrong in the same direction, dividing by only the papers of years where a chapter appears, so a dead chapter read as a live 1.00/paper; fixed before it reached any copy.
  - **`/guide` becomes a real exam picker**, which its own comment had anticipated verbatim ("when a second exam ships … this becomes a real exam picker"). It is **derived from `EXAM_REGISTRY`**, so a third exam's guides are a one-line `guidesPath` change. That also required the sitemap's "/guide is deliberately ABSENT — it is a redirect, not a page" note to be reversed: it is a page again, and belongs in the sitemap.
  - **THREE TESTS USED MHT-CET AS THEIR EXEMPLAR OF A GUIDE-LESS EXAM** — `resolveGuidesHref`, `resolveExamNav`, `pickExamCardHref`. MHT-CET was the codebase's canonical "no guide yet" stand-in, so shipping its guide surfaced every place that assumption was encoded. Each keeps its invariant on an exam that still qualifies (jee-mains / neet) **and gains a positive assertion for mht-cet**, rather than losing the assertion.
  - **`guide-strategy-headline` asserted NDA's marking scheme as a universal law** — `penaltyPerWrong ≈ marksPerCorrect / 3` for EVERY guide — which a correct MHT-CET headline would have failed. Same [[default-becomes-assertion]] shape as the coverage bug two weeks earlier: a rule true for the cases its author had, silently wrong for the first new one. Marking scheme is now explicit per-guide data, plus a new assertion that a no-penalty exam attempts all 50.
  - **THE NEW STANDING GATE FOUND A HOLE NOTHING ELSE COULD.** `tests/guide-mht-cet-maths-playbooks.test.ts` (11) checks structure, strand sizes, the 0.9 q/paper inclusion line, and computes the "47% of the paper" headline **from the data** so the copy cannot rot. The load-bearing one sweeps **EVERY taxonomy name the guide references** — strategy strands, the tail block, trends callouts — not just playbooks, because **`BrowseLink` fails silently**, widening to an exam-wide filter rather than erroring. Conic Sections is named by a trends drill and has no playbook, so nothing else covered it. A second test fails if a playbook lists only SOME of its chapter's live subtopics, the invisible under-coverage case.
  - **Built with 10 subagents against two written contracts** (a data brief carrying every verified number so nothing was re-derived, and a routes brief). Three times an agent was right and my brief was wrong, which is the argument for contracts over inline prompts: I asserted formulas.ts "contains LaTeX" — it must not, because `FormulaSheet` renders raw text and LaTeX would ship literal `\frac{...}`; the trends agent **refused to build the 27x5 drift matrix** the reference shape implies, because no verified per-chapter-per-year data exists and a fabricated grid reads as measured in every cell, shipping 4 honest rows of per-paper RATES instead (raw counts are meaningless when 2021 is 1 shift and 2023 is 17 — which also means the shared `DriftTable` cannot render them); and the landing agent cut "47 of the 100 marks" as a duplicate of "47% of the paper", true by construction at 2 marks/question.
  - **[[heredoc-backslash-eating]] fired FOUR times on me in one session**, once corrupting the very test I was writing to catch silent failures. The rule is not "be careful with heredocs" — it is **author anything containing a backslash through the editor, never a shell heredoc**.
  - Verified: **GATE_RESULT PASS** (3,397 tests + 213 prod-contract); prerendered `.html` **714 → 743** with all 27 MHT-CET pages, the hub and the picker static and every NDA guide page still present; an independent sweep over **260k chars of editorial** (0 control chars, 0 U+FFFD, 0 smart quotes, 0 double-escaped LaTeX); **27 chapters + 77 subtopic names diffed against live taxonomy, zero mismatches**; 22 + 5 = 27 chapters and 2,121 + 107 = 2,228 questions both reconcile against `OVERVIEW`. **Owed: the browser click-through** — prerendering proves these generate, never that they lay out, and the mobile side-nav is a Radix portal that does not exist until tapped. **Deliberately NOT built:** the principles axis (see above), and MHT-CET Physics/Chemistry guides — their banks are comparable in size but Chemistry is 3.3% HARD and flat where Maths is 38.4% and steeply tiered, so each needs its own template analysis rather than a copy of this one.

- **2026-08-21 — THE HEADER EXAM PILL IS GONE.** The nav no longer offers an exam switcher; `qb_exam` survives and is written only by `/welcome` + `/account`. Notes always routes to its index, Bank/Guides/Board still personalise FROM the cookie, and the Mocks tab is no longer exam-gated. 6 source files, 2 specs, no migration, no data change. Prompted by the user asking whether the pill was necessary on `/dashboard/health`.
  - **THE MEASUREMENT REFRAMED THE QUESTION, and it is the whole entry.** The instinct was "it does nothing, delete it". Measured across all 13 registry exams the pill's five effects split into two kinds. **Upgrades:** Bank —> the exam prefiltered (13/13), Board —> the exam's book (5/13). **Downgrades:** Notes —> `/notes/<slug>`, which renders *"teaching notes are coming soon"* for the **10 of 13 exams that have none**, and Mocks, whose tab the pill **HID for 11 of 13 states** — so a CBSE-12 student never saw that 44 timed mocks exist. Plus one effect that is simply **inert**: `/guide` 307-redirects to `/guide/nda` unconditionally, so the Guides href has never changed anything for anyone. A control that routes most visitors to a dead end is not merely useless, and that is what justified removal over the initial "just hide it on staff pages".
  - **NULL BECAME A REAL STATE, and that is the load-bearing change.** `readExamSlugFromCookieString` returned `DEFAULT_EXAM_SLUG` for a missing cookie, so "no choice" and "chose NDA" were indistinguishable. Harmless while the pill existed; **actively wrong once it does not**, because the pill was the ONLY way an anonymous visitor could ever set that cookie — and anon is the overwhelming majority (~2,969 visitors/month against 125 student profiles). Left alone, every anon JEE visitor's Bank tab would drop them into the NDA bank with no control left on the page to correct it. It now returns `ExamSlug | null`, and an **unknown** slug also reads as null: a retired slug in a year-old cookie must read as "no choice", never as somebody else's exam.
  - **NOTES IS THE ONE TAB THAT NEVER PERSONALISES, deliberately** — the asymmetry with Guides is evidence-based, not stylistic. Guides has no dead end (`resolveGuidesHref` already returns the index for an exam with no subtree) and sending NDA users to `/guide` would only add a redirect hop to reach the identical page, so it keeps its shortcut. Notes has a dead end for 10 of 13, so the tab goes to the cross-exam index that lists the 3 exams which actually have notes.
  - **`hasMocks` STAYS, and checking that before deleting it is the step that mattered.** The obvious cleanup — "the flag only fed the nav gate" — is wrong: `src/lib/mocks/mocksNav.ts` builds the `/mock` catalogue's own exam rail from it. `tests/mocks-nav.test.ts` passing **untouched** is the evidence, and it would have gone red on the naive removal. `/mock` has no exam filter at all (`getPublishedMocks()` returns everything; the breadcrumb reads "All exams"), which is why an unscoped tab cannot dead-end anyone.
  - **AN INTERMEDIATE DESIGN WAS BUILT, GATED GREEN, AND THEN DELETED.** The first pass scoped the pill instead of removing it — a `shouldShowExamPill()` hiding it on `/dashboard/*` + `/superadmin/*`. It passed the full gate, and the user's follow-up ("shouldn't it be hidden completely?") made all of it redundant, so the helper and its 5 specs were reverted rather than left as unreachable code. Worth recording because the *reason* the intermediate step looked sufficient was that only the Mocks downgrade had been found at that point; the Notes coming-soon downgrade surfaced only when the removal question forced a second look at what each tab actually lands on. **The cheap first fix is what exposed the real one.**
  - **Comments that justify a layout by naming a deleted component are a real defect class.** Removing `ExamPill.tsx` left six references, three of them load-bearing rationale ("so the tabs + exam pill + account fit at 360px" explaining why nav labels hide below `sm:`). All rewritten; the freed ~70px is now recorded as what affords Mocks being unconditional. A `git rm` does not clean up the prose that explains it.
  - Verified: specs written first and **confirmed failing for the right reason** in both passes (6 assertions for the nav rewrite, each the intended behaviour change); typecheck clean; `GATE_RESULT: PASS`; prerendered `.html` at **714**, the post-notes-handout baseline, so nothing de-cached. **Owed, and not provable headlessly:** the browser click-through — header with and without a `qb_exam` cookie, and at ~360px with a staff account (the pill's removal frees room, but Mocks is now always drawn).
  - **Deliberately NOT done:** deleting the cookie outright. It still drives the practice-only `/browse` default — the cookie branch mutates `filters` BEFORE the landing check, so Foundation/CBSE-11 students land on their practice questions rather than the landing panel — and it still personalises Bank/Board for the 92 students who declared an exam. Also left: `resolveNotesHref` + the registry's `notesPath` are now consumed only by tests (the nav stopped calling them); and **pill usage was never instrumented** — `user_activity`'s kind allowlist is learning-anchored and the `question-bank` Vercel project is unreachable through MCP — so this was decided on what the control DOES, never on how often it was used.

- **2026-08-21 — CBSE Class 12 gains a BOARD-PYQ corpus beside its textbook one: 1,766 questions from ALL 78 papers of 2022—2026, every one solved from the official marking scheme, flipped PUBLIC. The exam goes 1,414 -> 3,180 q; the bank 51,424 -> 53,332. New pipeline `scripts/cbse-12-pyq/`.**
  - **A SECOND corpus into the SAME exam and the SAME chapters, separated by `question_kind`** — the `mh-ssc-10` / `mh-hsc-12` shape. A chapter now carries its NCERT exercises and its board questions together, and the `/browse` PYQ/Practice toggle separates them. `practiceOnly` is DROPPED: Class 12 IS a board year.
  - **DROPPING THAT FLAG IS NOT COSMETIC, AND MEASURING IT FIRST IS THE POINT.** `listChapterLandings` derives the question KIND from it, so the flag also switches all 13 chapter landing pages from textbook questions to board PYQs AND re-ranks which chapters clear `MIN_QUESTIONS_FOR_LANDING`. A chapter with 300 textbook rows and 9 PYQs keeps its page today and loses it after — a live indexed URL disappearing with nothing in the diff to say so. `flip-impact.ts` measured it BEFORE the change: **12 chapters KEEP their page, Application of Integrals GAINS one (14 textbook rows against 74 PYQs), 0 LOSE one.** `/board` is untouched because it filters on non-null `section_seq`, and **0 pyq rows carry one while all 1,414 textbook rows still do**.
  - **78 PAPERS PRINT 3,519 QUESTIONS AND ONLY 1,766 ARE DISTINCT.** CBSE issues each sitting as three near-identical sets (65/N/1, /2, /3), so about half of every sibling is a reprint. Dedup is `content_hash`, and the work plan follows from it: solve the 17 openers first, after which each sibling owns only 4—15 unique rows. `solution-status.ts` counts rows a paper OWNS rather than prints — the difference between dispatching 52 agents and dispatching the ones that need one.
  - **EVERY MARKING SCHEME MUST BE READ AS AN IMAGE, and that is measured, not cautious.** Across whole schemes the text layer yields ZERO pi, ZERO theta and ZERO superscript digits, in a Maths paper full of trigonometry and definite integrals; 2025 65/1/1 gives ONE radical and no integral sign at all. Prose survives perfectly, which is exactly what makes it dangerous.
  - **THE SCHEME IS THE SOURCE, NOT THE AUTHORITY: 35 defect brackets** (2022 7 — 2023 15 — 2024 9 — 2025 3 — 2026 1). The sharpest are not arithmetic slips: **65/4/2 Q30's scheme REPRODUCES A DIFFERENT LPP than the paper prints** (its own solution correctly solves ours); two 65/3-series corner-point tables are **headed with another question's objective**, identified as boilerplate by finding that objective on a SIBLING paper and then checking the 65/4 series is clean; and one scheme's entire entry is a refusal — *f defined in the question is not a function, so full marks to be given for attempting the question*.
  - **THE DECLINES MATTER AS MUCH AS THE BRACKETS.** About 40 look-alikes were checked and refused. The brief itself had to be CORRECTED after it named one as a defect: **X-or-Y in a scheme means accept-either-form**, ordinary marking practice, and four agents independently refused the shape after one had duly bracketed it. The lesson is bigger than the item — a defect list is a set of hypotheses, and naming one makes an agent likelier to find it. Reporting a listed defect as ABSENT is a result.
  - **AND IT CUT AGAINST ME TWICE.** I put an unverified claim into an agent's prompt (a closed form that appears nowhere in the book) and a MIS-CITED one (I said 2025 65/5/2 Q12 was CBSE-acknowledged keyless; it has a perfectly good key — the keyless Q12 is in **2023**). Both agents checked rather than conformed, and the second read all 21 scheme pages including front matter before contradicting me. **Verify a claim about the source before putting it in another agent's prompt.**
  - **ONE GENUINE ANSWER DISPUTE IN 1,766 ROWS, and it is CBSE's.** 2023 65/4/2 Q13 asks how many solutions dy/dx = (y+1)/(x-1) has with y(1) = 2; the key says ONE. The general solution y = C(x-1) - 1 equals -1 at x = 1 for EVERY C, so no constant satisfies the condition and the count is ZERO (verified with sympy). **Key PRESERVED** per the paper-defect convention — students were marked against the issued key.
  - **FOUR PHRASINGS THAT MAKE `audit-keys` FIRE ON A CORRECT SOLUTION**, all found here and all now in the brief: Assertion-Reason's (A)/(R) statement labels; *option a <text>* where the article reads as letter A; **a closing parenthetical dismissing a distractor BY LETTER** (the commonest); and **Hence B is of order 3x4, where B NAMES A MATRIX**. The fourth was found by SCANNING all 494 solved MCQs rather than waiting for it: 1 live false positive and **2 LATENT**, agreeing with their key only by coincidence and one option-reorder from going red. Rule now stated: never put a bare capital A—D where a probe could read it as an option label.
  - **THE FIGURE LOAD IS 41, AND THE ROWS THAT REFERENCE A FIGURE THEY LACK ARE ANSWERABLE ANYWAY.** `audit-figures.ts` exists because no other gate reads a stem and asks whether the thing it points at exists. It found 23 such rows — only 8 distinct questions, 6 of them case-study sets — and every one was opened and read: the semi-vertical angle, the cup's depth and radius, the triangle's vertices are all stated in words. **Its own v1 was written from the rows it flagged and so was blind to three phrasings, under-reporting by 7 across two whole sets.** A probe validated only against what it already flags cannot show you what it misses.
  - **A SOURCE-OF-RECORD DEFECT NO GATE COULD SEE, caught by an authoring agent.** `dump-solutions` omits already-solved rows — that is what keeps the job finite — but these files are COMMITTED, so re-dumping cut one paper 53 rows -> 23 and would have deleted 30 authored solutions from the repo's record (I had already done it to another, 52 -> 9). Fixed with `--full`, which rebuilds a file as a MIRROR OF THE DB; all three restored and the rebuild PROVEN lossless by diffing HEAD row-by-row on hash.
  - **PARALLEL-RUN HAZARDS, each reported independently by two or more agents:** a generically-named scratch script **overwritten by a concurrent agent's copy hardcoded to a DIFFERENT PAPER** (running it would have written one paper's solutions into another's, silently, with every hash still valid); leftover probes carrying **literal control bytes inside a control-character regex class**, inherited by copying; and **my own `git add` of a PATTERN while agents were writing**, which twice swept in-flight files into a commit and once **silently invalidated a running agent's field-diff** by making HEAD its own half-finished edits. A scratch-file namespace protects an agent from other AGENTS, not from the orchestrator mutating shared state underneath it.
  - **A CONTROL CHARACTER IN JSON IS ESCAPED, so a raw-byte scan is blind to it** — an agent injected chr(1), the serialiser wrote six ASCII characters, and its check came back clean. THREE separate agents found a literal 0x01 in a file written through the ORDINARY Write tool, one inside a Python COMMENT where the interpreter parsed it silently. I put one in the brief while writing the paragraph warning about it. Scan BOTH layers, scan your own probes, and never type an escape sequence you are describing.
  - **The final audit caught a defect invisible on the website.** 4 math zones of the documented prime-on-a-parenthesised-group-containing-cup form: KaTeX renders it, so `/browse` and `/board` look right, and it surfaces ONLY as raw LaTeX in a teacher's downloaded Word key. `fix-omml-zones.ts` rewrites them to `\overline{...}` — the only form measured to survive the converter — and re-checks through the real `findOmmlFailures` before writing, so a repair cannot swap one unconvertible form for another.
  - Verified: **1,766/1,766 solved**, 3,180 PUBLIC / 0 PRIVATE, gate PASS with build, 631 prerendered `.html`, and all five audits clean (`audit-keys` 0 — `audit-omml` 0 — `audit:text` 0 across 5 classes — `board:lint` pass — `audit-figures` adjudicated). 0 of 1,766 rows lack a chapter or subtopic. **Owed, as on every board corpus: a browser click-through of the `/browse` answer reveal**, which reveals on click and so is not provable headlessly. See [[cbse-12-board-pyq-ingestion]].

- **2026-08-20 — TEACHING decks: the `.pptx` builder gains concept/derivation slides and question→answer pairs, and the first set ships — MH State Board Std XI Physics Ch.3 "Motion in a Plane", 3 decks (46 · 40 · 28) + a combined 117-slide file. `scripts/ppt/`. Three sizing defects fixed, one of them LATENT IN THE SHIPPED QUESTION DECK.**
  - **THE BUILDER WAS EXTENDED, NOT FORKED, and the seam was already there.** `SlideSpec` was a discriminated union over a generic `Block` model, so `teaching` and `answer` variants cost two block-builders; `questionSlide` became a generic `blocksSlide` all three share. **The 24 existing tests passing untouched is what shows the question deck was left alone** — and a new test walks every slide of a question deck and FAILS if a teaching accent leaks in, because that deck is a printed teacher artifact whose contract is black Cambria.
  - **A PDF CANNOT CLICK-TO-REVEAL, so the reveal is a second slide.** `planDeck` expands one authored `practice` entry into a question slide and then the same question answered, same number. Worse, I called the first one FIXED while looking at a render whose last word was missing off the bottom edge — the user caught it.
  - **DEFECT 1, and it was latent in the ALREADY-SHIPPED question deck: `pickFontSize` measured with the OPTIMISTIC line width while layout draws with the PESSIMISTIC one.** The builder deliberately keeps two estimates (`purpose: "sizing"` vs `"layout"`) and documents why — but choosing the FONT with the optimistic one means a slide sized "just fits" is then laid out a line taller and runs past the bottom. Building an unfittable control slide calibrated it honestly: **control 97.2%, worst legitimate slide 92.2%, flag above 96%.** A probe that has never gone red proves nothing.

  - **SYLLABUS FIT WAS MEASURED BEFORE PICKING PRACTICE QUESTIONS, and it inverted the obvious choice.** JEE files **~30 of its 52 "Circular Motion" questions as circular DYNAMICS** — banking, vertical circles, loop-the-loop — none of which this chapter teaches (verified by searching it: `banking`, `angular acceleration`, `non-uniform` all absent, while **conical pendulum and centripetal FORCE are present**). Spilling began at roughly **1,640 entries — 33% of max** — so the rule stayed silent through the entire incident and the problem was found by a human looking. It was not a badly-chosen number, it was **the wrong QUANTITY**: 0071 reasons about "3.8 MB of query TEXT" and used entry count as a stand-in, but the exporter materialises whole ROWS (~45 columns) — **1,580 kB against 911 kB of text**, a factor of 1.73 the proxy cannot see, and a ratio that moves with the mix of long ad-hoc SQL versus short PostgREST statements. Migration 0080 records `statements_bytes` + `work_mem_bytes` and the rule divides one by the other; `work_mem` is RECORDED rather than hard-coded because it is the denominator and is per-role settable (verified no role override exists today — a fact about today, not a guarantee).

The `temp written` sits on the **Function Scan** node, because `pg_stat_statements` is a set-returning function whose result is materialised into a tuplestore that overflows `work_mem`. Three differently-shaped queries (a sort, an aggregate, a count) each wrote **exactly 195 blocks**, and one query that scanned the store three times wrote 582 ≈ 3 x 194. **Any read pays the full cost** — a bare `select count(*)` is as expensive as a full scan.
  - **I CONTAMINATED MY OWN MEASUREMENT AND REPORTED IT AS FACT — the exact trap this repo already documents.** I quoted 3.73 GB/day from a 6.5-minute window in which **three of my own `pg_stat_statements` probes had run**, each spilling 1,560 kB. PG 17's `stats_since` then turned the correction from inference into measurement: exactly 3 probes fell inside that window (4.57 MB), and none fell inside the earlier 92-second sample, which is therefore clean. Corrected to **2.71 GB/day**, matching the uncontaminated 7.2 h window (2.73) and the 92 s sample (2.86). The conclusion survived; the number did not. **When measuring whether an intervention worked, the diagnostic tooling is part of the system under test** — and this failure mode was already written down before I hit it.
  - **THE REMEDY IS NOW SCHEDULED, because the recurrence interval was 10 DAYS, not the "~3 months" this file predicted.** `--reset-if-needed` on the daily job clears the store **after the snapshot is stored** (resetting first destroys the reading that justifies it) once it crosses the warn line. **Condition-based, not calendar-based** — a monthly job would have missed this incident outright. **Opt-in, never the default**: a reset is irreversible, so running `db:health` by hand can never wipe the history as a side effect of asking for a report. Migration 0081 exists because **`service_role` cannot execute `pg_stat_statements_reset` at all** (verified: `has_function_privilege` false; the function is owned by `postgres` and PostgREST cannot reach the `extensions` schema) — so a `SECURITY DEFINER` wrapper was structurally required, not stylistic.
