- **2026-08-06 — JEE Mains CHEMISTRY COMPLETE: 259 → 3,455 q PUBLIC across all 88 papers on disk. The exam is now Maths + Physics + Chemistry, every sitting 2021-2026.** Chemistry was the last subject; it had sat at legacy-2021-only since the exam was added. 45 papers ingested this run, the majority through the **BLIND lane** — no trustworthy key, so every answer is independently derived and the source key is never shown to the solver.
  - **The SAFE lane earned its keep on a paper my own triage called SAFE.** 2023-apr11's ENTIRE Q141-Q150 NAT key block is displaced by +1 — each key is the NEXT question's answer. Proven on three rows before touching anything: Q148 was keyed **224** for "maximum lone pairs on a central atom", which is impossible (the true max is 3) and is in fact Q149's 2.24 L written as 224 x 10^-2; Q149 was keyed 4, which is Q150's answer; Q141 was keyed 1, which is Q142's Kc. **Q143 is the trap worth remembering — its displaced value happens to EQUAL its correct value, so it agrees, and that agreement is pure coincidence.** Nothing in the numbering can see a shift INSIDE a complete block; only re-derivation can, which is why `triage.ts` documents itself as a report and not an oracle.
  - **Thirty source answer-key errors** caught and corrected across the run, each re-derived against the printed options rather than taken on an agent's word. Two recurring shapes: the printed solution contradicting its own printed letter (micellisation, where the body reads dS>0 and dH>0 while the heading prints the exactly-backwards option), and a dropped digit in the key table (dT = 0.82 K keyed as 2 instead of 82). Papers with ZERO errors are common and were reported as such — the 1-2 per paper rate is a prior, not a quota.
  - **~60 questions skipped rather than guessed**, and the reasons are specific, not "hard": two options printed byte-identical (chemistry unambiguous, LETTER not); a stem whose own numbers are self-contradictory; 63 g of a polymer whose repeat unit weighs 106; a Kc question where the paper's own solution derives 0.02 while its key says 50 (the reciprocal) AND the stem demands a "nearest integer", so neither value is defensible.
  - **The 2021 compilations are NOT 30/30/30 and the extractor assumed they were.** p16 prints 17 Physics / 24 Chemistry / 20 Maths, so its "Chemistry" dump was full of integrals, determinants and 3-D planes. Caught by scanning the dumps for cross-subject terms BEFORE dispatching agents at them. `retag-compilation.ts` now reads the truth the source states outright (`**PART-II CHEMISTRY**`) and refuses unless banner totals reconcile exactly with the record count. Checked, and did NOT touch, the already-shipped p11/p12 and the shipped Physics of p13-p16 — all were classified BY CONTENT in an earlier pass, so no backfill was owed. **Verifying that before raising an alarm mattered; the inference that shipped data must be contaminated was wrong.**
  - **Four latent pipeline bugs, every one a SILENT failure.** (1) `skip[]` is paper-global but keyed on question number, so an earlier subject's pass suppressed this subject's questions after the re-tag. (2) Both assemblers globbed `<id>_sol_*.json` and merged them — readdir is alphabetical, so `_sol_physics.json` **overwrote** `_sol_chem.json` for shared numbers, clobbering real answers with that pass's `skip:true`. This was the actual cause; fixing (1) alone changed nothing. (3) `assemble-blind`'s can-synthesize gate read options from the agent JSON only, so an option block restored by hand was invisible to the check it existed to satisfy. (4) Content-free math zones — `\(\ \)`, a trailing `\ `, and `\(\\)` (which parses as a lone backslash, since the closing `\)` claims the second one) — each reduce to a bare backslash that KaTeX rejects, taking the whole stem down, while `scan-flip` passes them because the delimiters balance. Together 1-3 were dropping **46 real questions** behind a bare "(skip)" that read like a deliberate call.
  - **New standing tools:** `coverage.ts` (reconciles a subject BOTH ways — it was validated against Physics, which correctly reported 0 not-ingested), `triage.ts` (SAFE vs BLIND per paper), `retag-compilation.ts`, `unskip-retagged.ts`, `apply-stem-fixes.ts`, `apply-option-fixes.ts`, `repair-broken.ts`, and `AGENT_BRIEF.md` (the two prompts, pulled out of the dispatch messages where they had been retyped for ten waves). `dump-subject.ts --blind` withholds the key, because an agent that can SEE a shifted key rationalises toward it rather than solving past it.
  - **Completion is verified, not asserted:** 88 papers on disk, 88 ingested, 0 not-ingested, 0 in-DB-but-not-on-disk; every short paper's gap accounted for by its own `skip[]` except 5 already-logged stragglers; 3 rows withheld PRIVATE, all deliberate; 1 KaTeX-broken row across 10,634 JEE questions, and it is the pre-existing PRIVATE one. **Caveat worth stating plainly: BLIND-lane answers have no external check** — they are derived, not verified against a key, because no usable key exists. That is weaker evidence than the SAFE papers carry, and it covers most of this run. `audit:keys` flags 381 of 2,539 MCQs, but 325 are `IMAGE_OPTIONS` (what a drawn option looks like, not a defect); of the 50 `SOLN≠KEY` I sampled ~26 and every one was a probe false positive, in three families the probe cannot distinguish — distractor-dismissal tails, match-list mappings, and statement-set answers where the trailing letters are STATEMENT labels rather than option letters. **Not all 50 were checked individually.** See [[jee-mains-ingestion]].

- **2026-08-05 — Egress measured and traced to BUILDS, not traffic: the gate's `next build` is now conditional on the changeset (`918f0b5`), removing ~3.9 GB/month with no loss of coverage.** Follows the query fix below; the Supabase free tier reads 11.48 GB against a 5 GB allowance, 96.4% of it PostgREST. **⚠️ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-13 — DO NOT PLAN AGAINST THESE FIGURES. The project is on SUPABASE PRO: 250 GB included, 1.73 GB used, 0 GB overage (~0.7%, 100–390 MB/day).** Egress is a non-issue with ~145× headroom, and it stopped being one at the plan change, not at this fix. The "11.48 GB / 5 GB" pair above is a free-tier reading preserved for the narrative only; it was quoted as current fact in a later session and sent an hour of work at a problem that no longer existed. The conditional build remains worth having (it is also build minutes and CI time) — just not as an egress remedy. **The only meter still worth watching is Vercel Hobby Active CPU.**
  - **THE ARITHMETIC, and it closes a loop left open on 2026-07-29.** A `/questions` landing-page response is **37 kB** (25 rows, 1,506 bytes/question, measured); a full build prerenders 689 pages of which ~317 query Postgres ≈ **25 MB**; git says **145 pushes to main in 30 days**, each triggering **THREE** builds — pre-push hook, CI, Vercel deploy. 145 × 3 × 25 MB ≈ **10.9 GB against 11.48 GB observed.** Builds essentially ARE the egress; scripts, audits, MCP and real users are the remainder. This also explains the flat ~200 MB daily plateau the first egress analysis flagged as unexplained: 200 ÷ 25 ≈ 8 builds ≈ a 3-push day. **It looked "quantised" because it literally is a count of builds** — a plateau in a usage chart is a hint to look for a fixed-size repeated unit, not a mystery baseline.
  - **THE FIX: 78 of those 145 pushes (54%) changed nothing the compiler reads** — pure ingestion data and docs — so their builds *could not have failed* and ran twice each anyway. Build is now conditional in both gates off ONE shared rule (`scripts/lib/needsBuild.ts`, spec `tests/needs-build.test.ts`, CLI `scripts/needs-build.ts`, consumed by `.githooks/pre-push` + a `if:` on CI's Build step) so the two cannot drift.
  - **The polarity is the whole design: an allowlist of SKIPS, never of builds.** Inert = `*.md` · `tests/` · `scripts/` · `supabase/` · `generated-papers/` (verified: nothing under `src/` imports any of them, and only a LEADING segment matches so `src/scripts/…` is still app code). Anything unrecognised — a new top-level dir, a new config file, a rename — **builds**. Inverted, this would be a silent hole in the gate that widens as the repo grows; as written it can only ever be too cautious. Fail-safe extends to the plumbing: an unresolvable base (new branch, all-zeros SHA, shallow clone, missing git) reports "build needed", and **CI needs `fetch-depth: 0`** or every run fails safe and silently undoes the saving.
  - **This beat the option I had recommended.** I first proposed dropping the local pre-push build outright (~3.6 GB) — but that trades away real protection, and measuring the src-vs-data split showed the conditional version saves **more** (~3.9 GB, because it covers CI too) at **zero** coverage cost, since it only skips builds incapable of failing. **Measuring the changeset split before choosing changed which option was correct.**
  - **Supabase Pro was ruled out by the user** (right call for now — it buys ceiling, not cause), and the reasoning inverted vs the entry below: capacity is the wrong answer for a defect that grows with the bank, but a reasonable one for a fixed quota. **Also on the table and cheaper than anything built: push less often** — 430 commits across 145 pushes is ~5/day; batching to 2/day would alone take builds to ~4.5 GB/month.

- **2026-08-05 — `/browse` was writing ~14 MB to disk on EVERY page load: `queryQuestions` sorted the full row shape to keep 25 rows. Split into two round trips; temp writes for that path go to ZERO (`fa9b627`).** Opened by a Supabase "running out of Disk IO Budget" email, and it turned out to be the same defect behind the ECONNRESET gate failures and part of the egress overage.
  - **THE DEFECT: a sort's payload is every SELECTED column, and this query selected everything.** `queryQuestions` fetched `text`, `context`, `solution`, four lateral joins and the options aggregate in the *same* query that carries the `ORDER BY` — so Postgres sorted ~22,000 rows at ~922 bytes each in order to keep 25, an `external merge` spilling **13.9 MB per call**. `pg_stat_statements` attributes **99.4% of the whole database's temp writes to that one query shape** (112 GB / 30k calls in the tracked window; **1,097 GB lifetime**, against a 144 MB database). Fix: an id-only query carries the filters + ORDER BY + range, then `queryQuestionsByIds` fetches the wide shape for the 25 surviving ids. Sort payload ~922 → ~30 bytes.
  - **Measured, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, TIMING OFF)` as `anon`: `external merge Disk: 13.9 MB` / 178.8 ms → `top-N heapsort Memory: 27 kB` / 33–48 ms, 0 temp.** The full gate then passed with **zero** ECONNRESET / statement-timeout / SIGTERM signals, 234 test files green, 623 prerendered `.html` (nothing de-cached).
  - **TWO of my own prior diagnoses were WRONG, and the wrong one was written into the code.** (1) The 2026-08-03 entry and a comment in `query.ts` both asserted the query "runs in ~13 ms" and blamed pure contention — that measured an index lookup, not the statement the app issues, and it sent the fix to `experimental.cpus: 4` + `staticPageGenerationTimeout: 180`, throttling the symptom. (2) The egress analysis concluded "no single runaway query is responsible" — true of bytes returned, false about the machine's health. **A plan-level measurement (`pg_stat_statements` / `EXPLAIN`) would have caught both; an EXPLAIN of a hand-simplified query caught neither.**
  - **`count: "exact"` was the obvious suspect and was NOT the problem** — PostgREST already compiles it to its own narrow `pgrst_source_count` CTE, measured at 10 ms as an index-only scan. Hand-splitting it would have been a no-op. Checking before building saved the wrong fix.
  - **This host's clock makes `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` lie by ~50×** (3,219 ms with per-row timing vs 178.8 ms with `TIMING OFF` for the identical statement). Any latency number from this database needs `TIMING OFF`; `Sort Method` and `temp written` are plan properties and stay trustworthy under load, which is why they are the acceptance criteria here rather than wall time.
  - **Deliberately NOT adding a covering index** for the sort: it would help only some filter combinations, and every index adds write amplification on ingestion — more of the same Disk IO the fix exists to protect.
  - **Incidentally fixed a live bug:** `queryQuestions` selected `numeric_answer` but never mapped it, so JEE Section-B NAT questions rendered a **blank answer on `/browse`** while `/saved` (which uses `queryQuestionsByIds`) showed it correctly. Sharing the mapper fixes it and deletes ~60 duplicated lines. **The general shape: two functions returning the same view-model with two hand-written mappers will drift, and the drift is invisible on the surface nobody re-checks.**
  - **Ordering was entirely unasserted** across 8 existing browse-query tests — precisely the invariant a two-phase fetch breaks. Three tests added (base contract, across a page boundary, subtopic teaching order) and **proven to go red** when the order restoration is removed. Egress is untouched by this fix (both phases still return 25 rows) — see the ROADMAP entry for what remains.

- **2026-08-05 — The Physics syllabus page was rendering an unchecked blank AS A CHECKED CLAIM, and its chapter matrix was entirely empty. Both fixed, plus the 238-section NCERT→State Board edge authored.** Triggered by the user asking "are these tables not updated?" — they were not stale; two of the three edges the page reads had never been authored for Physics.
  - **THE DEFECT: the alignment table printed "not in NCERT" on all 318 rows, and the page's own caption calls that "a checked claim".** Nothing had been checked — the NCERT→State Board edge had ZERO rows for Physics (Chemistry has 416). It was demonstrably false and contradicted by data already in the same database: the page said *Dimensional Analysis → not in NCERT* while NCERT XI carries 1.4/1.5/1.6 on exactly that, and my own JEE ruling cites them as `full`. **`AlignmentTable` now takes `ncertMapped`**, derived from the payload already in hand, and renders **"not mapped yet"** when a subject has no such edge — with the caption switching to say a blank is *an absence of review, not a finding*. Chemistry is untouched.
  - **THREE EDGES, and only one had been authored.** (A) exam subtopic → both books — 502 rows, done 2026-08-04. (B) NCERT section → State Board — 0. (C) State Board section → per-exam status — 0, which is why every cell of the chapter matrix showed "?". Naming them separately is what made the fix tractable; "the tables are stale" would have sent me looking in the wrong place.
  - **(C) was DERIVED, not authored — 1,346 rows, no new judgement.** `derive-board-status.ts`: a State Board section cited by a live exam subtopic is required by that exam. Two deliberate conservatisms, both learned the hard way this week: the verdict is **`partial`, never `full`** (a pointer proves the exam asks *something* in that section, not that all of it is needed), and **an uncited section gets NO ROW** rather than `not`, because "no exam cites it" conflates *not required* with *not sampled by the bank* — writing `not` there would be exactly the confident unreviewed verdict of [[default-becomes-assertion]]. The script **refuses to overwrite an existing column** without `--force`; verified it fires on Chemistry, whose 4,315 rows were hand-authored years earlier and would have been destroyed.
  - **(B) was AUTHORED — 238 top-level NCERT sections, five agents, every verdict from book text.** 232 full · 5 partial · 1 not. The alignment table went from **0 NCERT cells to 340** (of 414 rows), and the matrix's CBSE column filled by inverting the same edge. Every falsifiable claim was re-run by the reviewer and matched exactly (`banked` 15, `Aristotle` 5, `heat engine` 75 vs 13, `blackbody` 56 vs 6, `stationary wave` 46); one agent overstated a single count (`magnetisation` "zero" in the State Board chapter — actually 6 against 14 for the -z- form) and the note was corrected before commit.
  - **A silent-misapplication bug caught in `commit-bank-rulings.ts` BEFORE it ran.** `bySection` was keyed on `section_no` alone — safe for an exam spine, where `JEE-001` is globally unique, but **NCERT has a section "1.1" in Std XI *and* Std XII, and both are titled "Introduction"**. Half the rulings would have landed on the wrong year's row, and the subtopic-name guard could not have seen it because the names match. Now keyed by `class|section_no`, with a ruling able to carry `class`; where it does not, an ambiguous `section_no` is a **loud refusal** rather than a silent pick. All three Chemistry files re-validate byte-identical (298/244/94).
  - **What the mapping shows.** The books are organised very differently and a chapter-title comparison would miss nearly all of it: **Gauss's law is taught a year earlier** in the State Board (XI:10.8); electrostatics, current electricity, magnetism and semiconductors each **split across both years**; vectors live in a **Mathematical Methods** chapter NCERT has no counterpart for; friction is in **Mechanical Properties of Solids**; Work/Energy/Power has **no chapter at all**, folded into Laws of Motion; and **transformers are taught in Electromagnetic Induction, not the AC chapter** — independently reconfirming the 2026-08-04 finding from the JEE side. Genuine State Board gaps: **Power** (no section defines it; `kilowatt` and `horsepower` are ZERO), **rotational equilibrium / principle of moments / mechanical advantage** (all ZERO — corroborating yesterday's NDA "Simple Machines" partial), **applications of elastic behaviour** (`girder`, `buckling` ZERO), the **reflecting telescope** (`Cassegrain` ZERO) and **C = 3R for solids** (`Dulong` ZERO in both). Against those the State Board is the fuller book on Reynolds number, the hydrostatic paradox, blackbody radiation, heat engines, the cyclotron, the toroid, metre bridge and potentiometer, hysteresis, and the coefficient of restitution.
  - **The -s-/-z- spelling split was confirmed three more times** and is now unambiguous: `quantisation`/`quantization`, `magnetisation`/`magnetization`, `polarisation`/`polarization` — each NCERT-only in one form and State-Board-only in the other. Plus naming traps that would each have produced a false `not`: `law of inertia`, `relaxation time`, `mirror formula`, `power of a lens`, `forbidden` band and `equivalent solenoid` are all ZERO in the State Board while the content is taught under other words. See [[corpus-search-for-coverage-rulings]] + [[syllabus-map]].

- **2026-08-04 — Chemistry's MHT-CET and NDA spines ADJUDICATED for the first time: 169 subtopics / 2,427 PYQ, 338 cited link rows. 14 of NDA's 47 State Board verdicts (30%) were wrong, and every one of the 169 had been displayed as reviewed coverage having never been assessed.** Follows the table generalisation below, which exposed the problem: those two spines had a verdict for every subtopic and ZERO section citations.
  - **THE DEFECT: `ingest-exam-spine.ts` carries 226 authored rulings for JEE Mains and ZERO for MHT-CET and NDA, and defaults an unruled subtopic to `full`.** So all 169 read green. The generalisable lesson: **a default that is defensible for the case its author had in mind silently becomes an assertion for every case they did not**, and a green cell cannot tell you which it is. This is the same failure Phase 3a refused to ship for Physics, already shipped one subject over.

  - **THE DEFECT, and it was shipped: "old syllabus" was computed for JEE and then applied to EVERY exam's rows, matched by chapter NAME.** Exams share chapter names freely (27 collide in this data), so JEE dropping a chapter silently marked another exam's namesake dead. On the live Chemistry page that buried **MHT-CET Solid State (133 PYQ, examined through 2025), MHT-CET Surface Chemistry (40 PYQ) and NDA Chemistry in Everyday Life (10 PYQ)** — 183 PYQ of live content flagged as history. Worse than cosmetic: `loadExamSpineSummaries` drops old rows from `live` entirely, so each exam's coverage was computed over a SUBSET of its own subtopics (MHT-CET read 114 live of 122, NDA 45 of 47). All 10 rows are status `full`, so the gap LISTS were unaffected — the corruption was in the denominators. Fixed by keying the dead set BY EXAM (`loadOldSyllabusByExam`, one scan for all exams rather than one each); the single-exam function survives as a thin wrapper so the scripts are untouched.
  - **A shared key is not a shared fact.** The general shape worth keeping: "dead" is a property of an (exam, chapter) PAIR, and any set keyed on only half of a compound fact will silently over-apply. Physics happened to be clean — its one dead JEE chapter, Communication Systems, has no namesake elsewhere — so testing on Physics alone would have shown nothing.
  - **The render gate is CITATIONS, not row count — and that call was forced by the data.** Chemistry's MHT-CET and NDA spines carry a verdict for every subtopic but **zero section pointers** (122 and 47 rows), so a row-count gate would have rendered 169 rows of blank cells reading as "the State Board teaches none of MHT-CET Chemistry" — the exact opposite of true for an exam set on that syllabus. Unmapped exams are NAMED in a one-line note instead of silently omitted, preserving the map's core distinction between *reviewed and absent* and *never looked at*. The table appears by itself once someone authors the pointers.
  - **Copy is per-exam because a blank cell MEANS something different per exam.** MHT-CET gets "full State Board coverage is what should happen, not a finding — the informative column is NCERT"; NDA gets "a blank in BOTH columns means neither book has it, not that the row is unfinished — several are Class 9/10 general science". The old-syllabus sentence is **derived from the rows** (`rows.some(r => r.oldSyllabus)`) rather than asserted per exam, so it cannot go stale in either direction — it renders for JEE and correctly vanishes for NDA and MHT-CET, neither of which has a dead chapter.

And the verification script's clash detector counted "not in the other exam's dead set" as "live for that exam", so it reported Communication Systems as live for MHT-CET and NDA, **neither of which has that chapter at all** — absence from a dead set is not evidence of liveness. Also: a literal **NUL byte** reached the source through a shell heredoc (invisible, would have survived review), and a `\n` in another heredoc collapsed to a real newline breaking a string literal — reconfirming [[heredoc-backslash-eating]]: author code through the editor, never a heredoc.
  - Verified with `smoke-page-data.ts` (extended to all three exams + the live-gap summary + the render gate), which **proves rather than asserts** that the JEE dead set is byte-identical to what the pre-fix loader returned. Physics: JEE 106 · MHT-CET 93 · NDA 52, NDA's 4 blank-in-both rows exactly as ruled. Chemistry: JEE 149 only, the other two correctly suppressed. **Owed: the browser render** — the page is auth-gated and `force-dynamic`, so there is no headless proof; an anon curl is bounced by middleware before the route compiles ([[probe-must-reach-the-code]]).

The lesson generalises: **a default that is defensible for the case its author had in mind silently becomes an assertion for every case they did not** — and a green cell cannot tell you which it is. Reusing it here would have written **251 rows asserting the State Board fully covers Physics subtopics nobody has read**, contradicting 0065's core rule that an unassessed pair is the ABSENCE of a row. It is also the one error class no probe can catch: a wrong ruling is plausible, internally consistent and unfalsifiable by tooling — unlike Phases 1-2, where every defect was checkable against the printed page. Then: Std XII's chapter-OPENER headings are plain `Bookman`, no demi/bold, so a weight-only test dropped **the first section of several chapters** (2.1, 3.11, 5.2, 12.2) while keeping the rest — so the rule needs EITHER signal (heavier weight at body size, or clearly larger at any weight). Also: `11.7THERMODYNAMIC STATE VARIABLES` has **no separator at all**, so `\s+` made the line fail to match entirely; Std XI Part_2 puts the number alone with the title on the NEXT line; `KEEP_UPPER` containing AND/OR/NOT (for logic gates) produced "Units AND Measurement"; and titles wrap across lines in both years.
  - **Span-level and plain-text reads fail on OPPOSITE things, so neither is "the right one".** Std XI sets chapter titles in small caps — one span per letter-run with no spaces — so the span join yields `COUNITSANDMEASUREMENT` with every word boundary lost, while plain text is perfect. Std XII paints each opener heading 4-5× for a drop shadow with the first letter painted apart, so plain text yields `2.1  I` ×4 and only the span read disambiguates. Each volume needs the read that survives ITS typesetting.

What exposed the rest was counts that failed to reconcile — and the reconciliation itself needed care: a crude "collect every bare N.M" probe reported massive undercounts that were **false**, because **NCERT numbers end-of-chapter EXERCISES `N.1, N.2…` identically to sections**. Only 2 of 238 top-level titles needed this; the other 75 short ones ("Work", "Viscosity", "Radioactivity") are genuinely that short.

Scoping a query needs BOTH columns: source alone merges two subjects' Ch.1, subject alone merges three books' Ch.1. The new `src/lib/syllabus/subjects.ts` therefore carries only what genuinely differs.
  - **`liveFromYear` had to be per-subject, and this is the load-bearing data finding.** The old `LIVE_FROM_YEAR = 2023` is Chemistry-calibrated: its seven rationalised chapters go silent after 2021. **Physics' rationalisation landed a cycle later — Communication Systems (63 PYQ) was still set in 2023 and has nothing since, while all 27 other JEE Physics chapters reach 2026.** Since the test is `lastYear < liveFromYear`, sharing 2023 reads a dead chapter as live; 2024 splits it 1/27 with a two-year margin. Verified live: the Physics loader returns exactly `Communication Systems`.
  - **THREE pre-existing bugs, one destructive.** `ingest-ncert-spine.ts` pruned stale rows on `source='NCERT'` with **no subject filter**, and `wanted` only ever holds the running subject's sections — so running the CHEMISTRY ingest would have deleted the whole Physics NCERT spine, rulings cascading with it. Plus `loadChapterConcepts` took no subject param (would merge two subjects' Ch.1 in the drill-down) and `gap.ts` read the table unscoped — its LINKS needed membership-filtering, not a column filter, because `syllabus_concept_exams` has no `subject` column at all.
  - **Two bugs introduced by the route change and caught in self-review**, both of which would have shipped a broken Physics page: chapter expand/collapse links were hardcoded to `/dashboard/syllabus`, which now redirects, so expanding a Physics chapter would silently bounce the reader to Chemistry (→ a subject-aware `basePath`); and the NCERT cross-year callout ("NCERT teaches Thermodynamics and Equilibrium in Class 11…") is a **counted Chemistry claim that is false for Physics** → moved to `crossYearNote` and **left unset for Physics, where absent means "not measured yet", never "the books agree"**. Writing a plausible note before counting is exactly the fabrication this map exists to avoid.
  - **`subject` is REQUIRED on all eight loaders, not defaulted** — that is what made the typechecker enumerate every caller instead of leaving silent `"Chemistry"` fallbacks. Scripts take `--subject=<key>` as a FLAG, never a positional, because several already read a positional meaning something else (`export-chapter-map-xlsx` reads argv[2] as "ncert"|"jee"|"all"); the positional readers now skip flags. An unknown subject **exits 1** rather than falling back, and the route **404s** rather than serving the Chemistry map under `/physics` — a fallback would read as "Physics has been mapped". `seed.ts` also now refuses to write when a seed file's own `subject` disagrees with the flag, since the upsert key includes `subject` and a mislabelled file would overwrite the wrong spine.
  - **Acceptance was "Chemistry must not move", proved from artifacts not reasoning:** the loaders' output diffed byte-identical against a stashed baseline (863 concepts / 32 chapters / 145 NCERT / 149 JEE / 7 old-syllabus / 5 live gaps). Build clean, 689 static pages, **623 prerendered `.html` on disk** (622 before, +1 for the new static redirect) — the [[shell-component-decaches-site]] check, confirming nothing de-cached. 82 syllabus unit tests. **Owed: the signed-in render** — `[subject]` is `ƒ` behind the middleware matcher, so an anon curl is bounced before the page compiles and proves nothing.
  - **Sources confirmed on disk before any of this** (`Physics/State_Board/Topics/Physics_11th.pdf` 223 sections/14 ch, `Physics_12th.pdf` 312/16, NCERT Physics XI+XII ~440), all with the same numbered-section structure the Chemistry extractor consumes. Physics' bank is far deeper than Chemistry's (**JEE Physics 3,482 PYQ vs Chemistry 259**). Two structural differences will shape Phase 1+: the State Board Physics book is a **two-pass spiral** (Std XI Ch.10 Electrostatics stops at Gauss; Std XII Ch.8 resumes at potential/capacitance — likewise current, magnetism, optics, semiconductors), so a chapter has two legitimate book homes and the one-dominant-chapter model hides one (`spiralChapters` flag is plumbed but UNUSED — the multi-home change is Phase 0.5, deferred until real rows exist to verify against); and the XI/XII divergence from NCERT is far larger than Chemistry's, making the `XI:`/`XII:` cross-year prefix roughly a third of rows rather than a dozen. See [[syllabus-map]].

- **2026-08-03 — The cross-book syllabus map became a product: a three-book alignment table, JEE chapters ordered along the State Board book, NCERT gaps, and every table folded behind native disclosure (merges `08c01cb` → `5a11ef4`).** The driving question is a teacher's: *"a CBSE student shows me an NCERT topic — where is it in my State Board book?"* Precision beats recall there, so most of the work was refusing to assert things the data does not support.
  - **THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: co-location is not equivalence.** NCERT and JEE both point AT the State Board, so it is tempting to join them through a shared section. Measured against the separately authored JEE→NCERT edge, that inference **agrees 129 times, INVENTS 39 and MISSES 25** — 77% correct, and a fabricated row looks exactly as authoritative as a real one. `buildAlignmentRows` therefore pairs ONLY on the authored edge and gives everything else its own row, repeating the anchor. That repetition is what buys the honesty: it removes any need to squeeze a many-to-many mapping into one cell. `scripts/syllabus/audit-alignment.ts` re-measures the split and **fails** if a paired row ever loses its backing.
  - **A verdict rolled up to a chapter is a lie waiting to happen.** The old "State Board content NOT required by exam X" view reported *Std XI Ch.8 not required by JEE* while JEE's LIVE s-Block chapter maps straight into it — the page contradicting its own JEE table one section below. Root cause was structural, not clerical: that view read the State Board spine's per-concept `status`, authored BEFORE the `covered_by` mappings, and nothing kept the two directions in agreement. A probe found **33 concepts marked "not required" that a JEE subtopic points at** (16 from live chapters). Rather than patch 16 rulings and leave two datasets free to drift, the rollup view was **deleted** and the surviving gap list reads from the mappings directly, so the contradiction cannot recur. **Those 16 stale `status` rows are still in the DB** — inert today, but any future view reading that column inherits the defect.
  - **Ordering: whole chapters along the book, never individual rows.** Grouping ROWS by State Board chapter reads down the book a teacher teaches but shatters "what does JEE ask in Amines" across the table; alphabetical keeps chapters whole but says nothing. Ordering whole CHAPTERS by their *dominant* State Board chapter (by PYQ weight, ties to the earlier chapter) keeps both. Dominance is deliberately not the earliest pointer: d-/f-Block touches Std XI Ch.2 with one subtopic but holds 39 questions in Std XII Ch.8.
  - **Two blanks that look identical mean different things.** "not in NCERT" is a checked claim (135 of 145 hand-verified); "not asked in the bank" only means no past question has been sampled. Worded differently on purpose — identical wording would quietly overstate the second.
  - **`/questions` prerender failures FIXED at the cause.** The query is ~13ms on an existing index; the failures were **contention** from 317 pages generating at once, and the 60s `staticPageGenerationTimeout` was SIGTERMing pages **mid-retry**, turning a recovering page into a hard build failure. `experimental.cpus: 4` + `staticPageGenerationTimeout: 180` in `next.config.mjs` took it from 4–6 statement timeouts + 2 SIGTERMs per build to **zero of both across two consecutive builds**. Closes the 2026-08-01 SUGGESTIONS item.
  - **37 of 47 `Organic Reaction Mechanisms` questions reclassified.** The catch-all was not laziness: those stems carry no topic signal (the chemistry sits in an image), so ingest agents bucketed rather than guessed. The **authored solution text** was the signal and was already present. 10 stay put — 4 Match-Lists, 2 genuinely three-chapter, 4 whose solutions are too thin. Paper JSONs written FIRST (they are the source of record; a DB-only fix is reverted by the next resync), then the DB **by primary key** — matching on `source_file` scanned 24k rows × 37 and timed out mid-run.
  - **Page size: 1,112 rendered rows → ~40.** All eight tables now sit behind native `<details>`, not a JS accordion — the page stays fully server-rendered, gets keyboard/screen-reader behaviour free, and browsers skip layout for the collapsed subtree. Each summary carries its row count. Known limit recorded in the component: Chrome/Edge auto-expand a closed `<details>` on Ctrl+F, **Firefox and Safari do not**.
  - **I reported a measurement as fact and it was wrong.** I sized the page at 855 rows having counted only chapter rows in the two matrices, missing that every top-level section renders under its chapter (`return [chapterRow, ...sectionRows]`). Real figures: 121 and 170, page total 1,112. The first collapse commit therefore left 323 rows visible, not the 66 I claimed. Corrected in the follow-up commit and in [[probe-must-reach-the-code]] — **count what the render emits, not what the data holds.**
  - **Migration 0066 was applied to production via MCP but its `.sql` file was never written** — found during this doc pass, recreated 2026-08-03 (idempotent). A fresh checkout would have lacked `covered_by`, which the entire feature depends on. The convention is append-only *files*; applying through the MCP does not satisfy it.
  - See [[syllabus-map]]. Also shipped: `loadNcertGaps` (21 NCERT sections the State Board misses, 4 tagged as a hole an exam already reports from its own side, leaving **6 gaps only this view surfaces**), the Std XII Chemistry syllabus tracker (16 chapters / 159 subtopics, State-Board-sourced with 6 NCERT plugs), and a Biomolecules data fix — `14.9 "shows Haworth formula of maltose"` was a figure caption parsed as a section; deleted after confirming zero pointers, and a probe found no others of that class.

The answer states that rather than supplying a plausible case name, which is the single easiest invention in the whole batch.
  - **The grounding probe was sharpened three times by its own false positives, each fix strictly noise-reducing and TDD'd** (`tests/mh-ssc-10-text-grounding.test.ts`, 12 cases): a capitalised run may CONTAIN a lowercase connector but never END on one (so "UNESCO for" was being tested as a unit and reported missing while UNESCO sat in the chapter); the all-stopword filter compared case-sensitively, so the lowercase "the" admitted by that same connector rule let pure glue like "So the" through; and a GFM pipe-table cell is a sentence boundary, without which one concept-map answer contributed five bogus "names" (*Casts*, *Prepares*, …). **6 → 1 candidate on the first chapter; 5 across all four, every one a run-join artefact whose components are individually in the chapter (verified one by one) — so ZERO genuine ungrounded claims across all 48 authored answers.** The probe also caught something real: it was MY OWN MCQ justifications, not an agent's, that imported outside knowledge twice — a claim that two books were "English works" (the chapter never states a language) and a line identifying three distractor names from general knowledge. Both rewritten. The rule applies to the reviewer too.

The one figure (a rotated nested-diamond concept map whose labels the text layer scatters unrecoverably) was cropped, re-cropped after inspection to drop a sliver of the neighbouring question, and confirmed to leak no answer — its inner cells are the blanks. **Owed, as on every chapter of this book: a human spot-check of the derived answers.**

One figure (the Foreign Policy concept map, five empty boxes round a centre) took two re-crops — the first sliced the question heading, the second cut the bottom boxes. `/board` outlines are a single `exercise` block per chapter: this book has **no solved-example bucket at all**, so unlike Maths there was nothing shippable off the book's own working.
  - **Honest gaps:** 58 rows is small (a humanities chapter is 4-7pp with a one-page exercise) and all 16 chapters of this book would total ~180; several subtopics hold 1-2 questions, which resolves only as the remaining 11 chapters land; and every answer here rests on grounding discipline plus a blind MCQ pass, which is genuinely weaker than a book diff — hence the derived-provenance stamp on all 58.

- **2026-08-01 — JEE Mains PHYSICS COMPLETE: 1,845 → 3,482 q PUBLIC across 88 papers, level with Maths; ~13 wrong source keys caught; JEE bank now 0 KaTeX-broken (merges `5042d67` · `71c741a` · `3e61121`).** The ask was "ingest all remaining JEE Physics PYQs", and the user's correction — *"all papers contain physics. you will have to look into actual papers or read math extrction codebase"* — reframed the job before any code was written.
  - **THE KEY DISCOVERY: Physics was ALREADY EXTRACTED.** Extraction is subject-agnostic and only the DB *commit* filtered by subject, so ~3,685 Physics rows already sat in `out/*.records.json` from the Maths runs. The job was classify + verify, not extract. `dump-maths.ts` → **`dump-subject.ts --subject=Physics`**. Reading the pipeline (as instructed) rather than reasoning from counts is what surfaced it.
  - **The BLIND lane repeatedly justified itself.** Papers were triaged SAFE (trustworthy numbering) vs BLIND (key untrustworthy → derive every answer, ignore the key). The decisive case: **2023-feb01's ENTIRE shift-2 key block is displaced by +2**, confirmed against 18 independent derivations — trusting it would have shipped ~13 wrong answers from one paper. Twelve further single keys were proven wrong, each re-derived before acceptance: torque `[ML²T⁻²]` gives 25% not 5%; two Carnot engines in series match one ("same", not "always less"); constant velocity makes the contact force `Mg`, not `Mg cosθ`; a plane EM wave's electric and magnetic energy densities are EQUAL so the ratio is 1, not 2; Young's modulus DECREASES with temperature; 7 mA less a 1.5 mA load leaves 5.5 mA in the Zener, not 10; `a sinθ = 2λ` gives a 6e-3 rad divergence where the key read 60; AM bandwidth is `2f_m` (the booklet wrote the right expression then evaluated `2ω_c`). In nearly every case the booklet's own worked solution contradicted its own printed letter.
  - **A whole paper was nearly lost.** A completeness audit diffing every `papers/*.json` against the DB found **2023-jan30 with ZERO Physics rows** — never dispatched, and the subject would have been declared finished with a sitting missing. It had to reconcile BOTH directions: the 11 legacy 2021 papers legitimately have DB rows but no paper-file classification. → [[completeness-reconcile-both-ways]].
  - **`scan-flip` published rows it had no business touching.** It matched on `source_file` alone, but a JEE file carries all three subjects, each ingested in its own pass — so flipping Physics for 2023-Jan29 also published **Maths Q67/Q70**, which the Maths pass had deliberately withheld for corrupted options. Both restored to PRIVATE; every recorded withhold across the exam was then audited (apr10 Q171/175, jan30 Q176, jul28 Q69, Paper9 Q84, p19 Q18 — all correctly PRIVATE, Jan29 the only breach). `scan-flip` now takes `--subject`, scoping both the scan and the UPDATE, and warns on an unscoped flip. → [[scope-writes-to-your-pass]].
  - **A build failure whose obvious diagnosis was wrong.** `next build` began failing on the `/questions` landing pages with "canceling statement due to statement timeout", a DIFFERENT handful each run. The natural read was a missing index — but **EXPLAIN showed the chapter query runs in 13 ms** on an existing index. The real cause is contention: Next prerenders 300+ of those pages concurrently and this session's ~1,600 new rows tipped the burst over Postgres' `statement_timeout`. An index would have fixed nothing. `queryQuestions` now retries ONLY a cancelled statement (SQLSTATE 57014, with a message fallback since PostgREST does not always pass the code), twice with a short backoff; failing-twice → clean.
  - **Structured repairs beat prose.** The BLIND solvers were correctly diagnosing dropped-digit stems but recording the repair as *prose*, which nothing can apply — a question would have shipped with a correct answer and a still-unanswerable stem. The prompt now demands a structured `stemFix`/`optionFix`, and the applier **refuses any fragment that does not match exactly once** rather than force-applying a near-miss (~300 repairs applied). `assemble-blind` also now merges into an existing paper file instead of clobbering it (every BLIND paper already carried a shipped Maths block) and treats a row whose options were absorbed into the stem as shippable when all four labels are supplied — `commit.ts` could already synthesize them, but the assembler was dropping such rows first.
  - **Render cleanup, bank-wide:** 351 escaped fill-in blanks (`\_\_\_\_` renders literally outside math), 54 empty math zones, 19 KaTeX-breaking zones (a body ending in a lone `\`; `\text{∮}` → `\oint`), and finally 8 Maths rows where pandoc split a set `\{…\}` across zones and orphaned the braces — reconstructed by hand, then **persisted into the paper files as overrides** so a later `resync` is a no-op rather than a silent revert (→ [[persist-fix-to-source-of-record]]). **KaTeX-broken: 47 → 0 of 7,436**; render-corruption 221 → 6.
  - **Judgement calls made AGAINST the agents, in both directions.** Rejected jan31 Q22 (its uniqueness argument only tried integer thicknesses; `K = t/(t−1)` is equally clean for t = 1.5, 4/3, 1.25) and Q92 (its own note conceded the opposite reading gives another option) — jan31 being the one paper with **no solution document at all**, so it ran under a stricter brief (double-derive, falsify distractors, per-row confidence, skip readily). Conversely I nearly rejected p24 Q29, whose *stated* justification was an aesthetic "drop-pattern" prior — until the booklet's own working showed `250 + 150 = 400`. → [[classify-findings-by-evidence]] sharpened: an agent's stated reasoning is not its evidence, in either direction.


### 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-29 — archived 2026-08-11

Every one of the five History sittings split **23 History / 11 Political Science** and summed to the printed 40 marks, so the model held across years, not just on the pilot.

The reason is mechanical, not stylistic: **`content_hash` is computed from the stem, so a translated row can never dedup against the real English paper and would permanently duplicate the sitting.** `config.ts` records the reasoning inline so a later session does not re-add the years blindly.

The prescribed Balbharati textbook settles it verbatim — *"Thus, it is said that Voltaire was the founder of modern historiography"* — and the board question is copied word-for-word from that chapter's own exercise. Fixed via the existing `scripts/grounding/apply-key-fix.ts` (collision-guarded `content_hash` recompute) in the DB **and** the source JSON. Of its 5 hits, 1 was the real conflict, 2 were false positives (punctuation; two genuinely different questions sharing four options — *cheapest* mode vs *most common in Brazil*, both correct), 2 genuinely agreed. See [[cross-paper-stem-consistency]].

Two real catches: the 2020 pyramid first cropped without its title or X-axis scale, which `Q6(B)(5)` ("percentage of female aged 55-59") cannot be answered without; and a skewed scan whose instruction line dips below its own row-average band, so excluding it would have crossed into the map's top border — a sliver of instruction text is the better trade. **`attach-images.ts` is now size-aware**: 4× is right for a small geometry diagram, but near-full-page maps and dense graph-paper grids blew past the 1 MB storage cap, so it steps the render scale down and falls back to JPEG; small figures still take the 4× PNG path unchanged.

History and Political Science are two bank subjects **sharing one parent folder** (the board prints them as one paper) and both number chapters from 01, so the dir PREFIX is the only thing separating their output paths — hence two distinct helpers and a test asserting the routing. The explicit-registry choice paid again: the bank spells the Historiography chapters with a colon while the folders use an underscore.

- **2026-07-29 — THE SITE HAD NEVER CACHED A SINGLE PAGE. Root-caused to `AppHeader`, fixed, and 622 pages now prerender — plus `/questions`, 317 indexable per-chapter landing pages (merges `ae0fbed` + `a9b9a08`).** Started as "analyse this Vercel Active-CPU chart", ended as the largest perf/SEO finding in the project's history. Three shipped pieces, in the order they were discovered.
  - **The chart read (4h 03m Active CPU / 30 days, ~95% of the Hobby allowance, run-rate doubling).** Cross-referencing Web Analytics gave the number that mattered: **7,638 page views ⇒ ≈1.9 SECONDS of Active CPU per page view**, against a 50–200ms norm, on only ~255 views/day. Composition: function 94.2% / middleware 5.8% (so the [[middleware-auth-scope]] fix HELD — middleware is no longer the cost), nodejs 89.6% / edge 10.4%, iad1 92.2%. **The `edge` line minus the `middleware` line ≈ 11m/month is the seven `opengraph-image.tsx` routes** (`runtime="edge"`, satori+resvg — CPU-dense, cache busted per deploy); the non-iad1 regions ≈ that same edge work running near the viewer, which is a LATENCY signal (users in India, functions in Virginia), NOT a cost one, since Active CPU excludes I/O wait. **Rule banked: Active CPU counts CPU, not waiting — so DB-latency work does not move this meter; only doing fewer renders does.**
  - **Level 1 — `/browse` per-request work.** It resolved the viewer THREE times (`getSessionMember` + `getSessionUser` + `getSessionSuperadmin`, each with its own client and its own `auth.getUser()`, sequentially) and re-fetched the exam/subject/chapter/subtopic lists for every visitor. Now one `getPageIdentity()` with a **free cookie-name short-circuit** (no Supabase cookie ⇒ no session ⇒ zero auth work, the path most traffic takes), plus `unstable_cache` on the taxonomy reads. **Deliberately NOT cached: `get_chapter_facets`/`get_subtopic_facets`/`get_pyq_years`/the question list** — all four are `security invoker` (0019/0020/0037), so caching them against the anon client would hide staff's own PRIVATE rows from their filter counts. Visibility is untouched: the question query still runs on the cookie-bound client, and the identity booleans only drive UI.
  - **Level 2 — `/questions`, 317 per-chapter landing pages.** Every question sat behind a UUID query string and the sitemap offered Google **exactly one URL** (`/browse`) for ~24k questions; analytics showed **~196 of 7,638 page views (2.5%) arriving from Google search**. Now `/questions/<exam>/<subject>/<chapter>` for every chapter with ≥15 PUBLIC questions, plus a `/questions` crawl hub and 318 sitemap entries. Slugs are **derived** from taxonomy names (DB stays the source of truth; a new chapter gets a page free) with `dedupeBySlug` guaranteeing one-URL-one-page, and names with no ASCII letters (future Marathi/Hindi subjects) yielding an empty slug that is **skipped rather than romanised**. Counts come from the existing `get_chapter_facets` aggregate, never row-counting (the 1000-row cap). `landingFilterParams()` is the single definition of "which questions is this page about", feeding both the page query and its `/browse` deep link so they cannot disagree. **Routing conflict on the way:** Next forbids two differently-named dynamic segments at the same position, so `/questions/[id]/edit` blocked `/questions/[examSlug]/…` → **the admin editor moved to `/dashboard/questions/[id]/edit`** (where admin surfaces belong) with a **config-level** 308 for bookmarks — config rather than a route file precisely so it doesn't recreate the conflict. `robots.txt` then dropped its blanket `/questions` disallow, which existed only for that editor and would otherwise have hidden all 317 pages.
  - **THE FINDING — discovered only because the new pages refused to prerender.** `AppHeader` renders on every page and resolved the session + read the `qb_exam` cookie during server render. Both are per-request, so **every route was dynamic: zero prerendered HTML files existed, and `revalidate` on 77 notes chapters / 10 guides / the homepage / the mock catalogue had never once taken effect.** The build's route table hid it — a route with `generateStaticParams` still prints `●` even when every prerender bailed. Fixed by moving all per-visitor state to the browser (`HeaderBar` client island + a no-store `/api/me/header`), leaving only the **slug→exam-uuid map** on the server because it is public taxonomy identical for every visitor. **Result: 622 prerendered pages** (456 notes + 113 guide + 40 landing + …); `/notes` and `/guide` now serve `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` in 16–236ms; a landing page goes 458ms → **13ms** on its second hit. `/browse` stays dynamic by design (searchParams).
  - **Caching is a CORRECTNESS change, so the leak gate was the hard gate.** A cached page is one copy served to everyone — a header holding an email would hand it to the next visitor. Proved from the artifacts rather than by reasoning: swept every prerendered `.html` **and `.rsc`** → **0 org names, 0 "Sign out", 0 staff-only Papers tab, 0 session emails** (the only addresses present are the deliberate public contact address and a form placeholder), and confirmed `/dashboard`, `/me`, `/account`, `/saved`, `/upload`, `/uploads`, `/superadmin` all still render per-request.
  - **Two silent breakages the change forced** (both now in Recurring pitfalls): `ExamPill`'s `router.refresh()` would have stopped working on a cached page (a refresh re-serves the same copy), and `useSearchParams()` in `QuestionList`'s bookmark button **bails a static prerender to client rendering**, which was silently costing the landing pages their caching until a `<Suspense>` boundary was added.
  - **Retro-invalidates a prior fix:** the 2026-06-27 egress work bumped `revalidate` 3600→86400 on 208 pages — but no page was ever ISR-cached, so that lever was almost certainly a **no-op** for full-route caching (the calmer `/browse` sitemap entry was the part that could have helped). Any egress improvement then should be re-attributed. **Owed:** a signed-in browser click-through — the authed header has no headless proof in this repo. See [[shell-component-decaches-site]] + [[next-caching-traps]] + [[public-landing-pages]].

Shipped through the existing single seam: pure `formatSourceTag` → `buildQuestionPaper({includeSourceTag})` → `options.includeSourceTag` on `/api/export` (paper branch only) → a checkbox on both download surfaces (`/browse` DownloadDialog + the paper-builder `PaperDownload`). No migration, no query change — `QuestionRow` already carried `exam.name` + `pyqYear`.

So **a null year IS the "not a PYQ" gate** — a mixed paper tags its PYQs and never credits a practice question to a sitting it never appeared in, with no `question_kind` plumbing on the view-model.
  - **Exam + year only, and that was a data decision not a taste one.** `pyq_note` is a clean label only for NDA (`"NDA 1"`/`"NDA 2"`); within JEE the SAME column holds `"Paper 7"` AND `"29 June 2022"` AND `"8 Apr 2023"`, and MH-SSC-10 stores a 45-char provenance sentence. Deliberately NOT `formatProvenance` (the web card's `Q# · disambiguator · year` chip), which would print `[Q12 · Apr · 2023]` on a printed paper.

  - **Then the user's screenshot exposed a layout bug that was NOT mine but which my third checkbox tripped.** `DownloadDialog`'s scrolling body was missing **`min-h-0`**: a flex item's default `min-height:auto` refuses to shrink below its content, so the body never clipped, the dialog outgrew `max-h-[90dvh]`, and the `sticky bottom-0` footer rode UP over the tail of the content — swallowing "Group by subtopic" and stranding the new checkbox below the buttons. Fixed with `min-h-0` + dropping the `sticky` (the footer sits outside the scroll area, so it is always visible anyway and `sticky` only bought the overlap). Separately the 4-button footer never fit `max-w-lg`, drawing "Done" **outside** the dialog's left edge → `sm:max-w-xl` + `sm:flex-wrap` (same wrap fix on `PaperDownload`, which has the identical footer). See [[mobile-render-gotchas]].

Same family as the ƒ-page pitfall but a distinct trigger; the "Recurring pitfalls" bullet now covers interaction-gated components, and [[probe-must-reach-the-code]] is sharpened. The .docx itself WAS verified beyond fixtures (built the same 11 real bank rows both ways → 9 tags, both practice rows clean).

- **2026-07-27 — JEE Maths SUBTOPIC drift cleaned: 8 synonym merges, 127 → 113 subtopics, 3,687 q preserved exactly.** The 2026-07-24 reshape fixed JEE Maths at CHAPTER level but left subtopics, and the 2021 vs 2024+ ingest waves had classified the same material under different names. Merged (all within-chapter, so no `chapter_id` touched): Binomial Theorem's **4-way** remainder cluster (*Remainder and Divisibility* / *Divisibility and Remainders* / *Remainder Problems* / *Divisibility*) → 9 · AoD *Mean Value Theorem* → *Rolle's and Mean Value Theorems* 7 · PnC *Inclusion-Exclusion Counting* → *Counting with Inclusion-Exclusion* 5 · Probability's 3 *Random Variables …* buckets → *…and Distributions* 8 · Quadratic *Modulus Equations* → *Equations with Absolute Value* 24 · Mathematical Reasoning *Logical Connectives* + *Compound Statements* → *Tautology and Logical Connectives* 36 · Straight Lines *Orthocentre* + *Centroid* → *Coordinate Geometry of Triangles* 12 · Conics *Tangents to a Parabola* + *Normals to a Parabola* → *Tangents and Normals* 35. Integrity verified: **3,687 q preserved · 0 empty subtopics · 0 chapter/subtopic mismatches** (the 1 NULL `subtopic_id` is the pre-existing PRIVATE Paper-11 Matrices row, an untouched chapter). Reparent-then-delete order per [[fk-set-null-on-subtopic-drop]]; blast radius is the `/browse` dropdown only (JEE Maths has no notes/guide/mocks/concept-tags).
  - **The load-bearing part is the two clusters NOT merged — sampling stems refuted the drift hypothesis for both.** **3D Geometry's `The Plane` (70) vs `Line and Plane` (47)** looked like textbook drift (70/0 year cliff) but the names carve at a REAL joint: plane-only work (three planes, plane through a line of intersection, mirror image in a plane) vs line↔plane interaction (distance measured parallel to a line, foot of perpendicular on a line). The cliff is a **classification-preference shift** in the later ingest wave, not synonymy — merging would have destroyed a genuine distinction. **Binomial Theorem's coefficient trio** (*Coefficient Sums* 52 / *Coefficients and Series* 25 / *Coefficients* 17) genuinely overlaps, but a merge is the wrong remedy: *Coefficients and Series* is a catch-all holding **misfiled number-theory questions** (`3ⁿ+7ⁿ` multiple of 10) and *Coefficients* holds a remainder question — they need per-question reclassification, not a rename-merge. **Rule: a duplicate-looking subtopic name is a hypothesis; read stems from each before merging** (the catch-all-chapters pitfall, one level down). Both deferred in SUGGESTIONS.

- **2026-07-27 — NEW axis: the cross-exam SYLLABUS-FIT screen (migration 0062) — JEE Mains questions served as practice to NDA+CET students; first chapter screened 251 q → 239 usable · 12 dropped.** LWS teaches NDA and MHT-CET students and wants JEE Mains PYQs as *stretch practice*. So JEE is a **question SOURCE, not an audience**, and the only question that matters is: *can a student taught the NDA ∪ CET syllabus solve this?* That is prerequisite-coverage, **not** resemblance — an early framing measured "does NDA ask it this way", which would have wrongly discarded all 82 JEE parameter-consistency questions that NDA never *asks* that way but every NDA student can *answer*.
  - **The union is wide, so this is an EXCLUSION job, not an inclusion job.** NDA covers what CET drops (Height & Distance, Properties of Triangle, Binomial Theorem, Binary, Logarithms, deep Conics); CET covers what NDA drops (Mathematical Logic ↔ JEE's Mathematical Reasoning, Linear Programming, Cayley-Hamilton, Pair of Straight Lines, heavy Line & Plane). Together they cover nearly all of JEE Maths. **Matrices+Determinants: 239 of 251 pass (95%)**, and the 12 drops reduce to just **four tools** — similarity/conjugation (6), 3×3 Cayley-Hamilton (2), eigenvalues (2), 3×3 nilpotent shift + the XᵀAX skew test (1 each).
  - **Two sub-results worth keeping.** *All 82 linear-systems questions pass* — they look like the chapter's hardest ("has infinitely many solutions, then 13αβ =") but NDA teaches *Finding the parameter for consistency* as an explicit notes concept; JEE only wraps a composite output around it. And *all 104 non-system determinant questions pass, zero drops* — **NDA's determinant coverage is deeper than JEE's own notes chapter** (Vandermonde, cyclic, differentiating a determinant, sums of determinants, the full adjoint ladder).
  - **The data model is the load-bearing decision: store the EXCEPTIONS, not the verdicts.** A verdict row per question would be 251 rows to say "fine" 239 times. Instead: a 12-row exclusion table (0062) + a **reviewed-scope registry in TS** (`REVIEWED_CHAPTERS`, pinned by chapter **UUID** — the /notes+/guide name-joins are exactly what rots on a rename). This keeps **three states distinct**, which is the whole point: *passed* · *dropped* · *never looked at*. Collapsing the third into "passed" would hand students unvetted questions; into "dropped" would empty the bank. `fitCoverage()` surfaces it as an inline caveat instead of silence. It also matches the direction rulings actually move: the user loosened twice mid-session (trace IN, then 2×2 Cayley-Hamilton + nilpotent IN), and **loosening is mechanical here** — delete the rows carrying that `blocking_tool`.
  - **Verdicts judge what a question DEMANDS, not what our stored solution USES — and a keyword screen would over-reject ~3×.** `5c5efe8a` is solved in the bank via eigenvectors, but `(A−I)B = 0` with `B ≠ 0` forces `det(A−I) = 0` ⇒ `ad−bc = a+d−1`; `b29d23c8`/`2d6ac41f` are solved "by similarity" but `det(P⁻¹MP) = det M` follows from `det(AB)=det(A)det(B)` alone. All pass. This is why the screen cannot be automated.
  - **Surface + tooling:** `/browse` gains a **Syllabus fit** segmented control (`All JEE · NDA+CET · Excluded`) rendered **only when the exam is JEE Mains** — meaningless elsewhere, since a question already belongs to its own exam's students. The `Excluded` view exists so the teacher can audit my calls. `scripts/relevance/commit.ts` (dry-run default, validates every `blocking_tool` against `BLOCKING_TOOLS` and every id against the bank before writing, idempotent upsert) + `data/<screen>.json`. **Screening a new chapter needs BOTH steps** — commit its exclusions AND append the chapter to `REVIEWED_CHAPTERS`; the script prints the reminder. Verified live on `/browse` (251 / 239 / 12; bank-wide delta exactly 12; control hidden off-JEE; unscoped caveat renders) — the build alone proves nothing for a `ƒ` route. See [[syllabus-fit-screen]] + [[spec-narrower-than-artifact]].

- **2026-07-27 — Answer-key cross-check of 11 shipped MH-SSC-10 papers against the OFFICIAL solutions bundled inside their own source PDFs: 295 q → 279 AGREE · 14 BOOK-WRONG · 1 NO-BOOK-ANSWER · 1 BOTH-DEFENSIBLE · **0 OURS-WRONG** (merged `0853039`).** These papers shipped under the pipeline's "board QPs never ship an answer key" assumption, so every MCQ key was AI-DERIVED and every subjective answer AUTHORED, all `reviewFlag:true` awaiting a human check that never happened. A text-layer scan of all 69 Class-10 source PDFs found a `"Board Paper – <year> Solution"` section in **18** — the publisher's reproductions bundle the official key. 11 of those are already-ingested papers (Algebra 2016-2019, Geometry 2016-2019, Science I 2016/2018/2019); the Algebra/Geometry **2020** hits were FALSE POSITIVES (an inline `Solution:` belonging to a *complete-the-activity* question), so their answers stay derived.
  - **The finding is the asymmetry, not the count: not one of our 295 stored answers needed changing, while the publisher's key is wrong 14×.** Auto-applying the printed key would have CORRUPTED 14 correct answers. The brief's load-bearing rule — **the printed key is a PEER, not an ORACLE** — did the work; so did its corollary, *where a printed worked solution contradicts its printed final answer, the working is the better evidence* (3 of geo-2017's 4 errors are exactly that shape, self-evident from internal contradiction alone). Sharpest: **geo-2017 Q4(ii)** where the printed solution **fabricates its coefficients** (`4x = 12cosec+12cot` when multiplying gives `+16cot`) so the cot terms cancel — correct identity `(3x+4y)²−(4x−3y)²=625`, and the printed one fails numerically at θ=30°; **alg-2019 Q5(ii)** adds the two filling TIMES (times don't add, rates do) and is self-refuting; **alg-2017 Q3(ii)** factorises `3x²−12x` as `3x(x−12)`, and substituting its root 12 gives 208≠0.
  - **Applied: 14 `[Textbook answer-key error:]` + 2 `[Textbook note:]` brackets + 1 wording repair — all SOLUTION-ONLY, therefore hash-neutral by construction** (`solution` feeds neither `contentHash` nor `subjectiveContentHash`), so no recompute and no collision risk; verified idempotent. New `scripts/mh-ssc-10/`: `CROSSCHECK_BRIEF.md`, `dump-answers.ts` (**refuses to dump a paper with unanswered rows** — a cross-check against empty answers reports a meaningless all-AGREE, the bug that wasted a State-Board pass), `apply-errata.ts`, per-paper `data/<id>.crosscheck.json`.
  - **Two hazards banked into the brief mid-run, each of which would otherwise have manufactured false OURS-WRONG findings:** (1) **the PDF text layer silently DROPS MINUS SIGNS inside math zones** (a printed `x = −2` extracts as `x = 2`; also dropped from coordinates and determinants) → never call a sign disagreement without rendering the page; (2) **`render.ts` `rmSync`s the paper's `out/` dir** before rendering, destroying any `text.md`/`answers.md` dumps sitting there. Also: a Unicode match string (`∠`) silently found nothing where the DB stores LaTeX (`\angle`) and reported "already correct" — verify a no-op before believing it.
  - **Coverage gap found, NOT fixed (logged in SUGGESTIONS):** geo-2016 and geo-2018 are each missing their `Q5(ii)` construction sub-question (stored refs jump `Q5(i)`→`Q5(iii)`); geo-2017 and geo-2019 have theirs, so it is 2 specific questions, not systematic. Source + official solution both in hand; adding them is purely additive. See [[mh-ssc-10-ingestion]] + [[audit-probe-symmetry]].

- **2026-07-27 — Two student reports on a Class-10 Statistics question traced to a literal `\n`, which uncovered a year-old render-contract drift in the Word exporter (merged `cd97550`, `7bf32b9`).** The reports read as "typo-or-formatting"; the actual cause was that the stem and solution stored a **two-character literal `\n`** where line breaks belonged, so `parseTableBlocks` never saw line structure and the GFM pipe-table collapsed into raw pipes. Both are Statistics questions whose **data IS the table**, so they were unanswerable. Content was verified correct against the source PDF (values, structure, answers all match) ⇒ a meaning-preserving unescape, **not** a re-transcription.
  - **Root cause was two failures compounding:** the alg-2020 transcription agent double-escaped its newlines when writing its JSON (the committed source file is itself wrong — 23 of 27 rows, zero real newlines), and **`scripts/mh-ssc-10/commit.ts` never called `normalizeNewlines`** (7 of 12 commit pipelines didn't). Fixed at the choke point: `commitStaged` now **rejects** rather than silently normalises — see the write-boundary convention + [[reject-dont-normalise-when-hash-upstream]].
  - **The bigger defect the report uncovered:** `parseTableBlocks` was wired into the docx **stem** and **context** paths but never the **solution** path, so a table in any solution printed as raw pipes in every downloaded answer key — **123 PUBLIC rows bank-wide**, 5× the reported blast radius. The web renderer had the identical bug and was fixed 2026-07-06; the exporter was never brought along. Fixed via `solutionBlocks` + a **render-CONTRACT golden test** asserting the same fixture through both surfaces.
  - **Repaired 24 rows** (22 alg-2020 + 2 State Board Mathematical Logic), 4 collision-guarded `content_hash` recomputes, **0 collisions**; source JSONs fixed in the same pass so re-commit stays idempotent. Then `npm run audit:text` (new standing probe) found a **second, unrelated class** on its first run — 7 PUBLIC rows with pipe rows and no `|---|` separator — repaired 2026-07-27 with **two different remedies for one flag class**: the MHT-CET band-gap row is a real table missing its separator (restored), but the 6 Pariksha rows are label→text statement lists with **no header row**, where adding a separator would promote "Statement I" into a table HEADER — those were **linearised** per the NDA-Statistics house style (240 of its 241 rows linearise rather than tabulate). Bank-wide now 0/0.
  - **The probe took three attempts and the first two would have reported wrong numbers** — banked in [[stem-render-corruption-probes]]: Postgres `LIKE` treats backslash as its own escape char so `'%\n%'` silently matches the letter *n*; naive matching then flagged every `\neq`/`\nu`/`\nabla` (hundreds of false positives, incl. two matrix row-separators nearly reported as bugs); and excluding "followed by a letter" hid `\nThe`. Correct test: a backslash-n that is neither the tail of a `\\` pair nor followed by a **lowercase** letter.

- **2026-07-26 — MH-SSC-10 Science and Technology II COMPLETE: back-years 2016-2022 ingested (+204 q), the subject now spans all 10 available years (merged `07ac2db`).** Papers 2016 (24) · 2017 (34) · 2018 (24) · 2019 (41) · 2020 (41) · 2022 (40) → Science II 338 q / 337 PUBLIC / 53 figures.
  - **The load-bearing discovery: these back-years are NOT raster scans like the rest of the corpus — they are born-digital TYPESET reproductions with a real text layer** (4.7k–12.8k chars), so transcription is **hybrid** (text layer = ground truth for wording/options/numbering; rendered pages still needed for figures, flow-charts, boxed activities, reading order). New `scripts/mh-ssc-10/dump-text.ts` + a README rule: **always check for a text layer before assuming vision-only** (~0 chars ⇒ scan; a few thousand ⇒ hybrid).
  - **Source PDFs are BUNDLES and the bundling is unreliable — verify per file:** 2016/2017/2019 bundle their OWN official solution (so those keys are source-verified, not derived), but **`Science_II_2018.pdf` bundles the *Paper I 2017* solution** — wrong subject AND wrong year — and only 2 of its 8 pages are the question paper (marks reconcile to 40, so complete at 24 q).
  - **2016-2019 are OLD-syllabus:** Paper II was not Biology-only (chemistry half + the dropped *Control and Co-ordination* chapter) and the **MCQ block is Q1(B), inverted** from the modern layout; the Science II catalog gained 4 old-syllabus chapters following the identical block already established for Science I. `sci2-2017 Q3(1)` is held **PRIVATE** — it says "label the following diagram" and no such diagram exists anywhere in the PDF.
  - **All 30 new figure crops montage-verified individually**, which exposed a real tool limitation now in `scripts/lib/figures/README.md`: **snapCrop's `INK = 165` threshold cannot see pale art**, so it clips pastel line-work and light-gray blank chart boxes **while still reporting `ok`** — because `ok` only means the anchors sat in whitespace gaps, not that the crop is complete. Two agents hit it independently on different papers; one lost an entire blank box the question was asking about. See [[figure-snapcrop-verify]] + [[mh-ssc-10-ingestion]].

- **2026-07-25 — JEE Mains 2026 Maths ingested: all 19 Jan+April per-shift sittings → +475 q PUBLIC (380 MCQ + 95 NAT); JEE Maths 3,202 → 3,677.** A fresh `PYQs\2026\` folder (19 QP+`_ak` pairs) appeared. Ran the **SAFE lane** (the 2026 `_ak` files are full worked-solution docs with the answer key as the leading `**(x)**` token + clean sequential 1–75 numbering — the ideal number-matched case): per file `extract --numeric --layout2025` → `dump-maths` → 1 classify+VERIFY agent/file (25 Maths q each: classify into the live taxonomy + INDEPENDENTLY re-derive every key) → `assemble-safe` → `commit --subject=Maths` → `attach-solutions` → `cleanup-latex` → `scan-flip --flip`. Pilot-first (24 Jan S1), then batched the rest as background agents. **The load-bearing structural difference from 2021–2025: 2026 sittings are PER-SHIFT files of 75 q** (Physics 1–25 · Chem 26–50 · **Maths 51–75 = 20 MCQ + 5 NAT**), not the two-shift 180-q date files; `--layout2025` forces `shiftSize=75` so a standalone 75-block file maps Q51–75 → Maths correctly.
  - **5 genuine source answer-key errors caught + corrected by the SAFE verification** (apr05-s2 Q54 C→B, Q57 C→B, Q67 B→C; apr06-s2 Q58 C→B; apr05-s1 Q54 A→B) — in **every** case the official key LETTER contradicted the answer key's OWN worked solution (e.g. apr05-s2 Q67's AK literally writes "3 points of intersection" but marks (b)=2; apr06-s2 Q58's AK derives "x²−41x+420=0" but marks (c)). Adjudicated each with three independent grounds — my own derivation + the agent's + the AK's printed worked solution — before flipping (reconfirms [[audit-probe-symmetry]]: the AK key letter is a peer, not an oracle; the AK's own worked solution is the tiebreaker). All other 14 sittings: 0 key disagreements. Final **`audit:keys Maths 2026` = 380 MCQ, 0 flagged**; all 475 rows KaTeX-clean.
  - **Two durable pipeline fixes folded in (net-new work, no 360 needed):** (1) **trailing-backslash key parser** — 2026 pandoc renders the key as `**(c)\**` (a hard-break `\` before the closing `**`) on ~5–10 rows/file, which `parseAnswerTokens`/`SOLUTION_START`'s `\)\*\*` didn't match → those keys silently dropped to `no_answer_key`. Added an optional `\\?` before `\*\*` in both regexes (`scripts/jee/lib.ts`) — a **strict superset** (2021–2025 blocks without the `\` still match, verified by typecheck + 61 green tests incl. a new regression case). Recovered nearly all keys (per-file `no_answer_key` dropped ~30→5 across the batch), so `assemble-safe` could cross-check the agent vs the source key rather than blind-trust the derivation. (2) **stale-taxonomy guard** — the pipeline's `out/_maths_taxonomy.txt` handout predated the 2026-07-24 chapter reshape, so agents classified into RETIRED names (Integrals/Compound Angles/Trigonometry/Continuity and Differentiability) → commit would have re-created the dead chapters. **Regenerated the handout from the live DB** + added a per-file classification validator (checks every `(chapter,subtopic)` against a live-taxonomy JSON before commit, aborts on any mismatch). Net: JEE Maths chapters stayed at **27, 0 duplicates created, 0 empty**. **Lesson: always regenerate the agent classification handout from the live DB before an agent-classification batch — a stale handout silently re-creates renamed chapters** (a taxonomy-drift cousin of [[shipped-chapter-rename-downstream-sync]]).
  - **Edge cases:** 21 Jan S1's answer key was a **PDF** (pandoc can't OMML-extract) → parsed the `N. (letter)` tokens from the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF), pandoc-built a minimal `**(x)**` soln docx from them so the standard `extract` picked up the keys natively (all independently confirmed by the verifier). Two **duplicate-option-label** OCR defects (apr05-s1 Q52, jan21-s1 Q70: two `(b)`/`(d)`, no `(c)`) recovered via `optionOverrides` (all 4) + `answerOverride`. Two OCR-garbled set-builder stems (apr06-s1 Q53, jan23-s2 Q55) reconstructed via `stemOverrides` + `resync`. **Ops:** a mid-batch account **session limit** killed 3 agents (apr05-s1/apr06-s2/apr08-s2) — re-dispatched after reset; the memory's ≤3-concurrent-agent caution held only loosely (ran ~6–8, hit the limit at ~14 completions). Not yet committed at time of this entry. See [[jee-mains-ingestion]].

Reasoned NO to a full deep-read (the two-lane ingest already re-derived SAFE keys and BLIND-solved broken ones — stronger than the "no-source-needed" audit's core work), YES to the cheap `audit:keys` structural backstop, which had never touched JEE (it was practice-MCQ-scoped). Flags all characterized as non-key-errors: (a) all 6 `SOLN≠KEY` were probe FALSE POSITIVES — `concludedLetter`'s `Hence…([A-Da-d])` matched the first letter of the WORD after "Hence" ("Hence **c**ontinuous/**b**oth/**b**akelite/**c**ut-off"); **fixed durably** by tightening `concludedLetter` in `scripts/practice/audit-keys.ts` with a trailing `(?=[)\.,;:\s]|$)` lookahead (a genuine "(B)"/"B."/"B is" conclusion always ends in a delimiter, so it's a strict FP reduction — re-verified the practice probe still fires 7 real `SOLN≠KEY`, no true-positive loss). (b) The 2 Maths `DUP_OPT` (Q71 2022-Jun27 = c/d both `2−log₂3`; Q152 2024-Apr08 = b/c both `25`) are **FAITHFUL reproductions of source-side duplicate options** — pandoc'd both source docx and the dup is IN the source; answer present + correctly keyed → no fix (fabricating a distractor would violate no-fabrication; the docx is the source of record — the [[keep-duplicates-recurrence-signal]] carve-out). (c) The remaining `DUP_OPT` (Physics 10, Chemistry 47, all legacy-2021) are an extraction-COMPLETENESS gap — mostly organic-structure questions whose OPTIONS ARE IMAGES never transcribed (empty option text → flagged as dup) — in the deliberately-skipped Physics/Chemistry subjects, NOT key errors. See [[jee-mains-ingestion]] + [[audit-probe-symmetry]].

Fixed via `scripts/practice/apply-source-fixes.ts` (stem/option-text edits + key move + collision-guarded `content_hash` recompute), then synced the committed transcriptions (option/solution edits + universal key overrides in `overrides.json`) so re-ingest is idempotent (**140/140 `content_hash` match verified**). **The systemic finding drove a bank-wide sweep:** a **zero-LLM Tier-1 probe** (solution-concludes-a-different-letter-than-key · duplicate options · not-exactly-one-correct) over the whole NDA-Maths practice bank flagged 159; **10 parallel agents source-verified every book-sourced flag** → **140 fixes** (66 option · 30 key · 19 stem · 15 solution · 7 struct-collapse) + 3 user-approved book-key overrides (book self-consistently wrong, math-correct with `[Textbook note]`) → bank flag count **159 → 17 faithful/multi-answer residual**. **~12 of the 30 key-fixes were genuine book answer-key errors** the book contradicts itself on (caught by its own worked solution) — the rest were the option-scramble. The probe was promoted to a permanent **`scripts/practice/audit-keys.ts` / `npm run audit:keys`** (MCQ-scoped; pure `concludedLetter`/`auditRow` helpers) so this class is caught going forward.
