Merges through `495c3b9`. See [[practice-pdf-vision-ingestion]] + [[audit-probe-symmetry]].

- **2026-07-24 — JEE Mains Maths taxonomy reshaped to match its cleaned siblings: 24 → 27 chapters (3 structural fixes), 0 data loss.** The JEE Maths chapters were **auto-created by the ingestion agents** (the ~79 JEE auto-created chapters are tracked separately, NOT in the formal 13-subject cleanup register). A three-way comparison against the *cleaned* NDA (31 ch) + MHT-CET (27 ch) Maths taxonomies showed JEE was **slightly UNDER-split with three mis-drawn boundaries**, not over-split. **Note: taxonomy is per-exam** — the three exams intentionally use different naming conventions (NDA `&`/abbrev, CET full-words + roman splits, JEE NCERT-style), so the goal was **structural parity, not literal renaming**. The three fixes (all pure `execute_sql` data reclassification — chapters/subtopics are rows, not schema):
  1. **Integration cluster → 3 chapters** (matching both siblings, which split indefinite/definite): renamed `Integrals`→**Definite Integration** (169); created **Indefinite Integration** (39) from the mislabeled "Integration by Substitution" subtopic — a LaTeX probe confirmed that subtopic was ~entirely *indefinite* (`\int … dx +c`, no limits), so the split was clean; a per-question scan then moved 5 genuinely-definite stems (real limits `\int_{a}^{b}`) back to Definite (`\int_{}^{}` empty-limits = indefinite, a false-positive guarded against). `Application of Integrals` (98) left as-is.
  2. **Trigonometry cluster re-carved to NDA's model**: `Compound Angles`→**Trigonometric Identities** (155, absorbing the scattered *Trigonometric Identities* + *Inequalities* subtopics from the old jumbled `Trigonometry` chapter); `Trigonometry`→**Trigonometric Equations** (45); new **Properties of Triangle** (11) + **Height & Distance** (15) carved out; `Inverse Trigonometric Functions` (62) untouched. ("Compound Angles" was a non-standard chapter name = just trig identities.)
  3. **Limits/Differentiation boundary fixed** (the boundary was mis-drawn — continuity orphaned): moved the *Continuity* subtopic (35) into `Limits and Continuity` (now Limits 85 + Continuity 35 = 120, matching NDA's *Limits & Continuity*); renamed `Continuity and Differentiability`→**Differentiation** (70).
  - **Blast radius near-zero, verified**: JEE Maths has no `/guide`, `/notes`, mocks, or concept/principle tags — a `grep src/` for the old chapter-name literals hit only NDA/CET *notes* files (their own taxonomy), zero JEE refs; the only surface that changed is the `/browse` filter dropdown labels. **Integrity (SQL, the real gate for a data reclassification): 3,202 q preserved exactly · 0 empty chapters · 0 chapter/subtopic mismatches · 0 null subtopics.** No code diff → no lint/test gate run (would only exercise unchanged code against the shared prod DB during the live sync-test churn observed this session). **Method reused**: the reclassification pattern (create targets → reparent subtopics AND their questions' `chapter_id` via CTE → verify `(chapter_id,name)` collisions + 0-mismatch → verify no empties) — see [[reclassification-sql-pattern]] + [[fk-set-null-on-subtopic-drop]]. **Deferred**: a stale MHT-CET `__sync_test_9590c572__` chapter (2 `happy` questions, created *today*) was NOT swept — its 5-q sibling cascade-vanished between two queries seconds apart = **live/recent sync-test churn**, which `global-teardown` reaps by org-cascade; sweep only if it survives the next full `npm test` ([[test-data-leak-org-signal]]). See [[jee-mains-ingestion]].

- **2026-07-24 — JEE Mains Maths INGESTION COMPLETE: every sitting on disk 2021-2025 ingested (~40 sittings) — JEE 1,271 → 3,715 q PUBLIC (Maths 1,624 → 3,202, +1,578).** One autonomous run (across two account-session-limit interruptions, resumed at each reset) closed out all of 2022 (11 sittings), 2023 (13), 2024 (10), 2025 (9). **The core is a two-lane completion pipeline chosen per-paper by a numbering triage** (`grep -oE '^[0-9]+\.' out/<id>_soln.md | sort -u | wc -l` vs the extractor's "N ordered blocks for 180"):
  - **SAFE lane** (extracted key trustworthy: sequential/by-number distinct≈180, OR positional with exactly 180 ordered blocks): 2 agents/paper classify + author a solution to the given answer + INDEPENDENTLY re-derive each key, flagging disagreements → `assemble-safe.ts` (uses the source key; surfaces flags). **This caught 5 genuine source-key errors** (e.g. 2023 jan29 Q71 B→A + Q176 −6→4, jan31 Q153 C→D + Q172 84→5), all agent-verified + fixed via override.
  - **BLIND lane** (broken numbering: extractor finds ≪180 ordered blocks → positional keys are shifted; OR no soln docx at all): 2 agents/paper solve every question FROM SCRATCH, IGNORE the extracted key, and return the DERIVED answer → `assemble-blind.ts` (uses the derived answer, never the source key). **The blind solvers repeatedly confirmed the source NAT keys were positionally shifted (+1 or +2) and many MCQ keys wrong** — so blind-solve was the correct + necessary call, not a fallback. It also recovered the 2 previously-"deferred" papers (2023 apr11, 2025 apr04 — whose positional keys had been verified wrong) and the fully **keyless 2024 Jan-31** (no soln docx → extracted the QP using the QP itself as a dummy soln to get stems+options, then fully AI-derived, the CDS/pariksha keyless precedent).
  - **New durable infra (`scripts/jee/`):** `dump-maths.ts` (Maths dump for the agents), `assemble-safe.ts` / `assemble-blind.ts` (build `papers/<id>.json` from agent outputs), `sol-clean.ts` (`cleanSolution` = normalize double-escaped agent LaTeX via the `\\(` tell + strip a stray trailing `\)`), `scan-flip.js` (delim/`\n`/NO-SOLUTION scan → flip PUBLIC, `--except=N` keeps a row PRIVATE), and a **`paper.skip[]`** field in `PaperData` (config + commit) that drops an agent-flagged corrupted question BEFORE the classification requirement (so a committable "ok" row can be dropped without a "no classification" throw). **Bug fixed:** `isCommittable` treated a `numericOverride` of **0** as falsy → silently dropped a legit NAT-answer-0 row; now `!== undefined` (+4 regression tests). ~1-4 genuinely corrupted questions/paper skipped (truncated stem, or derived answer matches no printed option).
  - **De-glue gotcha (reusable):** `cleanup-latex`'s function-name de-glue turns an English word beginning with a trig/`\det`/`\log` name INSIDE `\text{}` into a LaTeX command (`singular`→`\sin gular`, `singles`→`\sin gles`) → KaTeX rejects it → `attach-solutions` skips the solution (NO-SOLUTION). Workaround: reword (avoid "singular/singles/cosine/determinant/logic/…" inside `\text{}`) — the blind-agent prompt now warns against it. A proper fix (don't de-glue when the function-name is followed by lowercase letters continuing a word) is deferred; the MHT-CET `cleanupArtifacts` de-glue shares the risk. See [[jee-mains-ingestion]].

Scoped + built a "known-visitor" suppression (AskUserQuestion settled 3 product calls): **signed-in → skip the sheet, grade only, write NO `quiz_leads` row** (they're already a known account — a deliberate lead-reduction: their quiz activity won't appear in `/dashboard/leads`); **anon returner (localStorage identity) → keep the sheet but remember consent** so a same-number reveal is a single tap; anon first-timer → unchanged.
  - **The load-bearing constraint + technique (sharpens [[signup-gate-placement]] — the INVERSE of gate-placement is gate-SUPPRESSION):** the page is ISR-static and the answer key is only ever revealed by the submit POST (never shipped to the static page). So "auto-grade with no sheet" required an **authenticated grade-only branch in the SAME capture endpoint**, not shipping the key: `POST /api/public-quiz/submit` now reads `getSessionUser()` (wrapped in try/catch → anon on throw, mirroring `/api/export`; the route is already dynamic so the ISR page is untouched) and, when signed-in, validates only `{slug, answers}`, grades, returns, and **skips `recordLead`**. The page-level skip/continue/form decision is client-side via `useSignedIn()` (keeps ISR, the notes-gate precedent). **Rule: to suppress a capture gate for a known visitor, decide the skip CLIENT-side (preserve ISR) but keep the server-gated secret behind an authed branch of the same POST — never move the secret to the page.**

- **2026-07-21 — Downloaded Word papers rendered set-complement math as raw LaTeX; fixed with a construct-agnostic prettify fallback + an `audit:omml` probe (export-path only, website untouched) — merged `db2184f`.** A teacher-reported "rendering issue" on a downloaded paper traced NOT to the web renderer (KaTeX renders it fine — **web and docx are SEPARATE math paths**; always confirm WHICH path a render bug is on) but to the **docx export**: `mml2omml` (unmaintained, latest 0.5.0) THROWS on temml's MathML for **a superscript applied to a `\cap`/`\cup` group** — set-complement expressions like `(A∪B)'`, `(A∪B)^c`, `n(A∩B)^2`. The trigger is NOT prime-specific (`+`/`\cdot` groups are fine; a group with no superscript is fine; `(x^2+y)'` works but `(A∩B)^2` crashes — obscure mml2omml internals). `latexToOmml` caught the throw → returned null → the exporter emitted the **raw `\(...\)` LaTeX as text**. **Probe-first paid off:** building the enumerator BEFORE fixing showed the class is broader than my first (prime-only) hypothesis — a prime fix would have shipped the `^c`/`^C`/`^2` siblings still broken. MathML-surgery fixes proved fragile (stripping the `tml-prime` class / `mo`→`mi` still throws), so the fix is a **construct-agnostic graceful fallback**: `prettifyMathFallback` (`src/lib/export/ommlBuilder.ts`) turns any OMML-unconvertible zone into readable Unicode (`(A ∪ B)ᶜ`) instead of raw markup — it NEVER restructures math (no complement-vs-derivative-vs-exponent guessing, since `'` is complement in sets but derivative in calculus), so it can't corrupt math; an unmapped macro is left verbatim (never worse than today). Paired with **`npm run audit:omml`** (`findOmmlFailures` in `src/lib/export/ommlAudit.ts` + `scripts/audit-omml.ts`) which scans the bank → `generated-papers/omml-sweep.md`, so a FUTURE mml2omml crash surfaces at ingest, not when a teacher opens a broken paper (first run: **20 zones / 12 PUBLIC questions**, all NDA/State-Board set theory). Export-path only → web untouched; validated on all 20 real zones (0 backslash-macros remain); 18 new tests; full gate PASS. **A fixed zone STILL shows in `audit:omml`** (conversion still fails; only the fallback improved) — the probe measures convertibility, not fallback quality. **Owed:** a manual Word-download eyeball (no headless docx render exists). Replacing/forking the unmaintained mml2omml is the eventual root fix (roadmap). See [[docx-omml-export-pipeline]] + [[render-bug-isolate-pipeline-and-probe]].

- **2026-07-20 — Superadmin-gated the platform-wide dashboard cards + routes (multi-tenancy leak surfaced by onboarding a 2nd org).** Onboarding **Arjunaa Foundation** (tenant #2, admin `careervvmhss@gmail.com`) exposed that `/dashboard` was gating every card on `role === "ADMIN"`, but **six of the surfaces read platform-wide, not org-scoped**, so a second-tenant admin was seeing LWS Pune's (and every org's) data. The split is entirely in the data layer: org-scoped cards use the cookie-bound server client (RLS scopes to `org_id`) — **Members, Branches, Batches, Papers, Question reports, Concept reports** (correct, untouched); the leaky ones use the **service-role admin client** with no `org_id` filter, because the data itself has no org dimension — students/entitlements/feedback/activity live on `auth.users` (no org), and mocks/quizzes are superadmin-authored *global* content. So there was no ignored `org_id` column to add — the fix is to move those to **superadmin-only**, matching the 0056 "platform-level = superadmin" model.
  - **Gated 9 routes** (redirect non-superadmins → `/browse`, mirroring `/superadmin`): `students`, `students/[id]`, `entitlements`, `feedback`, `activity`, `mocks`, `mocks/[slug]`, `quizzes`, **`leads`**. `/dashboard/leads` (quiz-funnel names + mobiles) had no card but was a reachable URL in the same platform-wide class — gated too. (3) **per-subject sections don't fit** — Biology is content-mixed Botany/Zoology (e.g. 2023 is 62/38, not 45/45) → **one "Biology" section spanning [Botany, Zoology]**, exactly the GAT multi-subject-section pattern; ordering by `source_row` recovers the true interleave (verified: 2024 row 114 is Zoology among Botany). (4) **slug collision** — null month made the two 2024 papers produce identical slugs → an **edition-aware slug** (`neet-2024` vs `neet-2024-re`).
  - **Two edge cases the user insisted be included** (verified against source, NOT assumed — the "dropped due to duplication" hypothesis held for only 1 of 4): **3 NTA officially-dropped/bonus questions** (2022 Q93 emf-no-option, 2022 Q128 all-5-true, Re-2026 Q26 vernier-bonus) — NTA awarded full marks to all, so they were modeled as a per-question **`grace` flag** (award full to everyone, `neg=0`, counted correct; graded via `gradeMock`, disclosed with an amber "awarded to all" badge + solution note) and flipped PUBLIC; **1 verbatim cross-bank duplicate** (2021 Q5, deduped at insert — its content survives as a Pariksha *practice* row) handled by a per-sitting **include-override** referencing the live twin at Physics slot 5, graded normally. The grace mechanism is the right pattern for any future exam with bonus/dropped questions (JEE/MHT-CET both have them) — model it as grace, never by flipping a key or excluding the question.
  - **Generalization kept the NDA path byte-identical** (still 36 mocks, strict count contract): section `count` became optional (soft-count when absent — NEET's short 199/198/179 sittings would just warn, though all 8 ended up complete after the 3 grace flips + 1 override); `buildMockPaper` derives totals + per-section counts from the actual rows placed (NDA's placed === declared); grace threaded snapshot→`gradeMock`→review verdict→UI. Worse, my *block-geometry heuristic* for per-page column layout mislabelled three pages (p-04/p-05/p-23), and **every time an agent caught it by actually looking at the page**; the README now says to tell agents "usually two-column — verify per page yourself" rather than hand them a derived map. Reconfirms [[state-board-ingestion]] + [[textbook-chapter-ingestion]] + [[audit-probe-symmetry]] + [[board-reader]] + [[heredoc-backslash-eating]] (the errata JSON was authored via Write, never a heredoc).
  - **19 `solution_image` diagrams — skipped at ingest, then BUILT on the user's call (same day).** The skip was defensible (no stem is unanswerable without a figure — the diagram is the SETUP, the answer is a number; the documented line is "build where the figure IS the answer", i.e. LP's feasible regions / App-of-Def-Integration's area regions), and the user overrode it. The build is the interesting part: it moved `render_solution_diagrams.py` from **coordinate-plots to PHYSICAL geometry**.
    - **New primitives:** `segments` (FINITE lines — the existing `lines` primitive is infinite + viewport-clipped, right for a plot and useless for a ladder; this was the core gap) · `axes:false` (a cone's cross-section has no X/Y axes) · arc `conics` via `t0`/`t1` in degrees · outlined `polys` · `rightangles` · caption **word-wrap** (it was one unwrapped line that silently clipped).
    - **`equal_aspect` is the load-bearing one:** `px()` maps xr/yr to the drawable box INDEPENDENTLY, so a semicircular window rendered as a squashed ellipse. It auto-expands (never crops) the deficient range until px/unit matches on both axes — verified exactly equal on all 18 geometry figures. **Default OFF**, so the 3 shipped chapters render byte-identically (verified; only LP changed, and only because its one over-budget caption now wraps — its LIVE image is untouched until a re-attach).
    - **Method:** 2 pilots hand-authored + rendered + inspected FIRST, so the 4 parallel spec-authoring agents got a proven contract rather than a guess; they emit `data/app-derivatives-12.diagram-specs.<group>.json` part-files (the builder globs them + errors loudly on a duplicate ref). **I then audited the geometry independently from the spec data** rather than trusting the agents' self-reports: every inscribed vertex exact on its circle (3-4-5 triples, `√6,√3`), the cone's semi-vertical angle exactly 30.000000°, both lamp-post rays exactly through the head. Where the optimum IS the answer it's drawn (cone-in-sphere `4r/3`, cylinder-in-sphere `2R/√3`, closed cylinder `h=2r`, sheet `k=3,x=5`); where the VARIABLE is the point it's deliberately generic (Q.13's rectangle non-square, since the square is the conclusion).
    - **Agents caught things I'd have missed**, all by looking at their own renders: `polys` draw AFTER `segments` so a closed outline silently overdraws a coloured highlight edge (label names a colour not on screen — now documented in the builder; the fix is segments-only, not layering); the `curves` label offset is hardcoded, not spec-configurable; dashed hidden edges read "closed" on an open-top box (solved with a double-line rim).

- **2026-07-15/16 — Mock-recommendation email: the project's FIRST outbound-email capability (migration 0059 · `src/lib/email/` · `scripts/email/`). SHIPPED + SENT: 31 students, 0 failures, campaign drained.** Ask: "mail every registered user about the next mock they haven't attempted, from a course they attempted earlier"; the sibling **English AI Tutor** (`Downloads/English_AI_Tutor`) is the reference implementation. Closes the long-standing ROADMAP gap *"Custom SMTP (Resend) — now a real need"* for this one campaign (magic-link + password-reset still ride on Supabase's built-in SMTP).
  - **The analysis changed the feature.** The literal ask reaches **~10 real students**: 41 students, only 13 have ever attempted a mock. And *"the course they attempted"* is **degenerate today** — all 36 published mocks are NDA, so an `exam_id` filter selects everything for everyone. The axis that carries meaning is **`paper_code`** (8 of 12 attempters have only ever sat a **GAT** paper; 2 only Maths). So the scope is exam **AND** paper — the exam leg is kept because it's correct once NEET/JEE mocks ship, not because it does anything now.
  - **The reach lesson was IMPORTED, not re-learned** ([[project-engagement-engine]]'s whole premise). The AI Tutor shipped a vocab nudge to a 5-student cohort and wrote down the regret: *"the bigger engagement gap is '66/77 students have never opened vocab practice' — that's an introduction-email problem, not a re-engagement problem."* PYQ Vault's mirror: **29 of 41 never attempted** (7 of them declared `nda` in `target_exams` at signup, then never sat one). Same build, one extra branch + template → **3× the reach**. User chose both cohorts: `next_mock` + `first_mock`.
  - **What we took from the sibling:** a PURE decision function with an injected `now` (their `src/lib/reminders.js`, 19 tests) · one-email-per-user-per-run (`claimed`-set) · **text + HTML always** (their v9 note: the plain-text alternative is *"the biggest deliverability win per Resend guidance"*) · raw-`fetch` Resend, no SDK · the 600ms throttle (their v8 bugfix after real 429s on the 2 req/sec free tier) · a no-send preview path (their `test_mode`).
  - **What we deliberately did NOT copy — their three weakest points:** (1) **no send log** — they stamp two timestamps on `profiles` AFTER the loop, so a mid-loop crash re-sends everything and there's no record of what went to whom; we log **one immutable row per attempt (sent OR failed)** with a **UNIQUE `dedupe_key`** (the 0052 lesson: a *partial* unique index isn't ON CONFLICT-targetable). **The key IS the policy**: `next_mock:{u}:{mock}` (never re-recommend the same mock → an ignored pick walks down the catalogue) · `first_mock:{u}` (once, ever — no mock id, so no nagging). (2) **no unsubscribe at all** — defensible for their closed school deployment with offline consent; **not** for PYQ Vault's public self-serve signup, so opt-out + one-click unsubscribe ship on day one. (3) **fetch-whole-tables-and-join-in-JS** — ours are paged service-role reads (the 1000-row cap).
  - **The dry run caught a live hazard on its first execution.** It picked `billing_paid_…@test.invalid` + `billing_expired_…@test.invalid` — fixtures the 2026-07-07 billing tests stranded in `auth.users`, which the roster derives from ([[test-data-leak-org-signal]], now proven to have a **second blast radius: outbound email**, not just inflated bank counts). `.invalid` is RFC 2606 reserved ⇒ **guaranteed hard bounce**, and bounce rate is what throttles/suspends a young sending domain. Fixed as a **property, not a skip-list**: `isUndeliverable()` in the pure core rejects reserved TLDs — it immediately caught our own `@example.com` test fixtures too, which is the guard working. **The durable lesson: any code path that emails a roster derived from `auth.users` must assume test fixtures are in it.**
  - **Unsubscribe is POST-only + smoke-tested, and that's load-bearing.** Gmail/Outlook link-scanners **prefetch** urls, so a GET that acted would silently opt out people who never clicked; `/unsubscribe/[token]` renders a confirm button, `/api/unsubscribe/[token]` (POST, service-role — the token IS the capability, no session exists) does the work, and `List-Unsubscribe`/`List-Unsubscribe-Post` (RFC 8058) give mailbox providers a native control. Both build `ƒ`, so the green build proved nothing — drove it live per [[probe-must-reach-the-code]]: GET 200 + *"Compiling /unsubscribe/[token]"* in the dev log (not a middleware bounce) + **`email_opt_out` still false after the GET** · POST flipped exactly one row · non-uuid → 400 · unknown uuid → 200 (not a probing oracle). *(Ops: a `rm -rf .next` racing the dev-server start produced a 500 on every route — the Windows zombie-`next-server` trap again; kill the PID holding the port and restart clean.)*
  - **A tsx script, NOT a cron** — the repo's batch precedent (`scripts/mocks/build.ts`, `scripts/activity/backfill.ts`), and the **engagement gate** says measure the usage shape BEFORE automating a mechanic (`/dashboard/activity` still reports `insufficient`). **Dry-run is the DEFAULT** and **writes nothing** (`ensureUnsubscribeTokens` upserts a profile row to mint a token, so it's deferred to the `--apply` path and the preview renders against a placeholder — the first cut minted rows on every dry run, which is why the whole roster suddenly had `student_profiles`); `--apply` must be typed. `--only=<email>` restricts to one address. Consent is opt-**out** (default false): these are product nudges to registered users, and opt-in would start reach at zero. The QA test account is suppressed **through the real mechanism** (`email_opt_out=true`), not a hardcoded branch. *(Roster addresses are personal data and this repo is PUBLIC — identify accounts by role here, never by address.)*
  - **Gotcha worth keeping:** `resend.ts`/`service.ts` are deliberately **NOT** `server-only` — that's a Next **build-time alias**, unresolvable under tsx (`MODULE_NOT_FOUND`), and the repo already solved this in `src/lib/quiz/assemble.ts`: *"NOT marked server-only precisely so the tsx script can import it"* + inject the client.   - **LIVE RUN (2026-07-16): 31 students · 11 next_mock + 20 first_mock · `sent=31 failed=0`**, staged `--limit=3` → rest. `pyqvault.com` verified in Resend (GoDaddy auto-configure; **independently confirmed from public DNS** — DKIM + the SPF *macro chain* `send → dc-…_spfm → include:amazonses.com` + MX `feedback-smtp.ap-northeast-1` — don't trust the dashboard's green alone; the delegated SPF chain is the leg that can silently break). **A pre-existing GoDaddy `p=quarantine` DMARC** means an auth failure lands in **spam SILENTLY** — the send log still says `sent`, so placement can't be inferred from `sent=31`. **Placement CONFIRMED same-day: 31/31 reached the INBOX**, Gmail reporting SPF PASS · DKIM PASS (`pyqvault.com`) · DMARC PASS, ~1s delivery. Re-run now reports `Recipients: 0` — every `first_mock` key permanently burned, the 11 `next_mock` behind the 7-day cooldown. **32 rows / 32 distinct students / 32 distinct dedupe keys — nobody got two.**
  - **Four things the LIVE run taught that the 75 tests could not.** (1) **The dry run WROTE**: `ensureUnsubscribeTokens` ran before the `--apply` check, minting `student_profiles` rows for every candidate (the whole roster had one where 16 did) — caught only by noticing a count that had no business changing; "dry run" now means *no writes*. (2) **The unsubscribe recorded no WHEN**: `student_profiles` has **no `updated_at` trigger** (the column DEFAULT only fires on INSERT), so the opt-out UPDATE left the creation timestamp — a row asserting "consent withdrawn" with no date, exactly the fact DPDP asks for. Surfaced only by two timestamps being 79 min apart in the wrong order. *(The same gap likely affects the other `student_profiles` writers — `saveOwnMobile`, the `/api/profile` PATCH — unaudited.)* (3) **The reply-to was off-brand**: `EMAIL_FROM` is send-only with no inbox, so replies bounced; adding `reply_to` then exposed that the address it pointed at (`connect.lwspune@…`) is the **TENANT ORG's**, on the most student-facing surface there is. (4) **A reply-to nobody is told about is dead weight** — the footer must invite the reply (the sibling app's reasoning: a student who can't sign in has no other channel).
  - **The brand leak was 4× bigger than it looked** (fix `375c3c6`): the public contact address was the tenant org's in **Footer (every page, directly under "From the team at PYQ Vault") · /privacy (the DPDP contact) · both anon report dialogs**. The 2026-07-12 sweep hunted the *"LWS" string* and an address doesn't contain it. **The DUPLICATION was the bug** — four copy-pasted literals with no single place to fix — so the remedy is `src/lib/brand.ts` + one `CONTACT_EMAIL`, consumed by all four *and* the email `REPLY_TO`. Verified in **rendered HTML** on `/`, `/privacy`, `/browse`, with the dev log checked to prove the routes compiled.
  - **Supabase Auth SMTP wired the same day (2026-07-16) — and it is NOT the same system as the Resend API above.** Our app POSTs `api.resend.com`; **auth mail (password-reset/magic-link/invite) is sent by SUPABASE**, configured with SMTP creds in its dashboard (`smtp.resend.com`:465, user `resend`, sender `noreply@pyqvault.com`). **Enabling SMTP does NOT lift the throttle** — the separate `GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_EMAIL_SENT` had to go **2/1h → 30**; the old ~2/hour cap WAS the bug. Verified live: `POST /auth/v1/recover` → `user_recovery_requested`, `status:200 error:null`, **duration 2.77s** = a real SMTP round-trip (**200 alone proves nothing — that endpoint always 200s to prevent email enumeration; the DURATION is the tell**). **⚠️ The stock reset mail lands in SPAM with Gmail's "might be dangerous" PHISHING banner — a CONTENT fault, not deliverability.** Supabase's `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` always points at `<ref>.supabase.co` while the From says `pyqvault.com`; a reset email whose link domain ≠ From domain is textbook credential-harvesting. **The same-day campaign is the control that proves it**: identical domain/provider/hour, identical PASS/PASS/PASS, links to `www.pyqvault.com` → **31/31 inbox**. So never chase DNS/warm-up for this; fix = template → `{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/confirm?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}` + that route + `/reset-password` + `/forgot-password` (= the ROADMAP "Password reset flow" item; magic-link + invite share the defect). **Deferred by the user** — nothing regressed: a student who forgot their password was already stuck.
  - **Roster hygiene the campaign forced:** 4 non-students suppressed via `email_opt_out` (the real mechanism — never a code skip-list) + **2 leaked `@test.invalid` billing fixtures DELETED from `auth.users`** (verified inert first: 0 attempts/activity/entitlements/bookmarks, created 83ms apart). **The structural finding: deleting an org silently PROMOTES its members onto the student roster** — `deriveStudents` = "any auth user with no `org_members` row", which was only ever a *roster* definition and is now also the *mailing list*; the ex-APJ org account surfaced as a student after the branch re-tenanting. Recurs on the next one. Addresses live in the private memory note — **this repo is PUBLIC, so roster addresses must never land in tracked docs** (a first draft of the SUGGESTIONS entry named all four and was caught pre-commit). See [[project-mock-recommendation-email]].

- **2026-07-15 — State Board Ch.1 Differentiation COMPLETE + PUBLIC (363 q; 10th Class-12 Maths chapter, the FIRST of Part-02's methods spine) — the largest State Board chapter yet, and the cleanest-authored/dirtiest-printed one to date.** 64pp (beats Vectors' 61pp), through the proven `scripts/stateboard/` pipeline: config → render → **13 vision fragments** → merge (363 q, 0 dup refs) → commit PRIVATE (97 solved + 254 exercise-subjective + 12 MCQ across 8 subtopics) → blind MCQ re-derivation → 6 parallel solution-authoring agents → `apply-solutions.ts` → answer-key cross-check → 24 errata brackets → flip PUBLIC → sections + `board:lint`. MH-HSC-12 **1,435 → 1,798**; total PUBLIC **23,646**.
  - **Subtopic arc is finer-grained than the MHT-CET Differentiation notes chapter (8, not 6)** because each textbook exercise block is *method-pure*: Chain Rule · Inverse Functions · Inverse Trig · Logarithmic · Implicit · Parametric · One-wrt-Another · Higher Order. **§1.2.1 "Geometrical meaning of Derivative" is motivating PROSE with no questions** → deliberately NOT a subtopic (verified: p12-13 flows straight into 1.2.2).
  - **The load-bearing lesson — a header scan is NOT a block map; sections start MID-PAGE.** My first band put Ex 1.2 at p28 because the regex found "1.3.1" on p29 — but 1.3.1 starts at **y≈531**, so the top of p29 was still Exercise 1.2. The validation agent flagged the boundary; re-deriving every block with **`get_text('blocks')` y-positions** recovered **31 rows (a whole Q.10 (i)-(ix) I hadn't listed)** — ~32% of that fragment, silently lost otherwise. **Always map blocks by (page, y), never by page alone** (same class as the Vectors gap-fill). Two agents independently caught straddles the page-boundary heuristic would have dropped (§1.3.3 Ex.6 sat above the Ex 1.3 header on p38).
  - **✅ GATE — answer-key cross-check vs the Part-2 ANSWERS section (p265-269), 6 parallel agents over 266 exercise rows: 208 AGREE · 48 NO-BOOK-KEY (show-that) · **8 BOOK-KEY-WRONG + 1 BOOK-QUESTION-MISPRINT + 1 INTERPRETIVE · 0 OUR-ANSWER-WRONG**.** Zero authoring errors — the first chapter with a clean sweep on our side. The method that made it trustworthy (now the standard): **a THIRD independent ground truth** — mpmath/sympy differentiation of the *actual stem* at 30-50 dps, testing **both** our answer AND the book's against it, because comparing the two to each other lets a shared error hide. **~20 apparent disagreements dissolved** on equivalence testing (`2\cdot4^x\log4` ≡ `4^{x+1}\log2`; single-branch book answers vs our documented ±branches). **`simplify()` returning non-zero is NOT evidence of inequality** — on Ex 1.3 that alone would have manufactured 3 false "our answer is wrong" findings (identities that hold only ON the constraint curve).
  - **The book's key is a PEER, not an ORACLE — and Misc I Q.4 proves it.** The transcription agent *predicted in advance*: "an answer key naming A or B here would be a book error; I'd expect C." **The book says B.** Three independent derivations say C; verified numerically on the non-trivial branch (C matches 7/7 at 25 sig figs, B 0/7). Option B is the correct expression **with its two brackets interchanged** — the question's own near-miss distractor, and *the book's key-setter fell for it*. Every agent tested the rival hypothesis "our transcription is wrong" by **rendering the source page and looking** (Ex 1.3 Q.5(iii): a flipped `(x⁴−y⁴)/(x⁴+y⁴)` would have vindicated the book — the page plainly prints the other way; hypothesis rejected).
  - **The book's printed SOLUTIONS are far dirtier than its questions: ~16 misprints in the 97 solved examples vs ~1 defective question in 266.** Worst: **`1.3.1 SolvedEx.1 (iii)` corrupts `(2x+3)`→`(3x+2)` across four consecutive lines into a WRONG printed final answer** — shipping it unflagged would have published a wrong answer. All transcribed **faithfully as printed** + bracketed. **25 errata items** (the most of any chapter) → `errata.ts` now spans **10 chapters / 99 items**.
  - **New durable pipeline artifacts** (fold-the-learning-in, each closing a bug that bit a *previous* chapter): **`dump-mcq.ts`** (blind dump — omits `is_correct` so step 4 stays independent; **guards that every MCQ carries 4 options**, the NCERT `options:[]` bug) · **`dump-review.ts`** (**refuses to dump unless every row carries real answer text** — the Line-and-Planes `has_solution`-boolean bug that made a cross-check meaninglessly all-AGREE) · **`dump-subjective.ts`** (partition authoring by ref prefix) · **`mark-mcq-verify.ts`** (computes `matches_current` *here*, so the verifier can stay blind) · **`apply-errata.ts`** (idempotent bracket prepend at the START — `errata.ts` scans `startsWith("[")`, so an appended bracket is invisible; mirrors DB↔source JSON so they can't drift).
  - **Zero figures / zero `solution_image`** — verified 0 of 363 stems reference a figure; only 1 of 254 authored rows flagged `diagramWouldHelp` (Misc II Q.1's corner sketch) and the prose stands complete, so skipped per the Vectors/Line-and-Planes precedent. **Ops:** ~6 agents died on API stalls/watchdogs — **12-page vision ranges stall, 5-9 pages succeed**; the fix is smaller ranges + **write the output file EARLY/incrementally** (a dead Misc II agent finished all its verification then lost it at the final write). A replacement **audited the dead agent's leftover script and discarded it** — it only tested OUR answer, never the book's, so its lost "all pass" claim wouldn't have been evidence anyway. The heredoc-eats-backslashes pitfall fired twice; both agents self-diagnosed. Reconfirms [[state-board-ingestion]] + [[textbook-chapter-ingestion]] + [[audit-probe-symmetry]] + [[board-reader]] + [[heredoc-backslash-eating]].

- **2026-07-15 — Paper editor renders questions like the bank (reuses `/browse`'s `QuestionCard`); Add-questions panel → a sheet (merge `25d57c8`).** Triggered by a paper review: the editor showed **raw LaTeX** (`\(Q_1 = 20\)` verbatim) in a 2-line clamp with no options. Three findings, one root cause.
  - **The render bug:** `PaperEditor` dumped `{p.text}` into a `<p className="line-clamp-2">` with **no `KatexRenderer`** — so every math question in every paper had been broken since the builder shipped. `AddQuestionsPanel` had the same bug, so you were picking questions out of raw markup too.
  - **The data was never there:** the editor loaded the slim `QuestionPreview` shape (id/text/taxonomy — the deliberately-light shape built for the **cart-preview** payload), which carries **no options**. So "show options" was a data change, not a CSS change. Fixed by swapping to `queryQuestionsByIds` (full `QuestionRow`, already the `/saved` precedent) + reusing `QuestionCard` **wholesale**. User chose to include solutions in the payload; bounded by the 200/paper export cap on a `force-dynamic` admin page. `queryQuestionPreviewsByIds` **stays** — `/api/cart/preview` is still its rightful user.
  - **The layout WAS the readability bug.** The add panel sat in a permanent `lg:grid-cols-2` column, i.e. 50% of a `max-w-5xl` page — which is *why* the stem was clamped to two lines. Moving it into a `Sheet` (mirroring the existing Sections-dialog idiom) freed full width. Kept rather than deleted: it's a weaker duplicate of `/browse` for discovery (no chapter/subtopic/PYQ-year filters, `kind` hardcoded `"all"`), but it's the only in-page targeted search; `/browse`+cart stays the bulk path.
  - **`hideCart` — reuse needs a carve-out, not a fork.** `QuestionCard` calls `useCart()` unconditionally and renders a toggle literally labelled *"Add to paper"*. On the paper editor that's **semantically wrong** (the question is already in this paper; the cart is a different global localStorage selection) and its in-cart ring reads as a meaningless selection state. Added `hideCart?: boolean` defaulting to `false` → `/browse` + `/saved` byte-identical (verified `/browse` 200 anon). **The general rule: when reusing a shared card on a new surface, audit every embedded control for whether its MEANING still holds; suppress via a prop rather than forking the component.**
  - **Bonus bug:** the panel seeded its exam filter from `exams[0]` with exams ordered `by name` — i.e. **alphabetical** — so an NDA paper opened its search on *CBSE Class 12*. Now seeds from `dominantExamId(questions)` (new pure `src/lib/papers/exam.ts`, TDD 6 cases: empty/single/mixed/tie-by-first-appearance/null-exam). `canEdit` also repointed to `getSessionSuperadmin()`, mirroring `/browse` post-0056.
  - **Verification gap (honest):** the page is `force-dynamic` + middleware-gated, so **the authed render was never driven** — my first "smoke test" was a middleware 307 that never compiled the route (see the sharpened `ƒ`-page pitfall + [[probe-must-reach-the-code]]). Compile is proven (build + the only-layout check that `CartProvider`/`BookmarksProvider`/`MobilePromptProvider` reach `/dashboard`); render is not. Merged + pushed on the user's explicit instruction with that gap flagged. **Browser check still owed** (SUGGESTIONS.md).

- **2026-07-14/15 — Member-management redesign: superadmin/admin/teacher + Org→Branch→Batch + per-batch paper non-repetition (migrations 0054–0057, 5 slices, all deployed).** Two orgs onboard initially (LWS Pune + APJ School — **APJ was folded into a *branch* of LWS Pune on 2026-07-15, see the entry above; the DB now has one org**). The user's model: a single **superadmin** (`connect.lwspune@gmail.com`) with full cross-org content + edit rights; **admins** who manage their org (branches, teachers) but do NOT edit content; **teachers** assigned to one-or-more **branches** who build QPs for those branches only. Built + shipped slice-by-slice (branch-per-slice → gate → merge --no-ff → push):
  - **Slice 1 (0054 batches + 0055 branches):** per-batch paper builder — a paper optionally targets a batch; the add panel soft-warns (amber "Repeated for this batch") when a candidate question is already in another paper for the SAME batch. Non-repetition **derives** from `paper_questions`⋈`papers.batch_id` (no ledger, no sync). Scope=per-batch, enforcement=soft-warn (user-chosen via AskUserQuestion). 0055 then made **branch a first-class entity** (`branches`, admin-managed) replacing 0054's free-text `branch` label (needed so teachers can be *assigned* to a branch — you can't attach a person to a label). `/dashboard/branches` + `/dashboard/batches` CRUD.
  - **Slice 2 (0056): content editing → superadmin-only.** `platform_admins` locked table + `is_superadmin()`/`can_edit_content()`; repoint every content-write policy to superadmin cross-org. **Key trap avoided:** `can_edit_questions()` was OVERLOADED (gated content edit AND paper building) — redefining it would've broken the paper builder; instead added a purpose-named `can_edit_content()` and left `can_edit_questions()` alone (see [[project-member-management]]). App guards (edit/upload routes + pages + browse Edit affordance + dashboard Upload card) → `requireSuperadmin`/`getSessionSuperadmin`. The 2 LWS teachers lost content-edit exactly as intended.

- **2026-06-27 — Cut Supabase egress (hit 120% of the 5 GB free cap): daily ISR on /notes+/guide + a calmer /browse sitemap.** The DB (~65 MB) + storage (~15 MB) are tiny, so it's a *transfer*, not data-size, problem. A 24h API-log sample was 100% `/notes` regen queries → **ISR regeneration of the ~500–650 indexed /notes+/guide paths is the dominant egress source**: cached pages cost Supabase **zero** (served from Vercel's edge), only regens hit the DB, and a 1h `revalidate` let crawlers re-trigger a fresh DB pull up to 24×/day per path. Fix: bumped `revalidate` `3600 → 86400` across 208 `/notes`+`/guide`+`/nda`+`/quiz` pages (content changes weekly at most → ~24× less regen), and dropped the `/browse` sitemap entry from `priority 1.0 / daily` to `0.8 / weekly` (it's the one uncached, heaviest surface). Deferred levers if that's not enough: trim `solution` (the biggest column) from the `/browse` *list* query; front question images through a CDN; Supabase Pro. Commit `7a7c47c`. Lesson → [[supabase-egress-levers]] (a sibling cost-lever to [[middleware-auth-scope]] — both: don't do expensive per-request work on public/cached/anon traffic).
- **2026-06-27 — Scoped the auth middleware to signed-in surfaces — killed ~40% of Vercel Active CPU (the whole Edge runtime line).** Vercel Fluid Active CPU hit **4h 2m / 4h (over quota)**. The Type/Runtime usage breakdowns showed the Edge runtime line (~1h 35m, 39.2%) ≈ the middleware line (~1h 27m, 36.1%) almost 1-for-1 — i.e. nearly all Edge CPU was the middleware. Root cause: [src/middleware.ts](src/middleware.ts) used a broad negative-lookahead catch-all matcher, so [updateSession](src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts) ran `supabase.auth.getUser()` — **a network round-trip to the Supabase Auth server, billed as Active CPU** — on **every public, anon request** (`/browse`, `/notes`, `/guide`, `/quiz`, …) that never uses the auth check. Fix: scoped the matcher to the four authenticated prefixes only (`/dashboard`, `/account`, `/upload`, `/uploads`), each `prefix` + `prefix/:path*`. **Not a security change** — every one of those pages already self-guards at the page level (`getUser`/`getSessionMember` + `redirect`); `updateSession`'s logic is untouched so the existing route-guard tests still hold. The only behavioural effect: a signed-in user's session cookie refreshes on those surfaces (+ server actions) rather than on every public page — fine for a public-first site (public pages use the cookie-less `createSupabaseAnonClient`, which never needed the refresh). TDD: 2 new matcher-scope tests in `tests/middleware.test.ts` guard against regressing to a broad catch-all; full pre-push gate green (commit `1d58461`, merge `2f123d3`). Projected **4h 2m → ~2h 30m**, back under quota. **Separate meter from the prior egress fix** — the 2026-06-27 ISR/egress commit cut the *Supabase* data-transfer bill; this cuts the *Vercel* compute bill (the middleware fix also lightens Supabase auth-request volume as a bonus). Lesson → [[middleware-auth-scope]].

- **2026-06-15 — Collaborative paper builder shipped, step 1 (migration 0039): multiple teachers assemble ONE exam paper together, partitioned by section.** Answers "GAT paper is created by multiple teachers — how can multiple teachers contribute to a single paper?" Today a "paper" is the ephemeral per-browser localStorage cart (`qb:cart:v1`); this promotes it into a persistent, org-scoped, section-partitioned entity. Two new tables: `papers` (org-scoped; `draft`/`finalized`; editable `section_template` jsonb; `finalized_snapshot`) + `paper_questions` junction.
  - **Why a junction table, NOT a `question_ids[]` array on the paper row:** two teachers adding to the same section concurrently must not clobber each other. Each add is one independent INSERT row; `PRIMARY KEY (paper_id, question_id)` + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes concurrent/duplicate adds idempotent (no read-modify-write lost-update window). Mirrors `quiz_atoms_map` — membership is a JOIN, not an array.
  - **Lifecycle mirrors the quizzes snapshot (0035):** `draft` is the live mutable junction table; **finalize** freezes the composition onto `papers.finalized_snapshot` (jsonb) so a later bank edit can't silently change a printed paper; **reopen** clears it. The export always feeds the paper's ordered ids into the existing `/api/export` `questionIds` path — **zero new export code**.
  - **The key insight — GAT papers are naturally partitioned by SUBJECT, and teachers are subject specialists.** So collaboration isn't N people editing one list (locking/CRDT) — it's N people each owning a SECTION; conflicts disappear by construction. The per-section progress view (English 48/50 · Physics 12/25 …) IS the coordination mechanism (falls out of the data model, not bolted on). The elegant tie-in: `subjectToSectionKey` derives a question's section from its subject, so adding auto-files (a "Physics" q → the Physics section).
  - **Collaboration model (user decisions, 2026-06-15):** (1) **org-wide access** — any ADMIN/TEACHER in the org opens + contributes to any of the org's papers (the org IS the boundary; no per-paper invite table). (2) **Soft section assignment** — anyone edits any section; assignment is a hint, never a lock. (3) **Multiple teachers per section** (native to the junction model). (4) **Sections fully editable** per paper (add/rename/delete/retarget); `section_template` seeded with a GAT default (English + GK subjects, ~150). (5) **Deleting a section is NON-destructive** — its questions keep their `section_key` and render under "Unassigned" until re-filed (any membership whose key isn't a current template key); no DB reassignment, no lost work.
  - **RLS:** org-scoped like PRIVATE questions — read = any org member; insert/update = org editors (`current_user_can_edit_questions`); **delete a paper = creator-or-admin, enforced in Postgres** (`created_by = auth.uid() OR current_user_is_admin()`). All FKs cascade from `organizations`, so the org-sweep `global-teardown` cleans test fixtures with **no teardown change** (advisor clean — no new lints).
  - **Access lives at `/dashboard/papers`** (list + `[id]` editor). Reachable via a **UserMenu link for org members** — teachers are redirected off the `/dashboard` home but still need Papers, so the entry point is the user menu (+ a dashboard-home card for admins). The editor: section progress bars, questions grouped by section (remove + move-to-section), an embedded search-and-add panel (reuses `queryQuestions`; auto-files by subject), editable sections, finalize/reopen, Download (reuses `/api/export`).
  - **Built ISOLATED — zero changes to `/browse`** (the only existing-code touches were the two additive nav entry points). TDD: 28 pure-helper unit tests (`papers-template`/`papers-sections`) + **9 RLS/data integration tests** (`papers-rls` — org isolation on read AND write, idempotent add, multi-teacher same-section add, finalize-freeze, creator-or-admin-only delete) — all green; full prepush gate green; new `ƒ` routes load (307 auth-redirect, not 500). The `/browse?paper=<id>` add-flow is step 2 (a fast-follow). Pure core in `src/lib/papers/` (`types`/`template`/`sections`/`admin`); UI under `src/app/dashboard/papers/`. See [[collaborative-paper-builder]].

- **2026-06-15 → COMPLETE 2026-06-16 — NEW exam: CDS English ingestion (`scripts/cds/` pipeline) — ALL 19 papers committed PRIVATE (2,280 q); no answer keys → LLM-derived + confidence-flagged answers.** First new exam since JEE. Source: 19 scanned CDS English booklets in `C:\tmp\PYQPs\CDS\02. English\` (2017-I … 2026-I), **image PDFs with no text layer and NO official answer key**. So: vision-transcribe → **DERIVE each answer + flag confidence** (HIGH/MED/LOW) → commit PRIVATE for human spot-check before PUBLIC. New DB exam `CDS` (id `07700c16-…`) + subject English, taxonomy **cloned from NDA English** (8 ch / 29 sub — CDS English ≈ NDA English in style). Registered in `examContext.ts` (`ExamSlug` + registry → exam picker + `/notes/cds` hub auto-derive). State + resume in [[cds-english-ingestion]]; durable how-to in [[section-based-exam-ingestion]].
  - **The pipeline (`scripts/cds/`, mirrors `scripts/practice`/`scripts/jee`):** `config.ts` (paper registry + the **section-type catalog** — each CDS section type → NDA-English taxonomy + `underline`/`inlineStimulus`/`passage`/`perQuestionSubtopic` flags) · `lib.ts` (pure assembly + `validateRows` collision/coverage/delimiter checks + `normalizeQuestions` self-heal; **TDD `tests/cds-lib.test.ts`, 19 cases**) · `render`/`commit`/`preview` + README. Per paper: render → **section-map agent** (`data/<id>.sections.json`) → **transcribe BY SECTION** agents (`data/<id>.questions.json`) → **underline agent** (`data/<id>.underlines.json`) → `commit` dry-run → `preview` → `commit --apply`.
  - **The load-bearing lessons (from the 2026-1 trial → [[section-based-exam-ingestion]]):** (1) **section order/selection varies every year** (2026 opens word-pairs; 2017 ordering-of-words; 2023 word-classes; 2024 antonyms — 13–16 sections) → a per-paper **section-map pre-pass** is mandatory; (2) **Directions are load-bearing, not decoration** — synonyms vs antonyms look identical without them and FLIP the answer; transcribing by raw PAGE range split the antonym section across agents and silently flipped 5 answers (Q56-60, one unflagged HIGH) → **transcribe BY SECTION**; (3) **directions in `context`, one set per section** (mirrors NDA English: 887/900 directions-in-context, 895/900 in sets — renders once per section); (4) **fold the per-question stimulus (match-list code grid / S1-S2 pair) INTO the hash-bearing stem** — `content_hash` excludes `context`, so a generic stem + shared options collide + silently drop (6 dropped on the first trial commit); RC/cloze passages stay shared in the set context; (5) **underlines** via `\(\underline{\text{word}}\)`.
  - **Pipeline hardening as papers revealed shapes:** the section-type catalog grew to **~27 types** as papers exposed new shapes (`word-usage-count`/`word-usage-select`, `voice-transformation`, `word-meaning-statements`, `usage-statements`, `spelling-select`, `sentence-transformation`, `reported-speech`, …). `normalizeQuestions` self-heals three recurring agent quirks: options emitted as an OBJECT instead of array; difficulty synonyms/casing; **and a rearrangement-grid agent returning the ordering STRING (e.g. "QSPR") as `answer` instead of the option label** — mapped back to its label. The biggest per-paper gotcha: **"Ordering of Words" P/Q/R/S grids span both columns → render the FULL PAGE hi-DPI** (`fitz.Matrix(3.0+)`); per-column crops split the grid at the gutter and drop fragments (bit 2024-2 + 2022-2, both recovered full-width). **5-option spotting-errors** (4 parts + "No error") refit to the 4-option bank.
  - **Subagent content-filter gotcha:** a transcription/section-map subagent reproducing **verbatim passage prose** (the 2024-I RC section is Faulkner's Nobel speech with "doom/dying" imagery) can return **"Output blocked by content filtering policy"** (0 tokens). Workaround: have the agent do **structure-only** mapping (no prose, `passage:"TBD"`) and capture the passage separately (OCR/manual) so the trigger text is never generated by the model.
  - **State — COMPLETE.** All **19 papers (2017-I … 2026-I) committed PRIVATE, 2,280 q**, on `main` + pushed; every q has Directions-in-context + 4 options + exactly 1 correct; 253 sets. `Eng_CDS_2024_1.pdf` was Elementary Mathematics until the **user replaced it with the correct English booklet 2026-06-15**. **The ONLY open item before PUBLIC:** human spot-check the LLM-derived answers (no official keys), prioritising MED-flagged items + the oldest dense scans (**2017-1 worst, 60 MED**) + the part-rearrangement grids. Per-paper review HTMLs at `scripts/cds/out/<id>.preview.html`; per-paper detail in [[cds-english-ingestion]].

The Tags file was **hand-built**, leaking wrong-key / mistyped-option / off-by-one / forgotten-GAT-subject errors — root cause: re-typing data that already lives, verified + structured, in the bank. Fix (Phase A): PYQ Vault emits the Tags sheet from the built paper, so there's no human transcription left to get wrong. Shipped both apps, green (PYQ Vault prepush PASS; nda-tracker 1494 tests). See [[cross-app-feature-execution]].
  - **PYQ Vault** ([tagsSheet.ts](src/lib/export/tagsSheet.ts) TDD 19 cases + `kind:"tags"` on [/api/export](src/app/api/export/route.ts) → `.xlsx` via SheetJS (already a dep) + a third DownloadDialog button): `buildTagRows` numbers via the **same `groupBySet` loop the docx uses**, so Q-numbers match the printed paper AND the Evalbee scan **by construction** (the load-bearing alignment). Answer derived from the `isCorrect` option; subjects mapped to nda-tracker keys (`Mathematics→Maths`, `Current Affairs→Others`, GAT subjects pass through so `validateGatSubjects` is satisfied); a **distinct `Context` column** for passage sets.
  - **nda-tracker** (derived copy — **NO DB migration**): `parseTagsFile` reads a `Context`/`Passage` column → a `context` field that flows untouched into the `exams.questions` **jsonb** (Step4Confirm stores the tags array verbatim, no field whitelist — *the schemaless jsonb blob is exactly why context needed no DDL*; typed columns would have forced an `ADD COLUMN`). The passage renders above the stem on all four review surfaces (`QuestionCard`→ExamInsightsPanel + inline `QuizResults` + `quizTaking` take/review), so RC/Cloze are reviewable instead of meaningless stems. `NDA_FREQ_BY_SUBJECT.Maths` synced to PYQ Vault's 31 canonical chapter names (the validation source — `getValidChapters` reads it; the freq *chart* reads each user's persisted `ndaFreqBySubject`, so existing users are untouched; parent `pct` split to keep the total).
  - **The design spine — PYQ Vault is master (user-confirmed).** The Tags Excel is a lossy, schema-coupled bridge; the durable context work (jsonb field + render) lives on the side we keep and is Phase-B-reusable. So context went in as a **distinct field, never inlined into the stem** — zero throwaway modeling, nothing to migrate out later. The one disposable bit is ~5 lines of column-detection in `parseTagsFile`.
  - **Deferred — Phase B (the long-term win, user-confirmed): retire the Excel via a direct API push.** PYQ Vault pushes the built paper's tags over the existing cross-app Bearer-secret bridge (same pattern as the Quiz Factory `quiz-import`), nda-tracker stores it keyed to a paper id, and the upload wizard picks a pre-loaded paper from a dropdown — so only the Evalbee Results is uploaded by hand. Carries context/set-grouping/images losslessly (writes the same jsonb the same way → still no migration). The Evalbee Results upload always stays (it IS the OMR output). → ROADMAP.

Maps each of the 14 NDA Physics chapters to the NCERT Class 9–12 chapters it absorbs, each row deep-linking to `/browse` via `resolveTaxonomy` → `BrowseLink`. New files: [_data/ncert-map.ts](src/app/guide/nda-physics/_data/ncert-map.ts) (curated TS map — NOT a DB table, same curation-is-signal rule as guide principles), [ncert-map/page.tsx](src/app/guide/nda-physics/ncert-map/page.tsx), [tests/guide-nda-physics-ncert-map.test.ts](tests/guide-nda-physics-ncert-map.test.ts) (11 cases, written test-first). One `ROUTES` entry auto-wired the side-nav + sitemap; Traps' `PrevNextNav` chained forward.
  - **The weak-signal detector (the durable design — [[weak-signal-trend-detection]]).** The user's framing: NDA questions mapping to NCERT *Class 12* in *recent* papers is a leading indicator of syllabus drift — don't ignore the weak signal. The map embodies it: tracked Class-12 topics carry live-bank recency, and a pure `signalStatus()` helper classifies each **live** (≥1 q since `RECENT_FROM=2024`) / **watch** (tested before, now cold) / **dormant** (mapped, never seen). watch/dormant rows render muted with a "last seen" chip, so the page IS the detector — it surfaces a topic the moment it climbs. But the inverse discipline is baked into the copy: **we do NOT pre-write notes/practice for dormant topics** — chasing an absent signal is the same error as ignoring a real one, inverted. Map it, flag it, act when it goes live.
  - **The premise was checked against data before agreeing — and it didn't hold (yet).** Per-paper-normalized probes showed the recent Class-12 footprint is flat-to-*declining* (Modern Physics 1.9→1.3→0.8 q/paper; EMI vanished since 2017; Wave Optics/Communication never seen). So no Class-12 wave is present today. Two corrections fell out: (1) my initial 9/10/11 framing **undercounted** — a large slice of NDA already maps to Class 12 (Ray/Wave Optics, Current Electricity, EMI, AC, all of Modern Physics), so the map is 9–**12**; (2) the "missing rotational-motion chapter" is a **non-gap** — only ~3 incidental q bank-wide, accurately reflecting that NDA barely tests it (surfaced as the `UNMAPPED_NCERT` footer, not manufactured into a chapter). `signal` recency numbers are an authored snapshot (`SIGNAL_SNAPSHOT=2026-06-14`); refresh by re-running the per-topic probe as the bank grows.

The build missed it because the page is dynamic (`ƒ`, never prerendered) and the test was data-only. Renamed `ref`→`item`; curl-verified HTTP 200. Lesson folded into the "Recurring pitfalls" `next build` entry (build-green ≠ runtime-ok for `ƒ` pages; smoke-test dynamic routes).

### 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-11 — archived 2026-06-26

_Newest-first, matching CLAUDE.md ordering. The `### 2026-06` header + 2026-06-12-onward entries stay in CLAUDE.md._

- **2026-06-11 — Production test-data leak found + cleaned (18 fixture questions, 11 PUBLIC + 12 leaked orgs), and `global-teardown` rewritten to an org-keyed sweep.** User shared a `/browse` screenshot showing dummy questions (`qprinciple…`, `resolver-C…`) in the live MHT-CET Optics bank. Investigation found **18 leaked test-fixture questions** (11 PUBLIC, inflating the MHT-CET count) + **12 throwaway test orgs** + 11 org_members + 2 upload_jobs + junk taxonomy (`EditSetSubj_*`, `UD_DelSubject_*`), all from integration tests whose `afterAll` was interrupted (parallel/killed run) and whose `global-teardown` never caught them.
  - **The detection lesson (the durable one — [[test-data-leak-org-signal]]):** no single content signal catches every fixture class. Orphan-signature (`source_file` + `upload_job_id` both NULL) missed `del-otherq` (it has a test `upload_job_id`); text-pattern missed the 5 **upload-flow fixtures** (`goodXlsxBuffer` rows — convex-lens / tuning-fork / enthalpy / d-dx — realistic text, **real sha256 `content_hash`, under canonical MHT-CET taxonomy**, PUBLIC); `content_hash !~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'` (provably 0 real rows) caught the named-hash bulk but missed those same 5. **`org_id` is the only universal signal** — every fixture belongs to a throwaway org whose name carries an 8-hex run-id (`randomUUID().slice(0,8)`), e.g. "Resolver Org fd90dd5f", "Upload Flow Org c8779c4c". Cleaned via an org-scoped cascade delete (`question_reports` first — its `org_id` FK is RESTRICT — then `organizations`, which CASCADEs questions→options/tags/reports + org_members + upload_jobs); MHT-CET PUBLIC back to the documented **4,686** baseline, NDA **4,860**.
  - **The fix (the real artifact) — [tests/global-teardown.ts](tests/global-teardown.ts) rewritten.** The old teardown swept only test-**named subjects** by a hardcoded prefix list (which had already rotted — `EditSetSubj_` was missing) + two canonical-adjacent nodes; it had **no mechanism for test questions under canonical taxonomy**, which is most of the leak. New primary mechanism = **ORG SWEEP** keyed on `isTestOrgName` (8-hex run-id token, with a `REAL_ORG_NAMES` allowlist guard), relying on the verified FK cascade. Secondary sweeps: test taxonomy (run-id-token names, empty-guarded) + the canonical-adjacent auto-creates (Chemistry "Chemical Thermodynamics" / Differentiation "Chain Rule", **exam-scoped + empty-guarded** so the real JEE Mains "Chemical Thermodynamics" chapter is never touched). Pure predicates extracted to [tests/global-teardown-helpers.ts](tests/global-teardown-helpers.ts) (`isTestOrgName`/`isTestTaxonomyName`/`isTestAuthEmail`/`hasRunIdToken`) with 8 TDD unit tests. **Validated end-to-end:** ran leak-prone test files (`reports-create`, `edit-apply-set`, `upload-delete`, …) → teardown left the DB pristine (only LWS Pune, baselines intact).
  - **Three follow-ups also shipped the same session:** (1) **auth-user sweep** — the org cascade clears `org_members` but NOT the `auth.users` rows behind them, so the teardown now pages `admin.auth.admin.listUsers`, deletes the `@test.local` fixtures (`isTestAuthEmail`; clears `entitlements` first), and 11 leaked accounts were cleaned. (2) **A guardrail** — after every sweep the teardown re-asserts zero test orgs / test subjects / test auth users remain and THROWS if any survived (safe to assert "zero" only because globalTeardown runs after the whole suite), turning a silent prod leak into a red run. (3) **Purged stale `pubtest` quiz cruft** — 2 empty test quizzes (`quiz:delete`, propagated to nda-tracker) + 3 dummy `pubtest-%` atoms; `quiz:lint` is now 0-flagged.
  - **Lesson reconfirmed:** the PostgREST 1000-row cap (the teardown id-fetches page defensively); [[verify-before-deleting]] (every delete guarded by a test-signature assert + emptiness check, real content provably untouched).

- **2026-06-11 — Quiz Factory: the formula-recall quizzes were unfair — reworked 86 atoms + guarded the root cause; plus the `/dashboard/quizzes` 60-cap + two follow-ups.** User flagged "Probability formula quiz reads off." Root cause: a `formula`-theme atom harvested at `status='auto'` carries the placeholder stem **"Which of the following is the formula for `<concept name>`?"** + random sibling-concept distractors — generic, guessable-by-elimination, and the assembler treats `auto` as publishable, so the Probability formula quiz shipped 15/15 from these. The audit (every `auto` atom ⟺ generic stem; every `verified` atom ⟺ concrete stem) found **9 pushed quizzes across 7 chapters** affected (88 atoms); Functions/Lines/Trig-Id were clean (all-verified).
  - **Fix (all on `main`, none was student-facing — every affected quiz was an nda-tracker draft, `public_slug=null`):** 7 parallel agents authored a concrete scenario stem + 3 tight permutation distractors per atom into each chapter's `verify/nda-maths__<chapter>-formulas.ts` module (the verify mechanism overrides `stem` + `distractors` + optional `correct`, promoting `auto→verified`). **86 reworked, 2 retired** (Probability `selecting-numbers` = classical-probability restated; `min-max-of-combined-probabilities` = the inclusion-exclusion identity mis-keyed as a min/max bound — Fréchet-Boole already covers bounds). Showed the user a **KaTeX-rendered HTML preview of all 86** (built read-only from the verify modules + DB keys) before applying. Then `quiz:verify` ×7 → retire the 2 → **delete + re-assemble all formula quizzes** from the clean pool: **0 broken stems across 20 formula quizzes / 263 q**, and coverage grew where previously-stranded `verified` atoms had been crowded out (Probability 1→2 quizzes, Statistics 2→3, Vectors 2→3).
  - **Durable guard (the real artifact):** `stemLint.flagStem` now flags `GENERIC_FORMULA_TEMPLATE` (reversing a prior *tolerated* test case — `quiz:lint` catches it) **and** `assembleNextQuiz` hard-excludes any stem matching `Which of the following is the formula for%` — so a bare-harvested formula atom can never be published until it's been verified into a concrete stem. TDD'd; runbook note in [QUIZ_FACTORY.md](QUIZ_FACTORY.md). See [[quiz-formula-coverage-gap]].
  - **`/dashboard/quizzes` 60-cap (surfaced by the rework):** `listAssembledQuizzes` did `.order(created_at desc).limit(60)` then filtered client-side *within* those 60. The bank now has 109 quizzes, so the 15 new formula quizzes shoved older ones (e.g. Probability's 6 computation + property + trap quizzes — all live on nda-tracker) past the cutoff, and the "Quizzes built" stat read the capped list length (60), not the true total. Fixed: limit `60→1000` (client cascade now spans every quiz; <1000 so no truncation) + new `countAssembledQuizzes()` head-count drives the stat (109). Server-side filtering + lazy-loaded questions + pagination deferred to ROADMAP (needed past ~1000 quizzes). **Lesson: any admin list with a hard `.limit(N)` silently hides rows once the table crosses N, and a stat derived from `list.length` lies — derive counts from a true `count:"exact"`, raise/paginate the list.**
  - **Follow-ups:** (a) `quiz:lint` sweep of all themes — but the lint's atom + map queries had the **PostgREST 1000-row cap** (bare `.limit()`, scanned only 1000 of 1762 ready atoms); paginated both → complete sweep is **clean** (only 3 dummy `pubtest` test atoms flagged; quiz-integrity 0). Reconfirms the recurring 1000-row-cap pitfall. (b) Removed the redundant standalone `formula` box from the `min-max-of-combined-probabilities` notes concept (its 4 bounds overlap Fréchet-Boole + the union-bounds concept, and the linking identity stays in intuition/definition/a trap — zero teaching lost) so the harvester never re-emits the mislabelled atom; re-harvested (206→205, no other correct/answer changed) + deleted the sourceless atom. Left `selecting-numbers` notes intact (legitimate counting concept; its atom is retired + guarded).

Lets a stale/superseded quiz be cleaned from both apps in one command.

`source_fingerprint`=sha1(source notes) drives staleness; `atom_key`=natural upsert key; `trap_hints[]`), `0031 quizzes` (`id`=pushed UUID=`slugToUuid(slug)`, status draft→pushed→published) + `quiz_atoms_map` (coverage = a JOIN, not a lint), `0032 quiz_atoms.theme` (formula|property|computation|fact|trap, backfilled from source_kind). **Pipeline (`scripts/quiz/` + `src/lib/quiz/`):** `quiz:harvest` (ConceptUnit → atoms: formula/reference → **auto** key+distractors correct by construction; practiceSet/selfCheck → **needs_review** key-correct + rough candidates; trap → "spot the mistake" seed; trap_hints carried on every atom for the verify pass) → `quiz:sync` (JSON→DB, staleness-preserving: skips verified-unchanged, re-writes changed) → `quiz:verify` (promote needs_review→verified; **Claude hand-authors the 3 distractors per chapter** into `scripts/quiz/verify/<name>.ts` — user declined both a UI form and a bulk pass, cadence is chapter-by-chapter on request) → `quiz:assemble` (ready atoms → quiz; **theme-filterable**, variety-interleaved when mixed, coverage-dedup vs `quiz_atoms_map`, records `quizzes`+map, pushes draft) → push. **Idempotency:** deterministic slug→UUIDv5, so re-push UPDATEs not duplicates. **Themed quizzes (user's call):** a daily recall drill wants ONE objective/day (Formulas day, Traps day…) — mixed-like-the-exam is the *mock test's* job; rotate themes across the week. **UI:** `/dashboard/quizzes` (admin) — pool StatCards + an Assemble control (chapter + theme dropdowns → server action `assembleQuizAction`, service-role, env-gated push) + a **filterable** assembled-quiz list (`QuizBrowser`, client; exam/subject/chapter/theme/status; **theme derived from the quiz's actual atom content** — single distinct theme → that, else "mixed" — same rule the assembler uses, so the title/pushed-theme/dashboard all agree). nda-tracker got the mirror filter bar on its Daily Quiz page (commit `e142ca0`). **Live state:** Quiz Factory in prod, 1018 atoms across 5 chapters, ~11 quizzes built (mostly pushed); full loop (assemble in browser → push → publish → student takes → results) validated. **Deferred:** approve more chapters (refills ready pool), QuizEditor classification fields in nda-tracker (so hand-made quizzes are filterable), student-portal filters. - **2026-06-07 — Word-export fix: math accents (\bar, \hat, \vec, \dot) + \overline now render properly.** User screenshot: the mean bar in an exported `.docx` showed as a tiny detached mark floating above-right of `x`, not a bar. Root cause (verified by dumping the OMML): `mml2omml` maps temml's single-base accents (`\bar`/`\hat`/`\vec`/`\dot`/`\tilde`, all `<mover>` in MathML) to an over-LIMIT **`<m:limUpp>`** — Word draws a limit at reduced size, detached above the base. And `\overline` maps to a top-only **`<m:borderBox>`** which renders invisibly under our injected math defaults (the same failure as the documented `\underline` borderBox). Both are now repaired by a new post-process **`wrapAccents`** in [ommlBuilder.ts](src/lib/export/ommlBuilder.ts), chained after `wrapMatrixDelimiters` (same render-only post-process pattern as the matrix-delimiter + underline fixes — **no DB/bank writes**; existing papers regenerate correctly on next download): a `<m:limUpp>` whose `<m:lim>` is exactly one recognised accent char → `<m:acc>` with the matching COMBINING char (overline U+0305, circumflex U+0302, arrow U+20D7, dot U+0307, tilde U+0303); a top-only `<m:borderBox>` (i.e. `\overline`) → `<m:bar pos=top>`. (A bottom-only borderBox — `\underline` in math — is deliberately LEFT as-is: the `\underline` text bypass + the preserved borderBox fallback are a separate intentional design — see `tests/underline-roundtrip.test.ts`.) A `<m:limUpp>` with any other lim content (real `\lim`/`\overset`/`\overbrace`) and `\overrightarrow` (already a correct stretchy `<m:groupChr>`) are left untouched. Scope was broad — PUBLIC field-occurrences: `\bar` 127, `\hat` 485, `\vec` 625, `\overline` 46, `\dot` 4 (`\overrightarrow` 125 already fine). +8 TDD cases in `tests/omml-builder.test.ts` (38 total in that file). Browser/KaTeX rendering was never affected — export-only.

The unfiltered /browse default (newest-first) is untouched (a global subtopic-order sort would meaninglessly interleave unrelated chapters). DB-integration assert in `tests/query-order.test.ts` (order_index `[1,2,null]`, proving NULLs-last).
  - **PostgREST gotcha (cost ~30 min, worth banking):** ordering the PARENT result by an embedded to-one column does NOT work via supabase-js's `.order(col, { referencedTable })` — that orders the embedded child *collection*, a no-op for a to-one embed (probe returned unsorted). The working form is to pass the **embed-alias column string** `.order("subtopic(order_index)", { ascending, nullsFirst:false })` with NO `referencedTable` — supabase-js forwards it as PostgREST's top-level `order=subtopic(order_index)` spec (uses the SELECT *alias* `subtopic`, not the table name `subtopics`). Verified live: `1×33 2×22 3×59 4×20 5×28 6×8` = exact Matrices teaching order. See [[postgrest-order-by-embedded-column]].

- **2026-06-03 — Word-export fix: matrices/determinants now render with stretchy brackets (`<m:d>` delimiters).** Bug: delimited matrix environments (`pmatrix` `(`, `bmatrix` `[`, **`vmatrix` `|` determinants**, `Bmatrix` `{`, `Vmatrix` `‖`) rendered in the `.docx` with **tiny, detached, single-line-height brackets beside the grid** instead of enclosing it. Root cause (verified by dumping `document.xml` from a real export): `mml2omml` converts the matrix grid to a proper OMML `<m:m>` but emits the surrounding stretchy fence operators as plain `<m:r><m:t>(</m:t></m:r>` text runs flanking it — never an OMML delimiter object, so Word has nothing to stretch. Fix: one pure helper `wrapMatrixDelimiters(omml)` in [ommlBuilder.ts](src/lib/export/ommlBuilder.ts), called from `latexToOmml` after `sanitizeOmmlForXml`, that rewrites the `fence-run + <m:m> + fence-run` shape into `<m:d><m:dPr><m:begChr/><m:endChr/><m:ctrlPr/></m:dPr><m:e><m:m>…</m:m></m:e></m:d>` with `begChr`/`endChr` taken from the captured fence chars (so `vmatrix` → real determinant bars). Only a fence run **immediately adjacent** to `<m:m>` is consumed → ordinary `f(x)` math and fence-less `\begin{matrix}` are untouched (negative tests lock this). **Render-only — no DB writes, no bank edits**; existing papers/keys render correctly on the next download (export regenerates from live data). +7 TDD cases in [omml-builder.test.ts](tests/omml-builder.test.ts) (995 → 1002 tests). Mirrors the existing "mml2omml limitation → post-process the OMML string" pattern already used for underline-bypass + XML-escape.

The real state was a 3-way mix: 49 unicode-subscript + 17 ASCII `->` arrows + 13 bare-digit (`FeCl2`) + a few already-LaTeX. User chose **full-LaTeX canonicalization**: every formula → `\(\text{El}_n\)` with `\to` arrows, `\cdot` for hydrates, `\rightleftharpoons` for equilibria, charges as `^{n+}`. Converted across stems + options + solutions; **23 rows had text/option changes (hash-refreshed, all 23 verified), 46 were solution-only** (no hash impact). **No key flips** — mechanical formatting only (no `is_correct` touched). All Phase-5 probes (standard unicode/balance + chem arrow/subscript/bare-digit) return **0**. **Canonical chem form going forward = LaTeX `\(\text{}_n\)` + `\to`** — unicode `→` can't be the target (it trips the latex-cleanup probe), and this unifies the previously-mixed conventions. DB edits already live; this logs them.
