- **2026-06-02 — In-app /notes concept reporting + admin triage (mirrors question-reports).** Logged-in users report a concept from its card (incorrect-content / confusing-explanation / typo / broken-visualization / wrong-example / other); admins triage at /dashboard/notes-reports with an open-count badge. Built TDD-first; migration 0028 + lib/notes-reports + 2 API routes + ReportConceptDialog + triage page; +19 tests (980 total); gate + advisors green.
  - **The load-bearing decision — org resolution for org-less content.** The user chose "org-scoped like questions" over a global model, but the schema then forced the interesting part: the ENTIRE taxonomy (exams/subjects/chapters/subtopics) has **no `org_id`** — only questions do — and a concept is TS editorial with no DB row at all. So a concept genuinely has no owning org. Resolved by routing the report to **the org that owns the bank questions the concept teaches**: `createConceptReport` resolves the subtopic via `resolveTaxonomy`, takes the `org_id` of a PUBLIC question in it, and denormalizes it. Reliable because every notes subtopic has bank questions by construction (works for tag-less foundation concepts too), unambiguous today (one org owns all PUBLIC questions), and a clean parallel to the question-report model. A DB test asserts the report lands on the content org, NOT the reporter's throwaway org.
  - **ISR preserved by client-side auth.** `/notes` pages are ISR-cached (cookie-free anon client). The browse `ReportQuestionDialog` gets `isLoggedIn` from the server — doing that on notes would force dynamic rendering and kill the cache on every page. Instead `ReportConceptDialog` resolves login **client-side** (browser supabase `getUser` on mount); the build confirms free notes pages stayed SSG-prerendered (●) even though the server-component `ConceptUnitCard` now renders the client dialog. Anon → sign-in prompt + concept-prefilled mailto.
  - **Identity + reuse.** Concept identity is the globally-unique `(subtopic_slug, concept_slug)` pair (same key as `question_concept_tags`); `getConceptIdentity` validates it against `NOTES_CHAPTERS` so a tampered POST for a non-existent concept is rejected (404). The `report_status` enum + status validators are REUSED from 0024 (lifecycle is identical) — only the category enum is new.
  - Also fixed a pre-existing dead mailto: the question-report fallback pointed at `report@questionbank.lwspune.org` (doesn't exist) → `connect.lwspune@gmail.com` (matches the Footer). Both report dialogs now consistent.

- **2026-06-02 — Bank-wide /notes worked-example de-duplication + a lint guard to keep it that way.** A concept-content alignment pass across the other 6 shipped chapters uncovered that the duplication caught on Matrices was **systemic**: the worked examples had been seeded from their featured PYQ's exact numbers in the *majority* of bank-anchored concepts. Caught only by DB-diffing each `pyqExampleId`'s live text against its `authoredExample`.
  - **Scale.** ~80 worked examples / self-checks re-authored (hand-verified) across Sound, Probability, Statistics, 3D Geometry, Vectors, Indefinite Integration — plus the backlog the new lint then surfaced (Matrices & Determinants 14, 3D Geometry 7 the LLM audit had missed). Two finding classes: **(A) wrong/misleading** examples — fixed always (3D `plane-through-three-points` taught intercept-form not the cross-product method; `dcs-from-a-line` orphaned `l⁴+m⁴+n⁴`; `sphere-and-axes` garbled `r/√2`) — vs **(B) redundant-but-correct** (right concept + method, same numbers as the PYQ below it).
  - **Structural fixes.** Indefinite Integration: **subtopic-order swap** (Rational/Partial-Fractions before Trig II) so the Weierstrass / divide-by-cos² examples meet the arctan-quadratic machinery before they need it — clean reorder, no concept moves, no DB-tag cost. Vectors `scalar-projection` forward-method (uses the component dot product a subtopic early): fixed with an **inline dot-product gloss, NOT a concept move** — relocating it broke notes-lint because projection questions live in the Magnitude/Projection *taxonomy* subtopic and a featured PYQ must sit in the same one ([[notes-concept-content-alignment]]).
  - **PYQ retags (2).** Statistics `arithmetic-mean-raw`'s featured discard-problem → `mean-replacement-correction`; Vectors `triple-product-cyclic`'s unit-vector-sinθ PYQ → `cross-product-magnitude`.
  - **The durable guard — notes-lint check #5.** Fetches each PYQ's text and WARNs when a worked example re-uses its distinctive numbers (subscripts stripped — they're indices, not magnitudes; superscript powers kept). Non-blocking. Reversed the "deliberately not lintable" stance for the *number-heavy* slice; concept-illustration / forward-method / arithmetic-correctness remain the manual read-through (no gate checks math — a wrong fresh example is worse than a correct duplicate). It immediately found ~21 dups the manual+agent audit missed. CLAUDE.md "Notes editorial workflow" Step 1 + 4 updated (author the worked example FIRST then attach a *different* PYQ; prefer a second real PYQ over an invented one). See [[notes-concept-content-alignment]] + [[audit-scope-separation]].

- **2026-06-02 — NDA Maths Matrices & Determinants /notes chapter (7th) + concept-content alignment rule + CI/pre-push gap closed.** Built pedagogy-first; 170 q · 35 concepts · 100% tag coverage.
  - **The chapter.** 6 subtopics (matrix-operations · special-matrices · determinants-evaluation-properties · special-determinants · cofactors-adjoint-inverse · linear-systems), 34 formula + 1 reference concept. Largest+hardest notes chapter (31% HARD). **Pedagogy-first manifested as a decision NOT to reshape** — the bank's 6 subtopics already tracked the teaching spine, so reordered via `subtopicOrder` with no Phase-D (contrast 3D Geometry, which needed a split). **Diagram-light** (3 static schematics) — the diagram decision rule predicting the right outcome for an algebraic chapter. 2 cross-subtopic passage sets co-located (S11→cofactors, S14→special-matrices).
  - **Concept-content alignment rule (the user caught it on a rendered page).** The "scalar multiplication" concept's worked example was actually matrix *multiplication* (taught later, didn't illustrate the concept); a sweep found the "evaluating-determinants" example row-reduced (taught 2 concepts later) AND duplicated its own featured PYQ. Both fixed. Codified the rule in the Notes editorial workflow (Step 1 + Step 4 manual read-through) + [[notes-concept-content-alignment]]: worked examples must teach THEIR concept using only techniques taught by then (forward-POINTERS in prose are fine; forward-METHOD is not); worked example must differ from the featured PYQ; retag PYQs whose dominant skill is a later concept (`66be5b2d` moved equality→multiplication). Semantic — deliberately not a notes-lint rule.
  - **CI ≠ pre-push.** CI red-failed on the Matrices push: `notes-index-helper.test.ts` used "Matrices & Determinants" as a *no-notes* example, which shipping the chapter flipped to true. **Pre-push runs only typecheck+lint+build; CI adds `npm test` + notes:lint + notes:latex** — so the test break passed pre-push and only CI caught it. Fixed the test (synthetic negative cases now) + added "run full `npm test` before ship" to workflow Step 4. See [[prepush-excludes-npm-test]].

- **2026-06-02 — NDA Maths 3D Geometry /notes chapter (6th chapter) + diagram decision-rule codified.** Shipped pedagogy-first in 2 commits; gates green (notes:lint, notes:latex, prepush, guide-nda-maths-taxonomy).
  - **The chapter.** 5 subtopics · 29 concepts (27 formula + 2 reference) on the teaching arc coordinates → direction cosines → line → plane → sphere, authored against the 89-q bank. **Phase-D split:** the bank lumped lines + planes into one 25-q subtopic; pedagogically distinct, so "Lines and Planes in 3D" was re-carved into "The Straight Line in 3D" (11 q) + "The Plane" (14 q) (NDA Maths 109 → 110 sub), and the nda-maths guide principle drill + CHAPTER_TABLE focus prose synced in the same change (the [[shipped-chapter-rename-downstream-sync]] discipline). 89 `question_concept_tags` inserted (100% coverage, all 12 passage sets co-located).
  - **Diagrams — first chapter to start static, then upgraded.** Initial ship leaned static-2D on a chapter that's the most spatial in the bank; a follow-up commit converted octants / line-plane / plane-normal to **drag-to-rotate** (the Vectors `makeProject(az, el)` turntable) and added 2 new rotatable figures (angle-between-lines, sphere centre/radius), keeping sphere↔plane tangency a static cross-section (clearer in 2-D). 6 new SVGs total → 51 bank-wide.

Codified the 4-step rule in the Notes editorial workflow (Step 1) + [[notes-diagram-decision-rule]]: spatial? → 3-D? rotate : 2-D static; cap to load-bearing concepts. The miss this session (static-first on a 3-D chapter) is exactly what the rule now prevents.

- **2026-06-01 — Premium paywall shipped end-to-end (4 phases): self-serve signup → entitlements → comp-access UI → notes preview-gate → Razorpay checkout.** Built test-first across the session; 2 migrations (0026, 0027), +42 tests (910 total), zero new npm deps. Driver: the user wants signups so a few *future* notes chapters can be paywalled, plus the ability to comp their own students.
  - **The load-bearing axis decision — entitlement is per-USER, independent of orgs.** The whole RLS model is org-based, but a paying/comped student has NO org. So `public.entitlements` (migration 0026) keys on `auth.users(id)`, not org. A row grants a `scope` ('all' = full premium; or a future content key), with `source` ∈ `razorpay | comp | manual` and optional `expires_at`. The gate asks only "is there an active entitlement?" — **source-agnostic**, so comp grants and paid grants write the SAME table. RLS: users SELECT own; **no write policy → service-role-only writes** (webhook + comp UI). Pure `isEntitlementActive`/`hasActiveScope` ([src/lib/entitlements/access.ts](src/lib/entitlements/access.ts)) + `userHasAccess` (RLS-scoped, fail-closed). Verified via JWT simulation (owner sees own row, others see 0).
  - **Phase 0 — self-serve students** ([src/app/signup/](src/app/signup/)): Google OAuth (primary) + email/password. **Confirm-email OFF** — payment is the real gate, and Google sidesteps Supabase's built-in email throttle (~2/hr, dev-only; custom SMTP needed for prod password-resets later). `AppHeader`/`UserMenu` now render the account menu for org-less users (role `null` → "Student"); `/dashboard` redirects org-less visitors to `/browse` (dropped the stale "ask your administrator" card). Client-safe validators extracted to [src/lib/auth/credentials.ts](src/lib/auth/credentials.ts) (out of the service-role members module). New `GoogleSignInButton`.
  - **Phase 2 — comp access** ([/dashboard/entitlements](src/app/dashboard/entitlements/)): admins grant/revoke free premium by email (`source:'comp'`), **require-signup-first** (no user auto-create → no password handling). Mirrors the members admin pattern (service-role helpers + action-discriminator route).
  - **Phase 3 — notes preview-gate**: `NOTES_CHAPTERS` gains `tier?: "free" | "paid"` + `paidScope` + `previewConceptCount`. On a paid chapter the landing + first N concepts (default 2) per subtopic stay public + **indexable** (the concept TOC lists ALL names), the rest gate behind `NotesPaywall`. **All 5 current chapters are FREE — machinery is dormant.** CONTRACT: a paid chapter's `[subtopicSlug]/page.tsx` MUST `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` + drop `revalidate`/`generateStaticParams` — the gate reads session cookies, so a statically-cached anon prerender would leak the preview. **notes-lint enforces this** (static guard, no DB). Verified live by temporarily flagging Sound paid: anon got 2 preview cards + wall with the locked card absent from HTML but its TOC name kept; free chapters unchanged.
  - **Phase 4 — Razorpay** (migration 0027): **₹999 / 365-day one-time pass** (NOT recurring — avoids RBI e-mandate complexity + the +0.99% subscription fee; renew = buy again). No SDK: Orders API via `fetch` + Basic auth, signatures via `node:crypto` HMAC, hosted `checkout.js` on the client. **Dual idempotent grant** — `/api/billing/verify` (client success → instant access) + `/api/billing/webhook` (`order.paid`, raw-body HMAC, authoritative). Idempotency enforced by a unique index on `(provider_ref) WHERE source='razorpay'` (0027) — verified a duplicate insert → 23505. `/pricing` + `/account` pages; "Account & access" in the user menu.
  - **OPEN (only thing left to transact):** Razorpay account not yet created. Checkout returns 503 until 4 env vars are set in Vercel + `.env.local`: `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID`, `RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` (= key id), `RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; plus an `order.paid` webhook → `/api/billing/webhook`. Test mode needs no KYC; KYC gates only LIVE keys. (As of 2026-06-01 the user's existing Razorpay login appeared to be a partner-linked/Route account — "Registered By: CREATOR ECONOMY TECH", limited nav — which may not expose standalone API keys; a fresh direct razorpay.com account may be needed.) Full state in [[project-paywall-build]].

- **2026-05-30 (later) — /notes template extension: `ConceptUnit` discriminated union + reference variant; NDA Physics Sound chapter ships (1st reference-variant, 1st non-Maths /notes subject).** Reframed the recall-strand authoring problem. The existing template (Statistics/Vectors/Probability) had one ConceptUnit shape — every concept needs a `formula?` + a required `authoredExample`. That works for technique-driven chapters but strains for Recall-strand chapters where the bank tests memorisation of flat tables (frequency bands, SONAR, ear anatomy, sound-speed-in-medium). Forcing reference content into "intuition → definition → formula → worked example" produced padded ConceptUnits ("Q: A bat emits 40 kHz; is this ultrasonic? A: Yes since 40 > 20"). **Template extension** (Phases 1+2 of the ship): `ConceptUnit` became a **discriminated union** `ConceptUnitFormula | ConceptUnitReference` gated by `kind: "formula" | "reference"`. Formula variant carries `formula?` + required `authoredExample` (existing shape). Reference variant carries required `table: ReferenceTable` with 2–5 columns, ≥1 rows (cell-count parity enforced by notes-lint), optional per-row `noteAmber` (amber-tinted callout) + per-row `pyqExampleId` (renders a `[Q]` chip linking to /browse). - **2026-05-26 — Word export underline fix: bypass OMML borderBox for `\underline{\text{...}}` and `\underline{\textit{...}}`.** Teacher reported the underlined keyword in NDA English antonym questions wasn't visible in the exported Word file (e.g. Q5 `01d50cab` "He nodded `absently` throughout the meeting." — rendered with no underline on `absently`). Root cause: the 2026-05-13 convention routed `\(\underline{\text{word}}\)` through `temml → mml2omml`, emitting `<m:borderBox>` with `hideTop/hideLeft/hideRight="on"`. The OMML markup is technically correct (only the bottom border drawn = supposed underline) and `tests/underline-roundtrip.test.ts` confirmed those markers landed in `word/document.xml` — but Word's actual rendering of an inline-math borderBox suppresses the bottom border under the `<m:mathPr defJc="left" wrapIndent="0" lMargin="0" rMargin="0">` defaults we inject for fraction alignment. The convention had been TDD-verified at the XML-markup level but never visually verified in Word. **Fix**: bypass the math pipeline for the documented underline patterns. New `OmmlSegment` variant `{ type: "underlined-text"; content; italic }` in [src/lib/export/ommlBuilder.ts](src/lib/export/ommlBuilder.ts) emitted when the whole inline-math segment matches `UNDERLINE_BYPASS_RE` (`^\s*\\underline\{\s*\\(text|textit)\{([^{}]+)\}\s*\}\s*([.,;:!?]?)\s*$`). `mathRuns` in [docxBuilder.ts](src/lib/export/docxBuilder.ts) renders the new variant as a native Word run — `TextRun({ text, underline: { type: "single" }, italics: italic ? true : undefined })` — producing `<w:r><w:rPr><w:u w:val="single"/></w:rPr><w:t>…</w:t></w:r>` directly, which renders rock-solid in every Word version, Word Online, LibreOffice, Google Docs. Trailing-punctuation capture handles the real-bank pattern where authors put sentence-ending `.,;:!?` INSIDE the math delimiters (`\(\underline{\text{insidious}}.\)`); the punctuation splits into a separate text segment so the rendered sentence keeps its full stop. Italic variant covers the taxonomy-formatting question (`860087ed`) where option D is `\(\underline{\textit{Amoeba}}\)` — without the underline, option D becomes visually identical to option A and the question is unsolvable. **What didn't change**: DB convention (`\(\underline{\text{word}}\)` stays in the bank — no backfill); browser KaTeX preview (KaTeX uses CSS `text-decoration: underline`); the `latexToOmml` borderBox path itself (preserved as fallback for direct callers — `/notes` preview + non-export surfaces — with isolated unit-test coverage so the LaTeX pipeline still has regression protection). **Audit + safety net**: new `scripts/audit-underline-patterns.ts` (`npm run audit:underlines`) scans every PUBLIC question's text/context/solution + every option for `\(\underline{...}\)` segments, classifies each as "covered" (bypassed → native underline) or "fall-through" (still routes through borderBox), prints a ranked list of distinct fall-through patterns. Live-bank run after the fix: **639/639 payloads covered, 0 fall-through**. The first run caught 5 trailing-period cases (`\(\underline{\text{insidious}}.\)`) that drove the regex extension. Fold into the post-upload ritual after each new English / Biology batch to catch silent-fall-through regressions. **Why "extend regex" over "fix the 5 DB rows"**: future uploads will keep producing trailing-punctuation-inside-delimiters patterns (extraction prompt doesn't enforce delimiter placement). Author-defensive in code beats chasing data each batch. Test churn: existing `underline-roundtrip.test.ts` updated — kept the LaTeX-pipeline borderBox assertion, inverted the docx-export assertion from "find `<m:borderBox>`" to "find `<w:u w:val="single"/>` AND don't find `<m:borderBox>` wrapping the same payload"; new fall-through test asserts non-matching shapes (`\(\underline{x}\)`) still route through OMML. New `omml-builder.test.ts` cases (10) cover the bypass + trailing-punctuation + each fall-through shape. Total: 776/776 vitest green, prepush clean. Out of scope (0 occurrences in bank): bold-underline (`\textbf` variant), mixed math+underline payloads, chained `\text{}\text{}`, block-math underline — all fall through to the still-broken OMML path with same behaviour as today (no new regression).
- **2026-05-26 — TEACHER role can edit questions + admin Members management UI (migration 0025, commit 683d9b2).** Reverses the long-standing "TEACHER is read-only" stance set during M2 (migration 0004). Migration `0025_teacher_editor_role.sql` adds `private.current_user_can_edit_questions()` helper (true for `org_members.role IN ('ADMIN','TEACHER')`); rewrites `questions UPDATE` policy → editor; splits the old `admin write options` FOR ALL into `admin insert options` + `editor update options` + `admin delete options`; opens the three `storage.objects` policies on the `question-images` bucket from admin-only → editor (TEACHER + ADMIN can upload/update/delete in own-org folder); adds `last_edited_by uuid references auth.users(id)` + `last_edited_at timestamptz` columns on `questions` + partial index. `src/lib/auth.ts` gains `requireEditor()` (401 if not signed in, 403 if role not in {ADMIN, TEACHER}). `applyEdit` signature gains optional `editorUserId` + `callerRole` params — stamps audit fields when given, AND returns new `kind: "forbidden_field"` result if `callerRole === "TEACHER"` AND `payload.visibility !== existing.visibility` (server-side guard against tampered requests; route maps to HTTP 403). `PUT /api/questions/[id]` + `POST /api/questions/[id]/leave-set` swap from `requireAdmin()` → `requireEditor()`. `/questions/[id]/edit` accepts TEACHER (was admin-only redirect to /dashboard); EditQuestionForm receives `isAdmin` prop and hides Delete button + Visibility section when `false`. `/dashboard` redirects TEACHER → /browse (admin-only territory). New `/dashboard/members` admin UI (page.tsx + MembersClient.tsx) wraps `/api/admin/members` POST endpoint (single action-discriminator route: `list | create | reset | remove | update_role`). Backed by new `src/lib/members/admin.ts` — pure validators + 5 DB helpers using `createSupabaseAdminClient()` (service-role; `auth.admin.*` needs it). Provisioning shape mirrors NDA Tracker's `TeachersTab.jsx` + `/api/teacher-account`: admin types **name + email + password + role** → auth user created with `user_metadata.name` stamped, `org_members` row inserted in one operation. Last-admin protection + self-protection (caller can't remove themselves OR demote themselves) enforced in the helpers. Test coverage: 32 new (8 validators + 5 RLS smoke + 5 audit+visibility-guard + `storage-rls.test.ts` updated for the opened editor write). All 764/764 vitest green; advisor lints unchanged (only the pre-existing `rate_limits no-policy` info + auth leaked-password-protection warning, both intentional). **Why:** user asked to enable teachers to edit questions, taking the NDA Tracker auth-shape as a reference. Borrowed: name + email + password admin form, serverless function with service-role, `user_metadata.role` stamping. Did NOT borrow: NDA Tracker's read-only-by-UI constraint (QB's TEACHER writes; the gating is in RLS + route guard, not just convention). Email serves as username (Supabase auth is email-native); the "non-email username" alternative was offered and the user picked email for simplicity.
- **2026-05-26 — Word export polish: student-first set banner + flush-left layout + lowercase option labels + per-question spacing (commits 92034c4, ac509df, 4d6b851).** Four coordinated render-time fixes to the `.docx` export, all in `src/lib/export/docxBuilder.ts` (+ new pure helper `src/lib/export/stripPassageCount.ts`). **(1) Student-first set banner:** when a user exports a subset of a set's siblings (cart picks just one, filter excludes others, extraction missed some), the verbatim PYQ banner "Set: …for the three (03) items that follow" promised items not on the page. Replaced with `Common context for questions X-Y:` where X-Y is the 1-indexed position of the first + last sibling in the export's question list (computed from a running position counter across the `groupBySet` loop), AND the passage is run through `stripPassageCountPhrase` which regex-strips the count claim (`for (the next |the )?\w+\s*(\(\d+\))?\s*items? that follows?` → `for the items that follow`). Bank text stays verbatim in DB; only render is normalised. Set-of-1 in the export falls through to inline `Context:` (no banner — a one-question "Set:" framing reads worst). **(2) Flush-left numbering:** changed `{left: 360, hanging: 360}` → `{left: 0, hanging: 0}` + `LevelSuffix.SPACE`. Wrap lines come back to column 0 instead of 0.25", aligning with options + Context + Set banner. **(3) Lowercase option labels:** `(A)/(B)/(C)/(D)` → `(a)/(b)/(c)/(d)` in both question paper AND answer key (`opt.label.toLowerCase()` at render; DB still stores uppercase). **(4) Per-question spacing:** one empty paragraph after every question (standalones AND set siblings) in the paper so the student's eye has a visible boundary between Q_n's option D and Q_{n+1}'s stem. The trailing blank after a set group moved to per-sibling instead, no double blank. Answer key: plain mode stays tight (one paragraph per question), solution mode gets the same blank between (answer + solution) blocks. New tests: `tests/docx-set-rendering.test.ts` (3 tests) + `tests/docx-spacing.test.ts` (5 tests) + `tests/strip-passage-count.test.ts` (10 unit tests). Existing `tests/docx-layout.test.ts` + `tests/docx-export.test.ts` updated for new numbering shape + lowercase labels. **Why:** progression across 3 commits — flush-left came from user feedback that wrap lines weren't aligned with the rest of the doc; lowercase was a same-day add; the K-of-N banner replacement was the third iteration after Option A (set-of-1 only) and Approach 2 (K-of-N from DB) — user pushed back that banner overpromise still happened on 2-of-3 cases, and the student-POV reframe ("student doesn't know what 'bank' means") drove Approach 4 which names the actual question numbers. Inter-question spacing was the fourth ask in the same review.

- **2026-05-27 — Solution cleanup: NDA · Mathematics · Differential Equations (chapter closure; follow-on to same-day /latex-cleanup Bucket B).** 2 wrong-key flips resolved autonomously: Q77 2020-Apr HARD `c05e4ee2` D(-4θdφ) → **B(-θdφ)** — differentiate \(e^{\theta\varphi}=c+4\theta\varphi\) using \(d(\theta\varphi)=\varphi d\theta+\theta d\varphi\), factor \((\varphi d\theta+\theta d\varphi)(e^{\theta\varphi}-4)=0\); the e^{θφ}≠4 branch gives \(\varphi d\theta=-\theta d\varphi\), with NO factor of 4 (key D's −4 coefficient was the error). Q99 2018-Sep HARD `7a0c2752` A(coefficient 4) → **C(coefficient 1)** — substitute \(v=x+y\), get \(dv/dy=2v/(v-1)\); separating and integrating gives \((v-\ln|v|)=2y+c\), so \(y-x+\ln(x+y)=c\) with coefficient 1 on the log (key A's "4 ln" was the error). 2 hash refreshes; both Q77 and Q99 self-flagged with REVIEW. **NDA Maths chapter closure: 18 of 31 fully closed** (adds Differential Equations + Quadratic Equations to Definite Integration / Sets & Relations / Complex Numbers / Application of Derivatives / P&C / Limits&Cont / Differentiation / S&S / Functions / Vectors / Lines / M&D / Statistics / Trig Identities / Probability / 3D Geometry).

- **2026-05-27 — Solution cleanup: NDA · Mathematics · Definite Integration (chapter closure; **stealth wrong-key caught by close-reading, not probe**).** 2 Bucket B deferrals resolved autonomously, zero PDFs needed. **2 key flips**: Q93 2026-Apr S18 `6f22751b` A(0) → **C(2)** — classic king's-property `∫_0^a f(x)/(f(x)+f(a-x))dx = a/2` with a=4 gives I=2. **Sibling Q94** `a5cc77c9` at correct key C=2 (its solution literally says "same as Q93") — independent confirmation that Q93 should be C, not A. Sibling unchanged. Q96 2022-Sep `0886bac8` D(0) → **A((e²−1)/e)** — **stealth wrong-key**: bank's solution claimed both terms of \(\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}(e^{\cos x}\sin x+e^{\sin x}\cos x)dx\) are odd, but second term is NOT odd (\(e^{\sin(-x)}\cos(-x)=e^{-\sin x}\cos x \neq -e^{\sin x}\cos x\) since exponentials are positive). Direct substitution \(u=\sin x\) gives \(\int_{-1}^{1}e^u du = e - 1/e = (e^2-1)/e\), matching option A. **Caught by close-reading the solution prose AFTER the unicode probe flagged the question for an unrelated `→` arrow** — neither `matches_option_disagrees_with_key` nor REVIEW-marker probes caught this since both solution and key agreed on the (wrong) value 0. **Probe-coverage gap pattern surfaced**: when bank solution + UPSC key both agree on a wrong answer with internally-consistent (but mathematically wrong) prose, current probes can't detect it; only close-reading of every flagged solution catches it. ### 2026-05 (pre-2026-05-26)

- **2026-05-25 — Click-to-reveal admin bypass removed.** The 2026-05-18 ship (commit 573d04b) added `revealed = isAdmin || picked !== null` on QuestionCard so admins saw answers immediately while non-admins clicked-to-reveal. Reversed today — admins now click-to-reveal like every other viewer. Three small edits in `src/app/browse/QuestionCard.tsx`: drop the `isAdmin ||` short-circuit on `revealed`, collapse the `isAdmin ? <div> : <button>` ternary on options to always render the clickable `<button>`, drop `!isAdmin &&` from the "Tap an option to check your answer" hint conditional. `isAdmin` is still threaded — it's used for the chrome that genuinely needs admin gating (the "Edit question" link in the expanded card footer). **Why:** role parity on /browse outweighs admin scan speed; an admin who wants to verify an answer goes to `/questions/[id]/edit`, which is the right surface for content verification anyway. Supersedes the 2026-05-18 "Admins see answer by default" decision in this file; `[[click-to-reveal-admin-bypass]]` memory updated to capture the reversal + new rule ("don't add isAdmin short-circuits to interactive student-facing affordances; isAdmin is for chrome, not for bypasses").
- **2026-05-23 — Shipped `/latex-cleanup` + `/solution-cleanup` skills at `.claude/commands/`.** Two project-scoped audit skills codify the per-chapter content-quality procedure from ROADMAP. `/latex-cleanup` handles mechanical formatting (unicode wraps, balance fixes, plain-text math); `/solution-cleanup` handles judgment-heavy work (wrong-key detection, hallucinated-solution rewrites, NDA-paper-misprint preservation). Built iteratively in-session: v1 = baseline probes; v2 added `≈ ≅ ≡` to unicode regex + `matches_option_disagrees_with_key` (the wrong-key smoking-gun probe — found 5 untouched candidates in Statistics, 5 in M&D, 6 in Trig Identities that earlier audits missed); v3 added symmetric option-level coverage (`unbalanced_options`, `pipe_cond_in_opts_prose`, `english_math_words_in_opts`) + `broken_matrix_env` extended to scan qtext + solution + options. v3 sanity test across 630 audited questions (4 chapters) confirmed 0 option-level hits — empirical rate ~0% since options come from clean PYQ-paper extraction, but symmetric coverage prevents silent future regressions and makes the audit story defensible. Workflow precedent: run `/latex-cleanup` FIRST on a chapter (mechanical, batchable 5–10 chapters per session), THEN `/solution-cleanup` (judgment-heavy, one chapter per session). The split was the user's call against my initial "one combined skill" proposal — formatting is export-blocker urgency, content correctness is judgment-bottlenecked, mixing them undersells both.

- **2026-05-08 — Tightened RLS writes to ADMIN at M2.** Original `0002_rls.sql` let any authenticated org member insert questions. M2 (`0004_upload_staging.sql`) added `private.current_user_is_admin()` to write policies on questions, options, and upload_jobs. Layered with `requireAdmin()` in route handlers — defence in depth.
- **2026-05-08 — `tsvector` + GIN index at M3 even with 150 rows.** Cheap to add now, expensive to retrofit. Schema designed for 10k+/org.
- **2026-05-08 — Export = current-filter set, no per-question checkboxes.** Avoids managing multi-page selection state in URL. Teachers narrow via filters, then export the lot. Per-question selection is a v2 if asked for.
- **2026-05-08 — Public storage bucket for question images, not private+signed.** Faster (no per-render signing round-trip), simpler client code (plain `<img src>`). URLs are obscure-but-not-secret — relies on UUID filenames for privacy-by-obscurity. Acceptable trade for a coaching-org tool; revisit if real cross-org confidentiality requirements appear.
- **2026-05-08 — PNG and JPEG only, WebP rejected.** The `docx` library's `ImageRun` doesn't accept WebP, and silently dropping WebP images at export time would surprise teachers worse than rejecting at upload time.
- **2026-05-08 — Per-question Edit Images UI rather than Excel-embedded extraction.** Smaller blast radius — Excel pipeline (xlsx parser) untouched. Teachers add images post-upload through the browse page. Excel-embedded extraction (xlsx → exceljs swap) is a separate future milestone.
- **2026-05-08 — `imageUrl.ts` split out from `images.ts`.** `images.ts` imports `node:crypto` for `randomUUID`; importing it from a client component pulls `node:crypto` into the browser bundle and breaks the Webpack build. The pure-function URL builder lives in its own module so client components can use it.
- **2026-05-08 — Edit lives on a dedicated page, not inline.** The M5 inline `EditImagesDialog` was cramped once we expanded scope to text + 4 options + solution + taxonomy. `/questions/[id]/edit` is admin-only and gives a full form. The browse card just links out.
- **2026-05-08 — Eager-upload image flow on edit (MHT_CET_AI pattern).** Image uploads happen on file-pick via the browser session client (storage RLS gates admin + org folder). The Save endpoint is JSON-only and receives storage paths. Server compares old vs new paths and deletes orphans. Keeps the route handler simple and decouples storage failures from DB writes.
- **2026-05-08 — Edit allows taxonomy moves but not auto-create.** The form lets admins reassign subject/chapter/subtopic from existing options. Auto-create from this UI was deliberately not added: a typo here is more visible (admin staring at one row) than during bulk Excel upload, and a typo'd "Phyiscs" subject would corrupt the canonical taxonomy. Auto-create stays in the upload pipeline only.
- **2026-05-08 — `applyEdit` extracted as a discriminated-union returning DB function.** Route handler is a thin auth + http mapping; all the logic (load + verify org + path-prefix check + taxonomy hierarchy + UPDATEs + orphan cleanup) lives in `src/lib/questions/applyEdit.ts` and returns `{ kind: "ok" | "not_found" | "forbidden" | "invalid_image_path" | "invalid_taxonomy" | "duplicate" | "error" }`. Lets us integration-test the logic directly with the service-role client without spinning up the route.
- **2026-05-09 — Login uses email + password (`signInWithPassword`), magic-link removed for now.** Supabase's default-SMTP cap of 2 emails/hour project-wide blocked the magic-link flow during development. Rather than configure custom SMTP just to demo, admin passwords are set directly in `auth.users` via `UPDATE ... SET encrypted_password = crypt('…', gen_salt('bf'))` (pgcrypto, bcrypt). No sign-up flow, no password-reset flow — both deferred until custom SMTP (Resend) is wired. When teachers come online, add a magic-link toggle alongside password sign-in rather than forcing them through admin-set passwords.
- **2026-05-09 — Public-product pivot (Phase A): visibility enum + drop auth wall.** Question Bank repositioned from "private coaching tool" to "public PYQ paper builder, fed by sync from MHT_CET_AI." `0009_visibility.sql` adds a `visibility (PUBLIC | PRIVATE)` enum on `questions` (default PRIVATE; LWS Pune's 150 backfilled to PUBLIC). New permissive RLS policies grant anon + authenticated read access to PUBLIC rows; existing org-scoped policies remain for PRIVATE. `queryQuestions` now accepts `orgId: string | null` — null means "RLS scopes." Browse page + export endpoint are unauthenticated; AppHeader shows "Sign in" for anon; middleware redirects anon /dashboard → /browse instead of /login. Multi-tenancy stays for the future "private branded bank for paying coaching orgs" tier (deferred).
- **2026-05-09 — Sync receiver (Phase B): `POST /api/sync/mock`.** A finalized mock in MHT_CET_AI (or any sibling publisher) POSTs its questions here; we dedup via `content_hash`, auto-create chapters/subtopics, and either INSERT a new question (visibility=PUBLIC) or MERGE attempt_stats into an existing row. Auth via `Authorization: Bearer <SYNC_SHARED_SECRET>`. `0010_sync_metadata.sql` adds five nullable columns on `questions`: `pyq_year`, `marks`, `neg_marks`, `attempt_stats jsonb`, `source_mock_id`, `source_app`. **Trade-offs:** (1) `source_mock_id` is last-write-wins, not a join table — loses cross-mock provenance; if needed later, promote to a `question_sources` table. (2) Subject names must match the canonical taxonomy exactly (e.g. "Maths" not "Mathematics") — easier contract; alias map deferred. (3) Synced rows always land as PUBLIC in the LWS Pune org with the org's first ADMIN as `created_by`; admins can flip to PRIVATE via the edit page if needed. (4) On near-simultaneous duplicate POSTs, the orchestrator catches `23505` unique-violation and re-routes through MERGE — no race window. The MHT_CET_AI publisher button is a separate cross-project change (not in this commit).
- **2026-05-09 — Public-launch polish (Phase E).** Five small things that together turn `/browse` from "looks half-built" into "feels like a real product." (1) **Hero + Footer:** new `Hero` on the browse landing (only when no filters applied) — exam-agnostic copy ("Build a question paper in 60 seconds") with a stat row showing what's available now (MHT-CET) vs coming soon (NDA, IPMAT, CUET, NEET, JEE Main); new `Footer` site-wide with LWS Pune attribution + Report-a-question mailto + GitHub link. (2) **SEO foundation:** full root `Metadata` (title template, description, keywords, OG, Twitter card), per-page metadata for `/browse`, dynamic OG image via `app/opengraph-image.tsx` (edge-runtime ImageResponse), `app/robots.ts` allowing public routes only, `app/sitemap.ts`. (3) **PYQ year filter:** new `pyqYears: number[]` field on `Filters`, parsed/serialized through URL, queried via `.in("pyq_year", ...)`, exposed as a chip toggle in `FilterBar` (only visible when at least one question in the public bank has a non-null `pyq_year`). (4) **Mobile pass:** QuestionCard padding tightens at `< sm`, MobileFilters Sheet now full-width on small viewports, AppHeader org name hidden on `< md` instead of `< sm`. (5) **Perf + analytics:** `0012_public_filter_index.sql` adds a partial index on `(visibility, exam_id, subject_id, created_at desc) WHERE visibility = 'PUBLIC'` for the public hot path; `@vercel/analytics` mounted in root layout. **Trade-offs:** OG image is dynamic ImageResponse not a designed PNG — looks fine but less polished than a real graphic; pyqYears filter UI is hidden when the bank has no PYQ data, which keeps the panel clean but means the feature is silently invisible until data arrives.
- **2026-05-09 — Rate limiting (Phase D): per-IP/per-user cap on `/api/export`.** Public + zero rate limit = scraping. `0011_rate_limits.sql` adds a `rate_limits(bucket, window_start, count)` table + `public.rate_limit_increment(bucket, window_start)` SECURITY DEFINER function (service-role only — `revoke from anon, authenticated` is required because Supabase auto-grants execute on `public.*`). The route handler does `checkAndIncrement` BEFORE payload validation so junk requests still count toward the bucket. Limits: **anon = 20 exports/hour/IP, authed = 200/hour/user** (originally 10/100; doubled 2026-05-13 when ZIP → two-docx made one teacher-export = two requests). Bucket key is `export:anon:<ip>` or `export:user:<user_id>`. Garbage collection happens inline (each call deletes rows older than 2h for the same bucket). 429 response includes `Retry-After` header + JSON body with `retryAfter`/`limit`/`used`. `getSessionMember()` is wrapped in try/catch in the route — outside Next request scope (i.e. in tests calling POST directly) `next/headers` `cookies()` throws; harmless fallback to anon for the rate-limit bucket lets tests work without cookie mocking.
- **2026-05-09 — Production polish (Phase H).** Hygiene pass before walking away from the codebase. (1) `.env.example` updated with `SYNC_SHARED_SECRET` + generation hint. (2) README rewritten as a real dev-onboarding doc (was stuck at the M1/M2 era, still mentioned magic-link). (3) Long-deferred `tsc --noEmit` errors in `docx-export` + `docx-layout` test fixtures fixed (added `imageUrl: null` to QuestionRow + OptionRow). (4) Branded `not-found.tsx` (Compass icon, "Browse questions" CTA) + `error.tsx` (global error boundary, AlertTriangle, "Try again" + reset()). (5) New CLAUDE.md "Operations" section covering monitoring (Vercel + Supabase logs, advisor lints), upgrade-tier triggers, rate-limit visibility SQL, secret rotation, admin password reset, and bulk visibility flip. **Deliberately NOT done:** Sentry (Vercel built-in covers it), health-check endpoint (premature without uptime monitor), About / FAQ pages (content, not infra). Phases C (user accounts), F (Resend SMTP), and G (accounts UI) were marked unnecessary per user — pivot to "complete this project, defer cross-integration."
- **2026-05-10 — Upload-detail page + per-question / whole-upload delete.** The dashboard's "Recent uploads" list became actionable. `0013_question_upload_job.sql` adds `questions.upload_job_id uuid references upload_jobs(id) on delete set null` (+ partial index) so questions can be claimed by their upload row; `commitStaged` stamps it on every insert. `0014_backfill_question_upload_job.sql` claims pre-migration questions by `(org_id, source_file)` *only* where exactly one upload_jobs row has `inserted > 0` for that combination — ambiguous ownership stays NULL. New `/uploads/[id]` page with a per-question Edit/Delete and a whole-upload Delete behind a single confirm dialog showing the question count. New `DELETE /api/questions/[id]` (existing route gained the verb) and `DELETE /api/uploads/[id]`. Both go through `applyEdit`-style discriminated-union helpers (`deleteQuestion`, `deleteUploadJob`) and clean up storage objects via the user JWT (admin storage policies in 0008 cover own-org folder). **Why `ON DELETE SET NULL` rather than CASCADE:** an accidental `delete from upload_jobs` shouldn't blow away questions; explicit whole-upload deletes go through the route handler, which orders the destruction (questions → storage → job row).
- **2026-05-10 — PYQ details: year + month + comment, set per-batch.** `0010` already had `pyq_year int`. `0015_pyq_metadata.sql` adds `pyq_month text` + `pyq_note text` (both nullable). The user wanted three fields, not just year ("Year, Month (Text), and Comment (Shift |) etc."), to capture the shift/slot context that distinguishes one MHT-CET 2025 paper from another. Two surfaces: (A) Phase-A picker on the upload form between Exam and Dropzone — value travels via formData → `upload_jobs.staged_rows.{pyqYear,pyqMonth,pyqNote}` → `commitStaged` and is stamped onto every inserted row; (C) Phase-C bulk-set on `/uploads/[id]` via `PATCH /api/uploads/[id]` and `setUploadPyqMetadata` — partial fields honoured, explicit `null` clears, no-field call is a no-op. `getUploadDetail` aggregates each field across the linked questions as `value | null | "mixed"` so the header can show a single value or a "(mixed)" badge. Bulk-set has a confirm-on-overwrite dialog that fires when the new value would overwrite a non-null non-mixed existing value (per user's choice).
- **2026-05-10 — Capture original Q-number from the Excel "Q" column.** `0016_question_number.sql` adds `questions.question_number text` (nullable). Parser reads the "Q" cell as optional `questionNumber` — numeric Excel cells coerce to string, text values like `1(a)` / `2A` round-trip, missing or empty stays NULL. **Why text, not int:** PYQ papers occasionally have sub-parts (`1(a)`, `2(b)`); int would force a lossy strip. **Why no backfill for the existing 150:** PYQ papers often section-break their numbering (e.g. Q1–Q50 PCM, Q1–Q50 PCB), so `source_row - 1` is not a reliable Q-number — pre-migration questions stay NULL and `/uploads/[id]` falls back to the existing "Row N" label. UI shows a monospace `Q1` chip when the column is set.
- **2026-05-10 — Test taxonomy globalTeardown.** Tests insert run-id-scoped subjects (PYQB_/QD_/UD_/EditTest…) and auto-create non-canonical chapters under canonical subjects via `goodXlsxBuffer` commits. `organizations.delete()` cascades questions/options/upload_jobs but NOT taxonomy — so 33 orphan subjects had piled up in the live `subjects` table and were appearing in `/browse`'s public Subject filter. Per-suite afterAll deletes the run-id-scoped subjects (no race because each file's RUN_ID is unique). The globalSetup-returned teardown in `tests/global-teardown.ts` sweeps any leftovers + the canonical-adjacent auto-creates that can't be cleaned per-suite without racing parallel-running test files. Cross-test fix needed at the same time: `taxonomy.resolveChapter`/`resolveSubtopic` now catch `23505` (unique violation) and re-find the winner's id, so concurrent commits cooperate instead of failing.
- **2026-05-10 — Save returns to previous page on edit.** Save was hard-coded to `router.push("/browse")`, dropping the admin onto `/browse` after editing a question from `/uploads/[id]` and losing their place in the list. Cancel and Delete already used `router.back()`. Save now matches: `router.refresh()` first to invalidate the destination's RSC cache, then `router.back()`.
- **2026-05-10 — Word export preserves natural aspect ratio.** Hardcoded 320×240 / 200×150 was forcing every embedded image into a fixed rectangle, stretching wide circuit diagrams and squashing portrait crops. New `src/lib/export/imageDimensions.ts` reads intrinsic width/height from PNG IHDR (bytes 16–23) and JPEG SOF markers, then `fitWithinBox` scales to the column-width cap while preserving ratio. Question cap 320×360, option cap 200×200. Falls back to the legacy fixed rectangle when a malformed header can't be parsed.
- **2026-05-10 — Inline diagram + clipboard image paste on edit page.** The Question Diagram ImageSlot moved from the right `<aside>` into the Question Section after Context — every other image (Option A/B/C/D) was already inline; the diagram was the lone outlier. Each content textarea (question + option A/B/C/D) now accepts clipboard image paste: `event.clipboardData.items` filtered to `kind === "file" && type.startsWith("image/")` → upload to that slot via the existing `uploadFile` helper. Plain-text Ctrl+V still works (no `preventDefault` when there's no image on the clipboard).
- **2026-05-10 — Parallel taxonomy auto-create (commit perf fix).** A 150-row upload of a brand-new MHT-CET paper was timing out (Vercel "An error occurred" + JSON.parse failure on the client). `commitStaged` was awaiting `taxonomy.resolveChapter` / `resolveSubtopic` per row sequentially — each unique new chapter took 2–3 round-trips, and 100+ sequential round-trips × ~150–300 ms latency exceeded the 60 s function ceiling. Pre-resolve unique `(subjectId, chapterName)` and `(chapterId, subtopicName)` keys via `Promise.all` before the row loop; the row loop becomes all cache hits. Made resolvers race-safe at the same time (catch 23505 + re-find) so the parallel fan-out doesn't introduce its own duplicate-INSERT race when two near-simultaneous user uploads share a new chapter name. 60 s timeout drops to 3–5 s for typical 150-question uploads.
- **2026-05-10 — Paper cart with localStorage + cart-mode export.** First per-question selection feature; revisits the 2026-05-08 "no per-question checkboxes" decision now that the user explicitly asked. **Storage:** localStorage (key `qb:cart:v1`); per-browser, anon-friendly, no server changes. Cap 200 mirrors the export ceiling. **Hydration:** CartProvider mounts empty (SSR can't read localStorage), reads on mount, persists on every change; consumers gate on `hydrated` to avoid the initial-render flash. **Order in printed paper:** cart-insertion default + sort-by-chapter toggle on the cart panel; the chosen order ships as `questionIds[]` to `/api/export` which preserves it through `queryQuestionsByIds`. **Filter-mode kept alongside:** existing "export the whole filter set" still works for one-click exports; `DownloadDialog` shows a mode segmented control only when the cart has items. **Server pieces:** `queryQuestionsByIds` (full row, for export) + `queryQuestionPreviewsByIds` (slim row, for the cart panel) — both drop unresolved ids silently so deleted/made-private questions just disappear instead of breaking the batch. New `POST /api/cart/preview` returns slim items for panel render. **UI pieces:** Add/Added chip on each `QuestionCard`, floating bottom-right `CartPill` (hidden until cart non-empty + after hydration), Sheet panel with sort toggle / per-row remove / Clear / Download.
- **2026-05-12 — UI/UX polish (mobile + a11y + motion, three sub-phases).** Phase 1 fixed mobile + a11y gaps: cart toggle tap target h-7→h-9 min-w-44px, /browse content pb-28 so CartPill never overlays last card or footer, mobile org chip in AppHeader, dark-mode emerald hardcodes replaced (Hero badges, dashboard "added", QuestionCard "Correct"). Phase 2 added the dismissible **active-filter chip rail** under /browse heading (pure helper `buildActiveChips` + 11 TDD tests; cascading rules match FilterBar's update() logic), refactored loading skeletons to mirror real card heights, restyled EmptyState. Phase 3 added CSS-only motion (no Framer Motion) via three keyframes in tailwind config: pill-in, count-pulse (re-keyed on cart count change so it fires on add not remove), fade-in-up; **dashboard StatCard count-up** via `useCountUp` hook + pure `interpolateCount`/`easeOutCubic` (11 TDD tests; honours `prefers-reduced-motion`); **UserMenu refactor to Radix Popover** (already in deps — no new dependency) which gave proper focus return + escape + click-outside for free.
- **2026-05-12 — NDA seeded + auto-detect exam from Excel "Course" column.** Live DB gained NDA exam + 10 subjects (Mathematics, English, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography, History, Polity, Economics, Current Affairs). Subjects unique constraint is `(exam_id, name)` so MHT-CET's "Maths" and NDA's "Mathematics" coexist; the "Physics" name appears under both exams now and any cross-exam lookup must be exam-scoped. Parser reads optional `Course` column; `/api/upload/preview` runs `detectCourse` (`none|uniform|mixed`) → `resolveExam` (matches against live `exams` list, validates against the form's optional examId, rejects mismatch with a clear error). Form's Exam dropdown becomes optional; placeholder reads "Auto-detect from file"; Review card surfaces the resolved exam with a chip ("detected from file" vs "selected"). **Mixed Course values across rows reject the file** (one upload = one exam) — chosen over per-row exam to keep the data model clean and match the existing PYQ year/month/note "one batch, one set of metadata" pattern.
- **2026-05-12 — OMML XML escape fix.** A real NDA Trig 2025 question contained `\(0 < α < 90\)`; mml2omml emitted `<m:t>0<α<90</m:t>` with literal unescaped `<`, which Word's strict XML parser rejected ("Word experienced an error trying to open the file"). New `sanitizeOmmlForXml` runs in `latexToOmml` — a targeted regex pass over `<m:t>…</m:t>` bodies that escapes `&`, `<`, `>` while preserving any pre-existing entities (`&amp;` doesn't double-escape). 5 new TDD tests cover the original failing input, ampersand variant, double-escape avoidance, raw-`<` direct escape, and "leave attributes/URLs in non-text nodes alone." Found via SAX parser run against the actual broken docx — column 30077 pointed at the failing byte exactly.
- **2026-05-12 — Question sets (NDA-style passage groups).** Three-phase ship for the "Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow…" pattern. **Phase 1 (data layer, migration 0017):** `questions.set_id text NULL` + partial index. New optional Excel column `Set` — type the passage once on the first row of the set, blank on subsequent rows; parser+`propagateSetContext` fill the canonical context onto siblings; commit stamps `set_id = "<uploadJobId>:<setLabel>"` (scoped per upload, so reusing "S1" across uploads forms different sets). Drift detection: two rows with different non-blank contexts in the same set → row-level error pointing at the drifting row. 12 TDD tests on the propagation helper. **Phase 2 (export render):** new pure helper `groupBySet` walks questions in input order; consecutive non-null same-`setId` rows collapse into a "set" group, anything else is "single." `buildQuestionPaper` emits one `Set: <passage>` italic+bold paragraph at the top of each unbroken run, member questions skip their per-row `Context:` line; standalone questions unchanged. 9 TDD tests. End-to-end verified against live NDA data: 1 banner replacing 2 duplicate Context lines, SAX errors 0. **Phase 3 (browse + edit UI):** new `QuestionList` groups consecutive set siblings under a passage banner card on /browse; `QuestionCard` takes `hideContext` to suppress its own Context block when it's inside a banner. Edit page surfaces a "Set · N questions" chip + propagation hint above the Context field; `applyEdit` fans out a context change to every sibling (only context, never text/options/taxonomy/images) with 4 integration tests; new endpoint `POST /api/questions/[id]/leave-set` clears `set_id` on this row only. **Why B over C (no `passages` table):** B and C are user-identical UX. C only buys cross-batch passage reuse; user said re-upload was their preferred backfill anyway. Migration B → C is mechanical (extract distinct set_ids into a passages table, swap FK), so B is not a one-way door.
- **2026-05-12 — `queryQuestions` sort gained `source_row` as the primary tiebreaker.** Bulk uploads insert all rows with identical `created_at`; the previous `created_at DESC, id ASC` made within-upload order random (UUID lexical order). Particularly visible on sets — Q34/Q35 could print in either order. New sort: `created_at DESC, source_row ASC, id ASC`. Within an upload, Excel-row order is now preserved end-to-end. 1 TDD test using explicit UUIDs whose lexical order is the *opposite* of source_row, so the failure mode is deterministic.
- **2026-05-11 — Normalize literal `\n` to real newlines at the boundary.** Real NDA Mathematics rows had two-char `\n` sequences (backslash + n) typed by the Excel author instead of Alt+Enter. `KatexRenderer` wraps text in `white-space: pre-wrap` and the docx exporter splits on `\n`, so both renderers were already correct — the data was wrong. Audit: 14 questions affected (text/context/solution); 0 options; 6 `\ne…` collisions inside `\(…\)` math that a naive replace would have corrupted. Fix: new `src/lib/text/normalizeNewlines.ts` masks math zones in delimiter-precedence order (`\[…\]` → `$$…$$` → `\(…\)` → `$…$`), replaces `\n` outside math with real newlines, restores math verbatim. Idempotent. Wired into `src/lib/upload/parser.ts` (every long-form cell) and `src/lib/questions/edit.ts` (zod transforms on text/context/solution/options — so the content_hash reflects the normalized text and save/re-save stays stable). One-shot backfill `scripts/normalize-newlines.ts` swept all 420 questions + 1680 options; 14 rows updated, second run = 0. 15 TDD tests added (13 pure-helper + 1 parser + 1 edit-validator).
- **2026-05-13 — Taxonomy cleanup pass (MHT-CET).** Three coordinated DB-only operations against the live Supabase instance, no migrations. (1) **Integration chapter split** — single `Integration` (order 12, 22 q / 5 PUBLIC) replaced with `Indefinite Integration` (12) + `Definite Integration` (13). Subtopics + questions classified by both name and content; one ambiguous case ("Reduction Formula for ∫tanⁿθ dθ") moved to Definite by inspecting `\int_0^{π/4}` in the question text. (2) **Duplicate-chapter cleanup, all 3 MHT-CET subjects** — 5 strict-duplicate pairs in Maths (Application of Derivatives / Circle / Permutations and Combinations / Determinants and Matrices / Sequences and Series) + 1 in Chemistry (Chemical Thermodynamics(+ and Energetics)); 10 semantic-overlap orphans (Limits & Continuity → Limits, Conics → Conic Sections, Lines → Straight Line, Inverse Trig + Trig Identities + Trig Equations → Trigonometric Functions, Properties of Triangle → Trigonometry - II, Probability → Probability Distribution, Functions → Sets/Relations/Functions, 3D Geometry → Line and Plane); 6 no-canonical-match orphans deleted (Binomial Theorem, Statistics, Height & Distance, Binary Numbers, Linear Inequalities, Quadratic Equations). Maths went 47 → 26 chapters with order_index re-packed to a contiguous 0–25; total questions / PUBLIC counts preserved end-to-end. Subtopic unique constraint `(chapter_id, name)` was checked for collision-free moves before any UPDATE. (3) **Intra-chapter subtopic merges** — 13 dup groups (token-aware normalisation: lowercase + strip punctuation + sort tokens + drop trailing 's'); examples include em-dash vs hyphen variants, word-order swaps (Order ↔ Molecularity), case-only dups (Conditional Probability vs Conditional probability), and phrasing dups (Integration by Partial Fractions vs Integration Using Partial Fractions). Seed `supabase/seed/taxonomy.json` updated for the Integration split + `+1` orderIndex bump on later chapters; chapters at orderIndex ≥ 23 in live DB are post-seed additions and intentionally not in the seed.
- **2026-05-13 — All questions flipped to PUBLIC.** Bulk `UPDATE questions SET visibility = 'PUBLIC' WHERE visibility = 'PRIVATE'` (598 MHT-CET + 120 NDA = 718 rows). The PRIVATE default for new rows remains — admins can flip individual rows back via the edit page. After this point, `/browse` anon view shows every question; the audit RLS still gates PRIVATE rows but no row currently is. **Reversibility note:** the flip is reversible (`UPDATE … SET visibility = 'PRIVATE'`) but any scraping / search-engine indexing in the window is outside our control.
- **2026-05-13 — Word export: ZIP dropped, two separate .docx downloads via `kind` selector.** Mobile-hostile ZIP format killed (Android lacks a built-in extractor; iOS hides it inside Files). Hard cutoff per user — no deprecation window. New shape: `POST /api/export` requires `kind: "paper" | "key"`. One request per file. DownloadDialog footer renders two distinct buttons; each tap is its own download gesture (iOS/Android block multi-download from one user gesture). Filenames are short-prefixed (`QP_…` / `Answers_…`) so mobile share sheets don't truncate the meaningful part. Rate limits doubled (anon 10 → 20, authed 100 → 200) so a teacher's per-hour cap stays neutral now that one export = two requests. JSZip removed from the route handler (still used inside `docxBuilder.ts` for OMML + math-defaults patching). 5 new validation tests cover the `kind` contract; existing rate-limit test bumped to the new caps. **Supersedes** the 2026-05-08 "Word export = ZIP of two files" decision.
- **2026-05-13 — Tailwind popover color mapping fix.** Both `Select` (FilterBar Exam/Subject) and `UserMenu` popover use shadcn convention `bg-popover` + `text-popover-foreground`. `--popover` was defined in `globals.css` but `tailwind.config.ts` had no `popover` entry in `colors`. The utility classes silently no-op'd; Portal'd dropdown panels rendered transparent. One-line fix mirroring `card`'s pattern. Verified the same fix lands UserMenu correctness too.
- **2026-05-13 — Subject-name aliases in upload validation.** Strict exact-match in `taxonomy.findSubject` (the 2026-05-09 "Subject names must match the canonical taxonomy exactly … alias map deferred" decision) was rejecting real Excels that spelled `Mathematics` against an MHT-CET upload (canonical `Maths`) or `Maths` against an NDA upload (canonical `Mathematics`). New `src/lib/upload/subjectAliases.ts` defines four alias families (`maths/mathematics/math`, `physics/phy`, `chemistry/chem`, `biology/bio`) + a `normalizeSubjectName` helper (trim + lowercase + collapse whitespace). `findSubject` now prefetches all subjects for the examId on first call into a normalized-name map, then walks `subjectMatchKeys(input)` canonical-first; the first map hit wins. Unknown subjects still return null + the existing "Subject does not exist for this exam" row-level error fires — typos aren't silently mapped. 13 TDD tests on the pure helper. **Defensive guard:** the prefetch throws if two seeded subjects in the same exam collide on their normalized form (no exam has this today; catches it early if it ever happens). **Supersedes** the "alias map deferred" decision from 2026-05-09.
- **2026-05-13 — Pagination revert: dropped Phase 4 smooth-scroll onClick.** A real prod regression. Phase 4 F25 added `"use client"` + an `onClick` handler to `Pagination` for smooth-scroll-to-top on page change. But `browse/page.tsx` is a Server Component passing `buildHref: (p) => string` as a prop — functions can't cross the server→client boundary. Production SSR threw on every `/browse` request with `"Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components"`. Only repro'd under `next start`, not `next dev`. Fix was a clean revert — Pagination back to Server Component, drop the smooth onClick; Next.js Link's default `scroll: true` still scrolls to top, just instantly. The polish wasn't worth the regression. **Process learning:** `npm run build && npm run start` should be the local gate before pushing client-boundary changes — `next dev` is permissive about server-component prop serialization in a way that masks this class of bug.

- **2026-05-13 — Dashboard stats RPC (migration 0018) — fix silent 1000-row cap.** Dashboard's "At a glance" showed totalQuestions = 1,000 against a live DB of 1,378 (MHT-CET 748 + NDA 630), and byExam slices were drifting + chaptersCovered = 167 vs true 170. Root cause: `getDashboardStats` did `.from("questions").select(...)` then `data.length` on [src/lib/dashboard/stats.ts:78](src/lib/dashboard/stats.ts#L78); PostgREST caps every response at 1,000 rows by default. Fix: new RPC `public.get_dashboard_stats(p_org_id uuid) returns jsonb` (migration 0018), returns `{total_questions, chapters_covered, by_exam}` via real Postgres aggregates. `security invoker` + `set search_path = ''` so RLS still applies and search_path-attack patterns are blocked. TS client now does a single `client.rpc("get_dashboard_stats", { p_org_id: orgId })` parallelised with the existing `upload_jobs` last-row read. **TDD regression test** in `tests/dashboard-stats.test.ts` ("matches SQL ground-truth even when org has >1000 questions") compares stats output against `count: "exact", head: true` HEAD-count queries (which use response headers, not row payloads, so they bypass the cap and provide trustworthy ground truth). Test failed `expected 1000 to be 1378` against the old impl, passes against the new. **Other broken stats fixed by the same change**: byExam now reflects real per-exam totals (was drifting because the truncated 1000-row sample skewed the per-exam tallies); chaptersCovered now uses `count(distinct chapter_id)` in SQL (jumped 167 → 170 — 3 chapters had ALL their questions in the truncated tail). `examsCovered` is now derived as `byExam.length` since the RPC already groups by exam. **Why an RPC and not multiple HEAD counts:** distinct chapter count has no PostgREST equivalent, so an RPC was unavoidable; bundling total + chapters + by_exam into one round-trip is strictly better than three. Pattern matches existing `rate_limit_increment` RPC.

- **2026-05-13 — Underline-in-question convention finalised: `\(\underline{\text{word}}\)`.** Audit of `NDA_GAT_2025_1_QP.docx` found 5 underlined words in Q16–Q20 synonym questions ("proportionate", "disenchantment", "imminent", "indelible", "instantaneous") — and the extraction prompt's `**word**` markdown emphasis was being lost entirely on the Excel→DB→render path. Investigated three options before deciding: (a) full markdown-emphasis layer with new segmenter + new docx-run path + tests — heavy; (b) HTML `<u>`/`<b>`/`<i>` with HTML-aware parsing — also heavy; (c) **reuse the existing LaTeX pipeline** by wrapping underlined words in `\(\underline{\text{word}}\)`. Picked (c). End-to-end TDD verification in `tests/underline-roundtrip.test.ts` (2 tests, both green): KaTeX renders it as `<span class="mord underline">` in the browser; temml + mathml2omml emits `<m:borderBox>` with `hideTop`/`hideLeft`/`hideRight` all `"on"` (= a box with only the bottom border drawn, which Word renders as an underlined run) with `<m:nor/>` on the inner `<m:r>` to force upright Latin rendering. Zero code changes to the existing pipeline — the test locks the OMML shape so a future temml/mathml2omml upgrade can't silently break it. `\text{…}` inside `\underline{…}` is required: without it, KaTeX would render the word in math-italic and the visual would diverge between browser and docx. Same trick available for `\textbf` and `\textit` if we ever need them, but the extraction prompt only requires `\underline` today (passage italics go in `Question Context` as plain text, not per-word emphasis).
- **2026-05-15 — Facet counts in the /browse filter sidebar (migration 0020).** Teachers using the bank to build papers wanted to see at a glance which chapters are worth filtering. Plain "Chapter" / "Subtopic" labels gave no sense of volume — they had to apply the filter, see the count, undo, repeat. Two new RPCs in `0020_filter_facets_fn.sql`: `get_chapter_facets(p_exam_id, p_subject_id, p_difficulties, p_pyq_years, p_q)` and `get_subtopic_facets(p_chapter_ids, ...same)`. Both are `security invoker` so RLS still gates PUBLIC vs PUBLIC+PRIVATE — anon sees the public-bank counts, authed org members see their own org's PRIVATE additionally. Counts are **context-aware**: applying difficulty=HARD recomputes the chapter list with hard-only counts (Statistics drops from 93 to 13, Properties of Triangle jumps from #19 to #4 because 52% of it is hard). Pure helper `mergeAndSortFacets(options, facets)` (9 TDD unit tests in `tests/facets.test.ts`) does the merge + filter + sort: zero-count entries are dropped, results sort by count desc with case-insensitive name tiebreak. `src/app/browse/page.tsx` adds two RPC calls to its Promise.all and pipes the merged options through to FilterBar / MobileFilters / ActiveFilterChips. FilterBar's `CheckboxGroup` renders the count as a right-aligned `(N)` in muted tabular-nums next to the label. ActiveFilterChips uses a `makeLookupWithCount` helper so removable filter chips read "Chapter: Statistics (93) ×". **Why context-aware over total-in-scope counts**: the cost is one extra aggregate per page render, but the strategic-filtering benefit (teacher sees how chapters resize as they narrow) was the whole point of adding counts. **Why hide zero-count rows over greying them out**: cleaner list, no "(0)" clutter; if a chapter has no q under the current filter, it's not actionable. 6 DB integration tests in `tests/filter-facets.test.ts` lock the RPC contract against the live bank (ground-truth match for spot-check chapter/subtopic, narrowing on difficulty + year filters).
- **2026-05-11 — Pin Word math defaults so fraction options align with text.** Real NDA Trig set 2025: option `(A) -3/4` rendered ~1″ to the right of the previous question's option `(A) -1`, even though both paragraphs emit identical `<w:ind w:left="720"/>` and identical `(label)` text + `<m:oMath>` shape. Cause: our `word/settings.xml` had no `<m:mathPr>`, so Word fell back to its built-in defaults (`defJc=centerGroup`, `wrapIndent=1440`, non-zero `lMargin`/`rMargin`), and any paragraph containing a 2-D math element (`<m:f>` fraction, etc.) got pulled right. Fix: `injectOmml` renamed to `patchZip`; same post-process step now also injects `<m:mathPr><m:defJc m:val="left"/><m:wrapIndent m:val="0"/><m:lMargin m:val="0"/><m:rMargin m:val="0"/>...</m:mathPr>` into `word/settings.xml` before `</w:settings>`. Applies to both `buildQuestionPaper` and `buildAnswerKey` (key never has fractions today but solutions can). 2 TDD tests assert the block + key fields exist in settings.xml. Why this approach: `docx` library exposes no API for `<m:mathPr>`, and post-processing the zip is already our established pattern from the OMML-injection work. `defJc=left` makes display math (`\[…\]`) left-align instead of center; we render display math inline anyway (no `<m:oMathPara>`), so the practical effect is "all math left-aligned" which matches teacher expectations inside a 2-column paper.
- **2026-05-14 — Two more PostgREST 1000-row cap regressions (pyq-year filter + upload dedup); fixed at SQL aggregate + DB constraint.** Same root cause as the dashboard-stats RPC (0018). (1) **PYQ-year filter:** the FilterBar's year list pulled raw rows via `.select("pyq_year")`, dedup'd client-side, then sorted DESC. Once year-tagged questions crossed 1000, the *oldest* years (2023, 2022, 2021) fell off the page even though questions for those years were still filterable by direct URL. Fix: migration `0019_pyq_years_fn.sql` adds `public.get_pyq_years()` (security invoker; returns `int[]` DESC of distinct non-null years). Browse page does `client.rpc("get_pyq_years")` instead of the raw select. 3 DB integration tests including the >1000-row regression. (2) **Upload dedup:** `commitStaged` used to pre-pull every existing `content_hash` for the org into an in-memory `Set`, then check `existing.has(hash)` per row. The Set silently truncated at 1000, so once an org crossed that size, duplicate rows whose hashes lived past row 1000 slipped the in-memory check, hit the `(org_id, content_hash)` unique index on INSERT, and 23505'd the entire batch. Fix: drop the manual dedup entirely; use `.upsert(rows, { onConflict: "org_id,content_hash", ignoreDuplicates: true })`. Returned rows = inserts, `skipped = staged - inserted`. Same change also fixed a latent options-build bug: within-batch duplicates that now reach `stagedInserts` (previously filtered client-side) no longer emit options twice for the surviving row. **Generalised lesson:** any code that aggregates rows client-side after a Supabase `.select` is suspect once orgs cross 1000 rows. Audit pattern: search for `.select("...")` calls that derive a count, a distinct set, or a sort from the row list rather than from response headers (`count: "exact"`) or a SQL aggregate.

User pushed back on the initial defer with a sharper challenge: "is there a theme of topics on which students can prepare?" — a productive reframe that turned the analysis from "memorise these facts? no" to "are there stable SHAPES? yes". **Half-life evidence** (probed against the live bank): of 67 explicit-year mentions in CA questions, **90% land within 12 months of the paper** (gap = -1: 36% · gap = 0: 54% · gap = -2: 6% · outliers: 4%). Of 13 Military Exercise PYQs across 5 paper-years, **13 different exercises** are named — almost zero recurrence (Garuda and Malabar each appear in exactly one paper). Empirical confirmation: the user was right — the bank's content goes stale. **BUT the user's reframe found the second half of the answer**: while specific facts rotate, **subtopic THEMES are stable** — 8 subtopics appear in 5+ years of papers (Cricket 8 yrs · Governance/UT 7 yrs · Health/Edu schemes 6 yrs · India bilateral 5 yrs · Intl Orgs 6 yrs · Military Exercises 5 yrs · Space Tech 5 yrs · Other Sports 5 yrs), carrying **86 q (48% of bank)**. The PREP HANDLE is THESE RECURRING SHAPES, not the historical facts. **NEW: Template D — Theme-Prep Checklist for short-half-life subjects.** Strand axis is **recurrence strength** (not skill, not strategic priority): Anchor themes (5+ year recurrence · 86 q · ~5 q/paper) → Recurring themes (3–4 year recurrence · 74 q · ~3 q/paper) → Occasional themes (1–2 year recurrence · 20 q · drill if time permits). **Anchor theme cards** carry: (a) question SHAPE — one sentence describing the recurring stem pattern (durable, sourced from real bank stems); (b) prep CHECKLIST — 3–6 fact-CATEGORIES to harvest from this year's news (durable directives, NOT specific facts); (c) optional durable-anchors callout (G7 nations, UN agency HQs, ICC Hall of Fame Indians — the 15–20% structural-fact subset that DOES stay stable); (d) drill BrowseLink for SHAPE practice. **Structure**: ONE page only. No /strategy, no /playbooks, no /trends, no /traps, no /reference-tables, no per-playbook detail pages. Single page contains: hero with 4 stats (180 q · ~10 q/paper · ~40 max marks · 12.2% HARD) + half-life directive callout (load-bearing — "Drill this bank for SHAPE, not for FACTS" with what-bank-gives / what-you-bring two-card layout) + 8-row CHAPTER_TABLE + 8 anchor-theme `<article>` cards + 16-row recurring themes table + 7-entry occasional themes chip grid + test-day plan callout (target 24 of ~40 marks, attempt 7 skip 3, watch the multi-statement trap) + 3 BrowseLink CTAs (all 180 + last 3 years + HARD only) + "why this guide is one page" closing rationale. NO DB tags table (cross-chapter axis impossible — each chapter is a different subject domain: Defence ≠ Sports ≠ Awards). NO new components — anchor theme cards render as inline JSX. **Plumbing**: sitemap +1 entry at priority **0.6** (vs Economics's 0.7 — thinner-flag because the page is shape-calibration not memorise-this); Footer +1 link with Newspaper icon; /browse Hero +1 pill; /guide/nda card grid bumped 9→10 (stays xl:grid-cols-4 for a 4+4+2 layout; copy updated "Nine evidence-led" → "Ten evidence-led"); /nda exam-home GUIDE_PREVIEWS +1 entry (180 q · 10-grid; "All nine" → "All ten"); /guide/nda-maths cross-link banner +1 row (Newspaper); `questionResources.ts` extended — Current Affairs removed from the default-null fallback, all 8 CA chapters now map to `/guide/nda-current-affairs` (single-page pattern, label "NDA Current Affairs strategy"). **TDD-first**: wrote `tests/guide-nda-current-affairs-themes.test.ts` BEFORE the data module — 10 invariants including slug uniqueness across all 3 buckets + qCount sums to 180 + recurrence-window definitions + live taxonomy resolution. tests/question-resources.test.ts updated (CA removed from no-guide list + 8 chapter→landing tests + null-subtopic fallback test added). All **727/727 tests pass; prepush clean (161 static pages)**. **The Template D lesson**: when the empirical evidence undermines a fact-memorise guide proposal, don't reach for "ship a thin landing with structural facts only" (the durability-tier proposal I'd drafted first — also wrong, because military exercises and schemes ARE largely year-specific). Instead, find the second axis (recurring SHAPES) and build the guide around prep DIRECTIVES, not prep FACTS. The bank is reframed as a shape-calibrator with explicit half-life framing in the copy. Earned its place as Template D because no prior template handles short-half-life content; the strand axis is genuinely new (recurrence-strength); and the framing rule "drill for shape, harvest facts externally" is non-transferable to subjects where facts ARE durable (Economics's Five Year Plans, Bio's diseases↔pathogens). User-driven turn from defer → ship via the "is there a theme" reframe is the load-bearing process learning here — captures the value of pushing back on a defer with a precise counter-question rather than a vague "are you sure?".
